proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, runtime security patterns, and privacy guardrails for agentic architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation ([AAIF](../governance/technical-committee.md)) technical workstream dedicated to developing pre-competitive security frameworks, threat models, runtime guardrails, and privacy-preserving execution standards across autonomous agent ecosystems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Operating under the oversight of the Technical Committee and Governing Board, the group functions as an intersecting security layer evaluating identity delegation, attack surface reduction, and sensitive data protection across foundation deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Operational Structure
The working group is open to all foundation membership tiers, with chair and co-chair leadership elected through LFX ranked-choice voting among Gold and Platinum member representatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Following its orientation in February 2026, Alex Frazer was elected working group chair in March 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]. The group operates on a bi-weekly cadence while drafting its formal charter and coordinates with external security initiatives, including the OWASP Agentic workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Workstreams and Scope
The working group's charter drafting process organizes technical activities across key themes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]:

- **Protected Data and Privacy-Preserving Agentic Workflows (Theme D):** Encompasses PII obfuscation, secrets management (focusing broadly on sensitive data and proprietary assets), blast radius measurement for rogue agents, and privacy-preserving execution patterns utilizing Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), zero-knowledge (ZK) verification, and encrypted vector stores [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Commerce and Payment Guardrails (Theme H):** Establishes runtime boundaries and anti-draining controls preventing unauthorized fund movements, account leaks, and excessive execution scope during autonomous financial transactions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Security Taxonomy:** Internal formulation of agentic security and privacy definitions before submitting standardized terms upstream to the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Inter-Group Boundary Alignment:** Questions concerning AI ethics, morality, and responsible AI policy are explicitly deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) working group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]. Non-malicious model hallucinations are aligned with the [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) working group, while non-malicious misbehavior, agent derailment, and deliberate sabotage remain under security evaluation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]. Capability-based auth and agent delegation interface directly with the [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) working group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-17:** Orientation and ideation session facilitated by Linux Foundation leadership; initial identification of threat modeling, runtime sandboxing, checkpointing standards, and privacy requirements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **2026-03-03:** Alex Frazer elected chair; charter scoping refined to integrate privacy-preserving execution (Theme D) and commerce guardrails (Theme H), while formally deferring ethics to governance workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing compliance frameworks, risk assessment protocols, and regulatory alignment for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to bridging global regulatory requirements with technical architectural patterns for autonomous AI agents.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in accordance with the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md), the group maps existing legal and risk frameworks to agentic execution patterns, surfaces domain-specific vulnerabilities, and produces guidance for pre-competitive industry adoption.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its primary work program around a three-step operational roadmap to address emerging agentic governance challenges[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. **Landscape Analysis**: Cataloging external regulatory frameworks, standards, and institutional initiatives—including the EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, GDPR/PII constraints, and Singapore regulatory co-creation models—alongside prior industry risk assessment methodologies.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
2. **Gap Analysis**: Identifying systemic blind spots where established IT and AI compliance models fail to mitigate risks unique to autonomous multi-agent delegation, memory retention, and tool execution.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Developing synthesized principles and implementation guidance for organizations deploying agentic systems into regulated domains.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]

### Operating Procedures and Meeting Governance
The working group convenes on a biweekly cadence, coordinating work through shared working documents as primary collaboration artifacts with Discord serving as a secondary communication channel.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77] Meeting proceedings follow a standardized documentation schema (`TEMPLATE.md` and `AGENTS.md`) requiring recorded action items, decisions, topical summaries, and linked LFX transcript and AI summary assets to ensure transparent archival records.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-19**: Inaugural kickoff meeting covering antitrust guidelines, charter development, chair and co-chair nomination processes, and regulatory focus areas across the EU AI Act and eIDAS 2.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]
- **2026-03-05**: Biweekly session formalizing the three-step deliverable pipeline (landscape analysis, gap analysis, distilled guidance) and organizing task assignments under lead coordinators Ryan and Junjie.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for project intake, working group oversight, and technical direction.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), operating under the authority of the Governing Board (GB) to evaluate project proposals, manage technical project lifecycles, and charter working groups[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Formally adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC charter establishes consensus-driven operations to align technical efforts across foundation initiatives[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification

## Composition and Leadership
- **Membership**: Each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative (TC Representative) to the committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Leadership**: The TC elects a Chairperson annually, and optionally a Co-Chairperson, to preside over meetings and administrative duties[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Core Responsibilities
The TC facilitates collaboration between technical projects and the broader open-source ecosystem by executing key responsibilities[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving AAIF working groups (such as [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md))[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending incoming projects to the Governing Board for acceptance as Technical Projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Applying and maintaining the Project Lifecycle Policy (`../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md`) and deciding stage transitions for projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Coordinating collaboration across technical initiatives and establishing technical priorities and ecosystem roadmaps[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending resource priorities to the Governing Board to support AAIF projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Decision-Making and Voting
The TC operates primarily via consensus but employs clear procedures when formal votes are necessary[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- **Voting Rights**: One vote per voting member[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Quorum**: Requires at least 50% of voting members present to conduct binding votes[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Lazy Consensus**: Approvals may proceed through a 72-hour silence-as-agreement window; any formal objection requires an electronic vote decided by a majority of all TC voting members[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Escalation**: Unresolved votes can be referred by any voting member to the Governing Board for assistance in resolution[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Charter Amendments**: Require approval from two-thirds of the TC and confirmation by the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-03**: TC Charter officially adopted, outlining composition, responsibilities, lazy consensus rules, and working group lifecycle governance[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared threat models, security architecture patterns, and privacy engineering frameworks across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP-WG) advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem, producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. Co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google), the group coordinates technical controls, bounding, logging, and privacy engineering while aligning with external frameworks and sister AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Architecture / Specification

## Mission and Scope
The working group's adopted mission centers on enabling builders to deliver secure, trustworthy agent architectures through shared responsibility between platform providers, consumers, and integrators[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:
- **Threat Modeling and Attack Surface Analysis**: Developing practitioner guidance and attack surface mapping covering prompt injection resilience, social engineering, and dynamic agent runtime vectors[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Security Architecture and Design Patterns**: Standardizing security patterns for runtime execution, guardrails, audit logging, and agent skills (`../taxonomy/skill.md`)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Privacy Engineering**: Focusing on concrete technical controls—such as data minimization, memory isolation, and sensitive data protection—rather than interpreting legal statutory text (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

## Cross-Workgroup Coordination
To prevent fragmented efforts across the AAIF, the SP-WG maintains explicit operational boundaries with other working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:
- **Identity and Authorization**: The SP-WG delegates identity provisioning and authorization mechanisms to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), focusing its own scope on logging, bounding, and auditing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Observability and Telemetry**: The SP-WG collaborates with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on behavioral anomaly detection, telemetry integrity, and runtime incident playbooks (e.g., kill switches)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **Commerce Security**: Coordinates directly with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) on payment execution guardrails and transaction safety[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Regulatory Alignment**: Defers legal interpretations and regulatory mapping to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

## Key Deliverables
The working group is developing five foundational deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]:
1. Living taxonomy of security and privacy terms and definitions.
2. Agentic AI threat model framework.
3. Security and privacy design patterns catalog.
4. Agentic AI security best practices guide.
5. Cross-workgroup security and privacy review checklist.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-17**: Junjie Bu (Google) appointed co-chair alongside Alex Frazer; agreed on cross-WG requirements model to avoid duplicating Identity and Observability WG scopes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **2026-03-31**: Formal adoption of Option G mission statement; expanded Security Architecture scope to explicitly include skills; established privacy engineering focus on technical controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing multi-turn agent telemetry alignment, session-level behavior trace standards, and vendor-neutral observability coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish a shared understanding of agent observability, align disparate initiatives, and produce specifications where gaps persist across the ecosystem[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Led by primary contact and chair Pavan Sudheendra, the group provides visibility into agent operations, multi-turn decision processes, and workflow outcomes to support debugging, evaluation, safety, and operational accountability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Architecture / Specification

## Guiding Principles and Positioning
The OT-WG explicitly positions itself as a coordination forum rather than a competing standards body, striving to resolve ecosystem fragmentation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
- **Coordinate First, Specify Only When Necessary**: Default to contributing upstream to existing efforts (e.g., OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context); introduce new specifications only when clear gaps exist[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Interoperability Over Innovation**: Prioritize extending existing instrumentation conventions and schemas rather than inventing duplicative formats[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Observable by Default**: Design agent architectures to provide built-in telemetry at runtime rather than requiring post-hoc instrumentation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Vendor and Framework Neutrality**: Produce schemas and conventions that function agnostically across proprietary platforms and open-source orchestrators[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

## Problem Space and Scope
The group addresses three structural challenges in production agent telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
1. **Ecosystem Fragmentation**: Mitigating proprietary siloed trace formats by defining interoperable interchange mappings.
2. **LLM Tracing vs. Agent Workflow Tracing**: Bridging the gap between isolated single-call LLM spans and multi-turn, multi-tool workflow execution graphs.
3. **Multi-Modal and Multi-Agent Accountability**: Establishing trace lineage, prompt grounding, and cross-agent context propagation standards across complex agent interactions.

## Focus Areas
The working group organizes its technical mandate through targeted focus groups, established around the founding focus area[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: The founding technical deliverable standardizing multi-turn session semantics, execution phase states, tool boundary telemetry, and evaluation checkpoints (`../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-13**: Working group charter drafted under leadership of Pavan Sudheendra, formalizing coordination-first principles, upstream alignment with OpenTelemetry, and founding the Agent Behavior Trace Model focus area[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, operational best practices, and cross-working group security reviews.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical workstream tasked with establishing shared threat models, defensive architecture patterns, practical hardening guides, and security review workflows for autonomous agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Operating under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group provides technical guidance and cross-cutting security evaluation across AAIF specifications, runtime patterns, and reference architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Charter and Scope
The working group's charter and operational scope were formally adopted by unanimous vote in April 2026 prior to presentation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. The group's technical purview covers:
- Threat modeling across internal, external, identity, and shared memory attack surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- Agent control, containment, and post-incident forensic boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- Extensible hook and interception mechanisms, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) interceptors and secure agent interfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- Privacy-preserving runtime architectures and semantic constraint enforcement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Deliverables Portfolio
The working group established five primary deliverables on an initial three-to-six-month roadmap [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:
1. **Taxonomy Contributions**: Living reference terminology feeding into the central [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
2. **[Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)**: Research evaluating industry frameworks (including OWASP and NIST) to develop an agent-native threat model accounting for dynamic context, trust boundaries, and plastic neural weights [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A builder-focused architecture catalog capturing human-in-the-loop gates, execution hooks, semantic guardrails, and privacy-preserving runtimes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
4. **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Educational and operational guidance covering secrets isolation, runtime permissions, and safe tool invocations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
5. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An early-engagement governance rubric based on established IETF-style review workflows to help sibling working groups identify security and privacy ramifications before milestone delivery [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-04-14, the working group unanimously approved its operational charter, scope definition, and five initial roadmap deliverables via formal vote, preparing the charter for formal ratification by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and YAML mapping of open source projects and open standards across the agentic AI landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive visualization and categorized directory of open-source software, community projects, and open standards across the agentic AI domain [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Maintained in alignment with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and hosted at `https://landscape.aaif.io`, the catalog highlights prominent ecosystem components and AAIF member initiatives.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is generated using the open-source `cncf/landscape2` compiler and data pipeline [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Data entries are maintained in alphabetical order within `landscape.yml`, and referenced vector logos are stored in the repository's `hosted_logos` directory. Site builds occur daily, deploying updates within 24 hours after a submission pull request is merged.

## Inclusion Criteria
To preserve ecosystem signal and prioritize open collaboration, projects submitted to the landscape must satisfy clear acceptance rules [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open-source threshold**: Projects must be open source with at least 1,000 GitHub stars and fit cleanly into an established category.
- **Single-category listing**: An organization or company is typically restricted to one listing representing its primary or best-known offering, with narrow exceptions for large multi-product organizations.
- **Exclusion of proprietary offerings**: Closed-source software, proprietary standards, commercial versions of open-source tooling, and closed-source products that merely implement open solutions are not eligible.
- **Legal ownership mapping**: The assigned Crunchbase entity must correspond to the company or organization controlling the software and its trademark.

## Asset and Metadata Standards
- **Vector logos**: Logos must be submitted in SVG format, include the project or organization name in English, use stacked rather than horizontal orientation when variants exist, and feature transparent or white backgrounds without color inversions [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Extra fields**: Project entries can provide supplemental structured metadata using the `extra` configuration section to define capabilities and documentation links.
- **Metadata licensing**: Crunchbase data incorporated into the generated landscape is governed by Crunchbase Data Access Terms for Linux Foundation landscape projects [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# References
- AAIF Landscape Web Portal: https://landscape.aaif.io
- Landscape Generator Engine: https://github.com/cncf/landscape2

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to evaluate agent vulnerability surfaces, design defensive architectural patterns, and define interoperability specifications for privacy-preserving multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Operating under the technical oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces threat catalogs, security guidelines, and protocol evaluations across emerging runtime boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes technical activities into self-organizing async workstreams and scheduled cross-initiative reviews[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]:

- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Anchoring the initial cross-working group taxonomy effort by supplying the baseline vocabulary extracted from security and threat modeling proceedings to coordinate with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Security Tracking**: Evaluating runtime interception, data redaction, and boundary traversal in agent integration specifications, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptor hooks and MCP Apps browser boundary implications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Runtime Sandboxing and Guardrails**: Formulating reference controls for multi-agent trust domains, hardware-bound authorizations, and agentic isolation mechanisms[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
The working group presented its charter to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in late April 2026[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. While procedural quorum was delayed by voting shortfalls and infrastructure outages, the group initiated operational workstreams and cross-WG taxonomy coordination without substantive objection[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary governing technical authority of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for steering the technical vision, evaluating working group charters, managing project lifecycle transitions, and ensuring architectural coherence across all foundation deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. All technical working groups and foundation projects require formal review and approval from the TC before becoming recognized AAIF entities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification
The Technical Committee exercises governance authority across several key operational workflows:

- **Working Group Oversight**: Reviews and approves initial working group charters and periodic renewals according to the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Proposal intakes are accepted through structured issue templates, with formal review cycles scheduled to begin June 1, 2026[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Project Intake and Progression**: Evaluates open-source project proposals according to the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md).
- **Cross-Group Harmonization**: Mediates shared deliverables across technical tracks, including cross-working-group taxonomy alignment between security, identity, and landscape bodies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
Following the departure of initial CTO Matt, Manik was appointed AAIF Chief Technology Officer and leads the technical direction alongside the committee members[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. In April 2026, the TC received working group charters including the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), establishing formal review precedents within the Linux Foundation umbrella[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal intake, documentation requirements, and submission workflow for establishing new technical working groups under the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. Administered through GitHub issue templates within the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository, proposals undergo structured review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under the Foundation's [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Architecture / Specification
Working group proposals must be submitted via the canonical issue template with the following mandated metadata and structures[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]:

- **Submitter Information**: Name, contact email, organization affiliation (requiring affiliation with an AAIF Member Organization), role title, and confirmation of whether the member company is a Platinum or Gold AAIF Member[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Scope and Deliverables**: Clear operational problem statements, technical boundaries, proposed workstreams, and target technical specifications or reference architectures.
- **Resources and Prior Art**: Identification of existing industry work, competing initiatives, and uploaded supporting documentation or attachments[^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].
- **Template Hygiene**: Issue templates enforce single header blocks, explicit triage routing with designated assignees, and unambiguous field labels[^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1][^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].

# Lifecycle History
The Technical Committee opened proposal intake via GitHub issue tracking in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository, establishing June 1, 2026 as the formal start date for initial working group proposal reviews[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

proposed_concept.description: Public repository packaging portable agent skills, recipes, prompt templates, and automated CI test harnesses across GitHub Models and Gemini APIs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Public Agent Skills repository (`aaif/public-agents`) is a public AAIF resource providing reusable agent capabilities, recipes, prompt templates, and automated validation actions for agentic workflows[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]. It acts as a shared catalog enabling developers to consume standardized [agent skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) and portable multi-turn execution runtimes[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

# Architecture / Specification
The repository organizes agent assets into standardized top-level directories and execution pipelines[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]:

- **Directory Layout**:
  - `skills/`: Installable agent skills providing reusable domain knowledge, brand guidance, and tool integration instructions.
  - `recipes/`: Repeatable task workflows and operational agent runbooks.
  - `prompts/`: Reusable prompt templates and evaluation queries.
  - `docs/`: User guides and contribution documentation.
- **Continuous Integration Test Workflows**:
  - `copilot-test-action`: Queries the GitHub Models inference catalog and executes test completions via the organization-scoped endpoint using default `GITHUB_TOKEN` authentication.
  - `gemini-test-action`: Executes direct prompt tests against Google Gemini endpoints (such as `gemini-2.5-flash`), securing credentials via GitHub repository secrets or environment isolation.

# Lifecycle History
Maintained as an open AAIF asset, the repository integrates standardized Agent Skills definitions with live model verification harnesses in GitHub Actions[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, verification test suites, and trust architectures for AI agent identity, authentication, and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical workstream responsible for defining vendor-neutral viewpoints, conventions, and architectural models for agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Led by chair Grant Miller, the group addresses how AI agents prove origin and operational authority, how human delegations are cryptographically and contextually bounded, and how cross-organizational trust is evaluated across disparate runtime environments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's technical scope and focus areas are structured around six core capabilities [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Standardizing how agent instances are identified, authenticated, and associated with their runtime system, operating organization, and base software environment.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Formalizing representation mechanisms for agents acting on behalf of individuals, organizational roles, services, or workflows, establishing explicit boundaries on delegated operational scopes.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Specifying short-lived, fine-grained access constraints and consent representations that integrate runtime governance controls, such as those described in [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Establishing policy mechanisms for evaluating external agents entering internal security boundaries.
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata**: Defining structured metadata schemas enabling agent discovery and operational traceability.
- **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts**: Harmonizing governance and identity patterns across diverse operational settings.

Explicitly out of scope is direct standards development organization (SDO) ratification, general agent runtime execution sandboxing (deferred to the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)), and formal public policy or responsible AI doctrine formulation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing multi-turn telemetry alignment, session-level behavior trace standards, and vendor-neutral agent observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to build a shared understanding and ecosystem alignment for AI agent observability, multi-turn tracing, and operational accountability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra, the group functions as a cross-industry coordination forum to eliminate fragmented trace formats, bridge the gap between low-level model call metrics and high-level agent session trajectories, and interface with external standards initiatives including OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG and OWASP AOS [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates under an explicit "coordinate first, specify only when necessary" principle, prioritizing upstream contributions and cross-vendor interoperability over creating competitive or redundant specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Key focus areas and structural mandates include:
- **Founding Focus Area**: The [agent-behavior-trace-model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), defining semantic trace representations across multi-turn, multi-tool agent execution loops.
- **Bridging the LLM-to-Agent Observability Gap**: Expanding telemetry capture beyond isolated completion metrics into holistic workflow histories, content lineage, and modality transformations.
- **Cross-Boundary Interoperability**: Ensuring compatibility with protocols such as the Model Context Protocol and OpenTelemetry pipelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Coordination Forum**: Maintaining bidirectional collaboration with OpenTelemetry, W3C Trace Context, and related AAIF workstreams such as the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process defines the operating procedures and submission criteria for incoming projects seeking sponsorship and lifecycle hosting under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Managed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the process establishes structured intake templates and validation rules aligned with foundation governance policies [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification
Prospective project submissions are ingested via issue templates in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository. To avoid administrative blockers during initial application, submission requirements strictly mirror the foundational project lifecycle policy [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]:
- **Mandatory Application Metadata**: Core descriptive metadata, license alignment, project charter, technical scope, and maintainer identities.
- **Optional Submission Attributes**: Prospective applicants may optionally provide a published product roadmap and an OpenSSF Best Practices badge; neither is mandatory for initial proposal filing [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

Submissions proceed through Technical Committee review stages, community feedback windows, and formal governing committee approval prior to legal onboarding.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, and containment controls for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (short name SPAA: Security & Privacy for Agentic AI) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Operating under AAIF governance, the working group produces open threat models, domain taxonomies, and architectural design patterns that platform providers, application consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to secure autonomous AI workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

SPAA focuses directly on systemic risks introduced by autonomous agency, including prompt injection, confused deputy scenarios, authorization boundary violations, unsafe tool execution, and poisoned agent memory where autonomous actions expand operational blast radius[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its responsibilities across explicit jurisdictional boundaries, deliverable sequences, and operational collaboration channels[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

## Scope Boundaries
- **In-Scope**: Threat modeling and attack analysis, security architecture and defensive design patterns, agent runtime control and containment boundaries, data protection and privacy preservation, and cross-working group security reviews[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Out-of-Scope**: Ethics, bias, and normative value-judgment frameworks (deferred to `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md`); prescriptive regulatory compliance interpretation; and third-party commercial certification programs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Workstreams and Deliverables
SPAA sequences its technical output across five core tracks coordinated asynchronously through dedicated workstream channels and biweekly all-hands meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]:
1. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: A near-term initiative evaluating existing industry frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO) against unique multi-agent failure modes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab] (see `../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`).
2. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical pattern catalog defining implementation guidance for hooks, checkpoints, and human-in-the-loop controls alongside known anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
3. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: High-level operational guidance establishing advisory practices and implementation guardrails[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab] (aligned with `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`).
4. **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Early-stage governance checklist intended for socialization with other AAIF working group chairs to embed baseline security criteria across all deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
5. **Taxonomy Integration**: Initial taxonomy drafts generated within SPAA were elevated into an AAIF-wide cross-working group initiative under `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`, with SPAA members serving as core contributors[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

## Governance and Operations
SPAA is led by Chair Alex Frazer alongside Co-Chair Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. Leadership operates under 12-month terms capped at two terms, employing consensus decision-making with escalation to the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The working group maintains external outreach to protocol bodies including Model Context Protocol (MCP) working groups regarding authorization hooks and adjacent standards efforts such as AARM[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was initially submitted in PR#1 and formally finalized on 2026-05-13 following community review and transition to Linux Foundation LFX voting infrastructure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and CNCF Landscape 2 visualization mapping agent runtimes, protocols, tiers, and project watchlists across the AAIF community.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive market map and ecosystem catalog modeling open-source runtimes, communication protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, and commerce rails across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Maintained in alignment with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the catalog organizes ecosystem tooling and tracks project adoption and maturity.

# Architecture / Specification

## Visual and Project Hierarchy
The landscape is built on CNCF Landscape 2 configuration specifications and renders via Next.js static exports [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Projects are organized across distinct tier classifications:
- **Graduated**: Flagship, fully matured production projects [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Incubating**: Scaling projects demonstrating multi-organization adoption [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Member**: Projects hosted, governed, or sponsored directly by AAIF members [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **External**: Ecosystem-adjacent protocols, frameworks, and tools [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

Organization members and project repositories are decoupled into distinct groups, introducing a dedicated watchlist for top open-source agentic projects aligned with the [Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard](https://insights.linuxfoundation.org/report/agentic-ai-momentum) on LFX Insights [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

## CI/CD Validation and Previews
Maintenance of landscape entries is governed by automated workflows:
- **Schema Validation**: Pull requests and merge group runs invoke `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` to validate both `landscape.yml` and `settings.yml` against Landscape 2 schemas [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].
- **Pull Request Previews**: When modifications to `landscape.yml`, `settings.yml`, or `hosted_logos/` are submitted, GitHub Actions automatically deploys and posts an interactive preview overlay URL in the PR thread [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group cataloging and harmonizing open specifications, interoperability patterns, and reference architectures for autonomous agent commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group chartered to catalog, align, and harmonize open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows carried out by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. The working group maintains strict protocol neutrality and deliberately avoids authoring competing commerce protocols, functioning instead as a neutral venue to identify common interoperability models and recommend standards paths to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

Formally ratified on May 15, 2026, the working group is chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, operating openly in the aaif/wg-agentic-commerce repository [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope and Technical Domains
The working group focuses on interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns bridging agentic systems with the broader commerce ecosystem, leaving operational implementation to domain providers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Agent-to-merchant interfaces for product offers, pricing terms, fulfillment alternatives, and inventory availability.
- **Cart & Checkout**: Structured payload representations for cart validation, multi-vendor composition, and handoff between agents and checkout endpoints.
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Authority scoping, buyer identity assertions, and verifiable consent conveyance, structured in coordination with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
- **Agentic Payments**: Interfaces connecting agents, wallets, and settlement networks across traditional cards, real-time rails, and decentralized networks, standardizing payment intent and authorization signals without defining internal rail mechanics.
- **Fraud Signaling**: Risk posture and telemetry signal exchange between agents, merchants, and risk analysis platforms.
- **Autonomy Boundaries & Human Oversight**: Integration of escalation gates, human confirmations, and autonomy-level transitions aligned with patterns like the [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Post-Purchase Operations**: Standardized signaling for order tracking, return requests, warranty claims, and dispute or chargeback processing.

## Out of Scope
The working group explicitly excludes operational mechanics of specific payment networks, proprietary fraud mitigation engines, identity provider internal architectures, end-user terminal or point-of-sale hardware design, general societal AI policy, and the development of proprietary commerce protocols [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was ratified and approved on May 15, 2026 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operating guidelines governing proposal requirements, member eligibility, submission structure, and evaluation criteria for new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines define the formal criteria and intake process through which member organizations propose new Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working Groups operate as structured, time-bound bodies of subject matter experts convened to advance research, author specifications, and build practical guidance around core agentic challenges [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

Submission eligibility is strictly restricted to Foundation Member organizations in good standing across all membership tiers; submissions submitted by non-member parties are not reviewed [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification
## Submission Requirements
Working group proposals submitted to the Foundation must provide comprehensive documentation covering eight mandatory areas [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Proposer full name, organizational affiliation, role, contact email, leadership availability, and membership tier.
2. **Working Group Identity**: A clear, concise title and a single-sentence plain-language summary of the proposed group's focus.
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Specification of the agentic AI gap or opportunity addressed, its technical urgency, and alignment with Foundation objectives.
4. **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Boundaries of technical work and tangible targets, such as technical whitepapers, architectural frameworks, reference datasets, benchmarks, or policy guidance.
5. **Timeline & Structure**: Target milestones, meeting frequency, and estimated charter duration (standard charters span 12–24 months).
6. **Membership & Expertise**: Identified skill profiles, prospective participating organizations, and pre-existing commitments.
7. **Impact & Urgency**: Industry significance, ecosystem demand, and adoption trajectory.
8. **Resource Considerations**: Foundation infrastructure, tooling, or hosting support requirements.

All formal submissions are tracked through the Foundation's public intake repository and portal [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a] [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-4].

# Lifecycle History
Guidelines were updated in March 2026 to clarify submission eligibility and correct foundation portal links [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a] [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-4].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining intake requirements, stage progression across Growth, Impact, and Emeritus tiers, and annual reviews for AAIF technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy specifies how open-source technical projects enter the Foundation, progress across maturity tiers, and undergo annual governance reviews [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Overseen by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy governs both existing external projects transitioning into the Foundation and new technical projects initiated under AAIF auspices [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

Effective March 18, 2026, the policy ensures structured mentoring, shared foundational resources, and progressive operational maturity across project lifecycles [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
## Project Intake Requirements
All prospective projects must submit formal proposals via the project proposals repository detailing [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Project identity, functional description, origin story, and historical background.
- Explicit alignment with AAIF objectives and architectural integration with other Foundation projects.
- Documented production use cases and evidence of practical adoption.
- Technical Committee mentor or sponsor commitments.
- Permissive OSI-approved open-source licensing.
- Public repository infrastructure, automated build/test/release pipelines, and transparent contribution processes.
- Transparent leadership structures, documented decision-making processes (e.g., GOVERNANCE.md), and official public communication channels.
- External technical dependencies, third-party software licenses, and Foundation infrastructure requests.

## Project Maturity Stages
Technical projects progress through three structured lifecycle stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
1. **Growth Stage**: Incubation tier designed for developing projects establishing multi-organizational contributor bases, formal governance, and consistent release cycles.
2. **Impact Stage**: Mature tier for widely deployed, production-proven projects demonstrating broad ecosystem reliance, cross-project integrations, and robust self-sustaining governance.
3. **Emeritus Stage**: Retirement tier for superseded or inactive projects that are no longer actively maintained [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Annual Review Process
The Technical Committee conducts annual evaluations of all active projects to assess operational health, monitor dependency security, affirm stage suitability, and approve advancement or transition to Emeritus status [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
The Project Lifecycle Policy became effective on March 18, 2026 [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Textual cleanups for the Emeritus stage specifications were incorporated via PR #30 [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the intake, submission schema, review, voting, legal formation, and onboarding for prospective AAIF foundation-hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Project Proposal Process establishes the operational and governance path for open-source initiatives applying to become foundation-hosted projects under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in coordination with foundation staff, the intake framework governs qualification, stage classification, community review, and formal Governing Board referral [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

Participation is open to all open-source projects meeting technical criteria, without requiring contributing individuals or entities to hold existing AAIF membership [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Application Workflow
Project leads initiate intake via standard issue forms on the foundation proposal repository after verifying baseline criteria in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Submissions proceed through a defined lifecycle tracking pipeline:
1. **Intake Triage**: Application is placed in backlog under the `New` status label.
2. **Review Presentation**: Project authors collaborate with AAIF staff to prepare technical evaluation decks for presentation to the Technical Committee [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
3. **Committee Review**: The submission is scheduled and evaluated at a formal Technical Committee meeting, where technical merit, governance fitness, and target stage (Growth or Impact) are evaluated [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
4. **Voting and Escalation**: The proposal is put to a formal vote [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Voting and Governance Rules
- **Voting Threshold**: Acceptance into the foundation requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) across all voting members of the Technical Committee [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Board Approval**: Projects receiving committee approval are forwarded to the Governing Board for final legal and institutional sign-off [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Reapplication Window**: Submissions receiving a declined vote may submit a revised proposal after demonstrating tangible progress, permitted as early as three months following the initial determination [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Status Label Taxonomy
The proposal board utilizes standardized status indicators during triage and review [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: Submission is registered and awaiting triage in the intake backlog.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers require clarification or supplementary data from project leads.
- `Too Early`: The initiative does not yet demonstrate required maturity; guidance for future submission is provided.
- `Approved`: Application accepted by the Technical Committee and referred for foundation onboarding.
- `Declined`: Application declined with documented rationale recorded in review discussions.

## Foundation Membership Relationship
Hosting status is independent of commercial membership tiers [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- Project maintainers are not required to be AAIF member organizations.
- Project acceptance confers foundation hosting and governance oversight but does not grant corporate membership tiers (such as Silver, Gold, or Platinum) or Governing Board seats to contributing entities [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Lifecycle History
The proposal workflow was updated in PR #35 and PR #36 to reference formal submission guidance documentation and clarify status workflows, voting thresholds, and reapplication terms [^evt-project-proposals-pr-35] [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, and compliance guidance for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a formally chartered technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, and baseline security practices across autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Operating under an approved foundation charter, the group collaborates across AAIF workstreams to address agent runtime vulnerabilities, prompt injection mitigation, privilege boundaries, and data privacy safeguards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

The working group interfaces directly with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to apply defensive analysis to cross-ecosystem tools and multi-agent coordination architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical outputs across dedicated functional workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Structured evaluation mapping industry risk catalogs (including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and CSA MAESTRO) to agentic operational boundaries, tightly coupled with taxonomy and landscape telemetry [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive operational recommendations structuring runtime sandbox boundaries, tool egress filtering, credential management, and input sanitization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Codified architectural patterns detailing verifiable runtime authorization, hardware attestation, and isolation mechanisms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Unified criteria evaluating security and privacy considerations across external AAIF specifications and reference implementations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

## Governance and Operating Cadence
- **Charter Status**: Formally approved by foundation governance in May 2026, transitioning the group from provisional formation to active execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Workstream Leadership Model**: Rather than central appointment, contributors in individual workstreams self-select leads and co-leads responsible for facilitating discussions, managing status reporting, and delegating PR-based authoring tasks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Collaboration Infrastructure**: Bi-weekly synchronous meetings are paired with asynchronous channel coordination; meeting milestones reflect a one-month scheduling extension instituted following formal charter approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History
Following initial organizing sessions, the working group's charter was officially approved on May 26, 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Deliverable schedules were adjusted by one month to accommodate the charter finalization timeline, and workstream leadership was transitioned to contributor self-selection [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified agentic terminology, schema-validated taxonomies, and the open-source ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting technical initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for standardizing industry terminology, defining machine-readable classification schemas, and cataloging open-source agentic frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. The workstream provides conceptual clarity and ontological grounding across all AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstream Organization and Leadership
The workstream is organized into complementary tracks led by appointed chairs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:
- **Taxonomy Workstream**: Co-chaired by Junjie Bu, standardizing terminology, definitions, and SKOS-Lite schemas across agentic capabilities, failure modes, and architectural components [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Landscape Workstream**: Chaired by Junjie Bu, curating and maintaining the interactive agentic software and runtime ecosystem catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

Technical work proceeds primarily through asynchronous pull requests, supported by a weekly 30-minute synchronization call [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

## Working Group Alignment
The workstream categorizes the ecosystem into seven primary landscape domains mapped directly to corresponding AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:
1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Aligned with [Workflows & Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md).
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Aligned with [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md) and Accuracy trust anchors.
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Aligned with [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md).
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Aligned with [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md).
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Aligned with [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md).
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Aligned with [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Aligned with [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md).

# Lifecycle History
In May 2026, Junjie Bu was appointed co-chair of the cross-working group Taxonomy workstream and chair of the Landscape workstream, opening contributor participation via lightweight asynchronous pull request workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and CNCF Landscape 2 visualization mapping agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, and telemetry tooling.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an open, interactive ecosystem catalog mapping technologies, developer frameworks, runtime environments, and governance platforms across the agentic AI domain [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. Modeled on the CNCF Landscape 2 engine and maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the repository provides machine-readable metadata classifying software projects by functionality, governance affiliation, and working group alignment [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification

## Catalog Structure
The landscape is maintained in declarative YAML format (`landscape.yml`) dividing the technological domain into seven primary categories [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:
1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Covers autonomous agent frameworks and cyclical graph orchestration runtimes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Catalogs communication protocols, agent-to-agent interfaces, and discovery services [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Tracks runtime policy enforcement proxies, tool sandboxes, and behavioral guardrails [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Classifies trace recording formats, execution backends, and semantic monitoring tools [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Maps transaction primitives, payment rails, and autonomous settlement layers [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Tracks regulatory alignment platforms, compliance tooling, and assessment frameworks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Catalogs benchmark suites, accuracy scorers, and behavioral test harnesses [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

## Entry Schema and Classification
Items in the catalog are registered with standardized schema attributes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:
- `name`: Formal title of the framework or product.
- `logo`: Vector SVG asset stored in foundation repository assets.
- `homepage_url` and `repo_url`: Authoritative project URLs.
- `description`: Single-paragraph summary of capabilities.
- `project`: Affiliation status classifying entries into member-backed foundation initiatives (`member`) or broader third-party open-source implementations (`external`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Lifecycle History
The landscape structure was formalized into seven foundational categories to mirror the technical working group domains across the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operating guidelines governing proposal intake, issue templates, triage stages, and Technical Committee approval criteria for creating new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal process for proposing and chartering a new working group under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Proposals are initiated through structured issue templates in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository and progress through a tracked review pipeline managed by the Technical Committee.

Charter approval requires affirmative consensus from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) alongside final confirmation by the Governing Board under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Intake and Review Process
Proposals advance through three primary phases:

1. **Application Submission**: Prospective leads open a formal Working Group Proposal Application using the standardized repository issue template, detailing problem statements, proposed scope, initial deliverables, and sponsor interest[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
2. **Triage and Scheduling**: Submitted proposals are logged on the public Working Group Proposals Project Board and placed into a triage backlog before being assigned a slot on an upcoming TC meeting agenda[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
3. **Review and Voting**: The TC reviews the submission during public meetings. Acceptance requires a simple majority vote of all Technical Committee members, followed by formal Governing Board approval[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Status Taxonomy
Proposals are tracked across five lifecycle states[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- `New`: Newly submitted proposal queued in the triage backlog.
- `Approved`: Proposal formally accepted by the TC and ratified by the Governing Board.
- `Declined`: Proposal rejected with documented feedback provided in issue comments.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Evaluation paused pending additional clarification or charter refinement from submitters.
- `Too Early`: The proposal lacks prerequisites or community breadth; reviewers supply guidance for reapplication.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops defensive specifications, threat modeling frameworks, and security verification checklists across agentic execution boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Operating under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group coordinates multi-turn safety boundaries, attestation primitives, and secure tool execution protocols.

The group delegates domain representatives to cross-cutting efforts such as the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and maintains asynchronous monthly reporting to the TC[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Active Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical work across four active project workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:

- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy; provides a baseline compliance rubric for evaluating agent frameworks across other AAIF working groups.
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg; documents deployment patterns, runtime isolation, and operational guardrails associated with the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg; expands on the [Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) evaluating OWASP, ATLAS, and MAESTRO coverage.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora; catalogs concrete architecture patterns mitigating autonomous execution vulnerabilities.

# Cross-Working Group Coordination
To resolve terminology drift and unify classification across foundations, Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the group's appointed delegates to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (also referred to as Governance, Risk, and Regulatory) establishes policy-as-code mappings, auditing frameworks, and risk evaluation standards for autonomous systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. The working group is co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

The group operates under the governance oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in accordance with the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

# Operational Cadence and Reporting
The working group reports its progress to the Technical Committee through a standardized asynchronous pull request process[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]:

- Reports are authored in `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` using the standardized monthly reporting template.
- A monthly PR titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>` is submitted by the last business day of each reporting month.
- The designated Technical Committee GitHub team reviews the report during an asynchronous 7-calendar-day review window prior to merging[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
- Reports catalog monthly progress, blockers, explicit TC decisions required, and upcoming milestones.

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified agentic terminology, schema-validated taxonomies, and multi-working-group landscape classifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative established across the Agentic AI Foundation to unify agentic computing terminology, resolve conflicting definitions, and maintain decoupled, schema-validated ecosystem metadata[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. Rather than operating as an isolated silo, the workstream relies on designated delegates from each AAIF working group to review cross-domain terminology and harmonize definitions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

Work is managed asynchronously via GitHub pull requests and issues under the guidance of Junjie Bu and working group representatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Cross-Working Group Delegate Model
To prevent conflicting vocabularies across domains, every AAIF technical group appoints delegates who participate in consensus resolution and terminology harmonization[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md): Delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Active cross-group participation aligning telemetry semantics and behavioral tracing definitions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Technical Architecture
The workstream structures its deliverables around decoupled data files submitted via git PRs, separating semantic taxonomy terms from runtime implementation engines. Concepts progress through open review to prevent premature consensus on competing industry paradigms[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
