proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill aggregating monthly working group notes, GitHub activity, and decisions into standardized reporting templates for asynchronous Technical Committee review.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Working Group Monthly Report Generator is an operational agent skill designed to compile monthly working group progress, blockers, and milestone metrics into the standardized reporting format required by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. It extracts records from GitHub pull requests, issues, and meeting minutes to produce scannable markdown reports that support asynchronous TC governance without creating administrative bottlenecks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Reporting Specification and Lifecycle
The skill targets the official AAIF working group reporting workflow[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]:

- **Target Location**: Writes output to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md`.
- **PR Title Format**: Formats the pull request title as `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`.
- **Submission Schedule**: Automated runs trigger prior to the last business day of the month.
- **Review Window**: Sets reviewers to the designated TC GitHub team; reports auto-close after a 7-calendar-day asynchronous review window if no blocking objections are registered[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

# Report Schema
The skill populates six mandatory sections per report[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]:
1. `Summary`: 2–3 sentences synthesizing the month at a glance.
2. `Progress Against Objectives`: Concrete deliverables and workstream progress tied back to charter objectives.
3. `Blockers and Risks`: Cross-cutting technical, logistical, or organizational dependencies.
4. `Decisions Needed from the TC`: Actionable governance questions requiring explicit TC decisions.
5. `Next Month's Focus`: Top 2–3 priorities for the upcoming cycle.
6. `Metrics / Links`: Pointers to merged PRs, meeting notes, releases, and project boards.

mutations.rationale: Harmonizes the standardized monthly reporting template, PR workflow, review deadlines, and WG leadership metadata across AAIF working groups reporting to the Technical Committee.

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting template, pull request workflow, review timelines, and required sections for AAIF working groups reporting to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Reporting Template defines the standard cadence, pull request intake workflow, review window, and markdown document schema for monthly progress reports submitted by Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md). Standardized reporting ensures that asynchronous governance reviews remain scannable, blockers receive timely technical committee interventions, and progress tracks directly against defined working group charters under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md).

Reports are tracked within each working group's repository under `reporting/` and can be prepared or synthesized using automation skills such as [AAIF WG Monthly Report](../skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Submission and Review Workflow

Working groups execute the following monthly reporting lifecycle:

1. **File Path**: The reporting template is copied to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (for example, `reporting/2026-06-report.md`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
2. **Pull Request Convention**: The submission PR must be titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
3. **Review Assignment**: The author assigns the Technical Committee or designated TC GitHub team as reviewers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
4. **Deadlines and Windows**: Reports are due by the last business day of the reporting month. The Technical Committee review window closes 7 calendar days later[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
5. **Merge Criteria**: The report PR is merged once the Technical Committee signs off or when the 7-day review window closes, whichever occurs sooner[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

## Report Document Schema

Every monthly report must supply the following frontmatter metadata and structured sections:

- **Header Metadata**:
  - Working Group Name
  - Reporting Period (`<Month YYYY>`)
  - Chair(s)
  - Date Submitted (`<YYYY-MM-DD>`)
- **Summary**: Two to three concise sentences capturing the month at a glance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Bulleted achievements highlighting shipped deliverables and ongoing work tied back to stated roadmap milestones[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- **Blockers and Risks**: Operational or technical obstacles requiring visibility, or explicit note of `None this month`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Specific, actionable requests for Technical Committee resolution, or `None` if no decision is pending[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- **Next Month's Focus**: Top two to three prioritized milestones planned for the subsequent reporting month[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- **Metrics / Links**: Direct links to relevant pull requests, issues, specifications, meeting notes, or project dashboards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

## Working Group Adoptions and Leadership Registry

The reporting template is adopted across active AAIF technical working groups and workstreams:

- [WG Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md): Co-chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].
- [WG Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981].
- [WG Governance, Risk & Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Adopted report template via repository pull request[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-4].
- [WG Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Co-chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].
- [WG Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
- [WS Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md): Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-ddc8f32].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical workstream within the Agentic AI Foundation chartered to develop threat modeling frameworks, defensive architecture patterns, and runtime safety baselines for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]. The group defines standardized operational controls and coordinates cross-domain security analysis across AAIF projects and external security taxonomies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its repository into dedicated operational directories covering charters, published deliverables, and chronological meeting records[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]:

- `charter/`: Contains the working group charter (`DRAFT.md`), which requires recorded meeting consensus before formal adoption[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- `deliverables/`: Houses all published specifications and technical guidance documents under a strict stage lifecycle[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- `meeting-notes/`: Maintains dated session summaries (`YYYY-MM-DD.md`) capturing recordings, topics discussed, formal decisions, and action items in reverse chronological order[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31].

## Deliverable Lifecycle Governance
Deliverables follow an explicit transition model enforced through repository instructions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:

1. **Draft (`DRAFT-*.md`)**: All work-in-progress deliverables originate in draft form with prefixed filenames and tracked modification timestamps[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
2. **Final**: A deliverable cannot transition to Final status without an explicit approval recorded in the Decisions section of a corresponding meeting notes file; finalization strips the `DRAFT-` prefix and logs the approving session[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
3. **Moved**: When a deliverable transitions to a cross-working group effort or an external repository, the original file is preserved as a permanent redirect note to retain link integrity while updating status to Moved in the index[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-06-22, the working group moved its foundational deliverable, the Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions, to the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) hosted at `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` to support foundation-wide maintenance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body focused on defining standardized workflow execution models, state persistence mechanisms, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and orchestration primitives for multi-step agent systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]. The working group is co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group interfaces with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through standardized monthly reporting procedures aligned with the [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].

## Monthly Reporting Lifecycle
Working group operations follow a structured asynchronous reporting cycle[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]:

- **Submission Timeline**: Reports are filed as pull requests against `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` by the last business day of each reporting month[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee conducts an asynchronous review that closes seven calendar days following submission[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].
- **Core Tracking Sections**: Each report captures progress against stated objectives, operational blockers and risks, actionable decisions requested from the Technical Committee, forward-looking monthly priorities, and metric links[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].
- **Merge Criteria**: Reports are merged upon explicit sign-off from the Technical Committee or expiration of the seven-day review window[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing guidance, and cross-working-group review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish threat models, defensive patterns, practical builder guidance, and cross-working-group evaluation criteria for autonomous agent ecosystems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Operating as an intersecting architectural layer across the foundation, the working group audits and informs related technical streams on identity delegation, audit tracing, and payment safety[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives across five dedicated workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

## 1. Threat Modeling
- **Mandate**: Assesses existing industry threat modeling frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threat surfaces, such as multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation vulnerabilities, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply chain integrity (system prompt integrity, model provenance, and tool manifest verification)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Deliverable**: A comparative gap analysis and framework design establishing whether existing models suffice or new agentic frameworks are required, serving as input to design patterns and best practice guides[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. See [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Leads**: Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

## 2. Design Patterns Catalog
- **Mandate**: Curates reusable design patterns documented in a problem / context / solution / trade-offs format, accompanied by anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **Focus Areas**: Hooks and checkpointing, human-in-the-loop gates, privacy-preserving execution (zero-knowledge proofs, trusted execution environments, encrypted vector databases), blast radius containment, secure memory retention and deletion lifecycles, and runtime interventions (kill switches, execution rollbacks, permission downgrades, and off-task detection)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **Leads**: Dan Kommatas (Circle), Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

## 3. Best Practices Guide
- **Mandate**: Provides higher-level practical operational guidance for builders and operators answering implementation choices rather than low-level pattern formulation, alongside external framework references[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. See [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Focus Areas**: Secrets management, secure tool invocation, model guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].
- **Leads**: Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

## 4. Cross-WG Review Checklist
- **Mandate**: Formulates and executes a lightweight review procedure evaluating cross-working-group deliverables through security and privacy criteria[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- **Priority Engagements**:
  - [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Agent identity attribution and delegated authorization scopes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
  - [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging guarantees[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
  - [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): Fund draining protections, credential leakage prevention, and payment agent transaction limits[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].
- **Lead**: Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

## 5. Taxonomy Integration
- **Structure**: Standalone SP WG taxonomy drafting was merged into the centralized [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream chaired by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **Delegates**: Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) represent the SP WG to resolve security-specific terminology questions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Lifecycle History
The working group structured its five workstreams and assigned initial leads and contributor benches via pull request #5[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling evaluation analyzing CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF frameworks against agentic-specific vulnerabilities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a foundational security deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The project evaluates existing artificial intelligence threat model frameworks—including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—to determine whether they adequately capture vulnerabilities unique to autonomous, agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis evaluates frameworks against several agentic attack vectors and operational boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]:
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion**: Vulnerabilities emerging from agent-to-agent negotiation, prompt injection cascading across peers, and deception.
- **Tool Invocation Risks**: Exploits targeting tool parameter parsing, untrusted local execution, and unverified API side effects.
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Privilege escalation across multi-hop subagent delegations and ephemeral authorization tokens.
- **Supply-Chain Integrity**: Verification mechanisms governing system prompt integrity, model provenance, and tool manifest signing.

## Workstream Structure
The deliverable establishes whether existing external standards suffice or if an agentic-specific framework must be formalized by the AAIF[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. Its outputs directly feed requirements into the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and the Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

- **Workstream Leads**: Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
- **Contributors**: Bar Kaduri (Capsule), Brad Tumy (Twilio), Carollan Helinski (Semiotic AI), Erin Farr (IBM), Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), Hsiao-Ying Lin (Huawei), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), Philipp Tiesel (SAP), Saquib Saifee (IBM), and Sohrab Farooq (TELUS)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Lifecycle History
The threat modeling workstream charter and gap analysis mandate were formally published in the Security and Privacy WG repository via pull request #5[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical implementation guidance, operational security controls, and external framework references for builders of agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is an operational reference curated by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. While architectural pattern catalogs specify how to construct particular defensive implementations, this guide delivers higher-level builder guidance answering what controls should be applied when deploying agentic workflows, referencing established external standards rather than re-deriving them[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

# Architecture / Specification
The best practices framework addresses six critical operational domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]:
- **Secrets Management**: Safe provisioning, injection, and isolation of credentials, API keys, and environment tokens away from model contexts and untrusted agent execution planes.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Egress controls, schema validation, input sanitization, and execution sandboxing for external tool calls.
- **Guardrails**: Model-level and harness-level constraints preventing unauthorized tool execution, toxic emissions, or policy breaches (see [Guardrail](../taxonomy/guardrail.md)).
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Standardized benchmarks and adversarial testing pipelines validating runtime safety and robustness prior to release.
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Behavioral logging, execution replay traces, and provenance records required to reconstruct agent failure states and compromised sessions.
- **External References**: Curated pointers to validated industry standards and upstream open-source security tools.

## Workstream Leadership and Contributors
- **Workstream Leads**: Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].
- **Contributors**: Allie Howe (Keycard), Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), Bar Kaduri (Capsule), Brad Tumy (Twilio), Dan Kommatas (Circle), Erin Farr (IBM), Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), Hsiao-Ying Lin (Huawei), Jonas Pfoh (Bluerock), Mitesh Bhawsar (Equinix), Mithil Patel (Equinix), Philipp Tiesel (SAP), Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), Saquib Saifee (IBM), Sohrab Farooq (TELUS), and Tom Sheffler (Lenovo)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

# Lifecycle History
The guide's scope and contributor roster were formalized under the workstreams structure in pull request #5[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation technical body chaired by Junjie Bu, chartered to establish shared terminology, reconcile conflicting definitions, and maintain decoupled machine-readable datasets for the agentic ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. The working group consolidates terminology contributions across all AAIF working groups, resolving domain overlap through pull request reviews and multi-group delegate participation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy effort functions as an overarching harmonization layer rather than an isolated silo:
- **Decoupled Data Architecture**: Definitions and taxonomy terms are maintained as structured, decoupled data updated directly via pull requests, allowing automated validation and continuous evolution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **Cross-WG Representation**: Each AAIF technical working group designates delegates who actively review proposals, provide domain-specific expertise, and assist in resolving contradictory semantics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **Security & Privacy Delegation**: The [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) merged its standalone taxonomy stream into this cross-WG initiative, naming Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) as permanent delegates to steward security terminology[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Lifecycle History
The merger of working group specific vocabulary streams into the cross-WG Taxonomy / Landscape effort chaired by Junjie Bu was finalized during the 2026-06-09 working group cycle[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, schema-validated vocabularies, and an ecosystem landscape across working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative chartered to establish unified agentic AI terminology, reconcile conflicting definitions across working groups, and map the broader agent ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Originally seeded from the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) taxonomy draft, the effort was elevated to an AAIF-wide workstream in May 2026 to ensure cross-discipline harmonization across accuracy, reliability, security, observability, and workflow domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Working Group Integration
The workstream operates in a dedicated repository (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) and meets weekly in a 30-minute sync, conducting most drafting and harmonization asynchronously through pull requests[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Junjie Bu serves as workstream lead, coordinating with designated working group delegates to assemble 10–20 core terms per working group into a single reconciled taxonomy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]:
- **Security and Privacy**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as formal delegates reviewing terminology and resolving definition conflicts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Coordinates through a JSON-first review process across nine domain sections (`s03-boundaries`, `s04-core`, `s05-reliability-dimensions`, `s06-governance`, `s07-grounding`, `s08-failure`, `s09-metrics`, `s10-ecosystem`, `s11-response`)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].
- **Observability and Traceability**: Coordinates plane definitions (orchestration, execution, protocol, reasoning/context) and alignment guardrails with upstream standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

## Scope and Cross-WG Initiatives
Key initiatives within the workstream include:
- **Unified Terminology Reconciliation**: Ingesting and standardizing core domain vocabularies across AAIF working groups while eliminating conceptual duplicates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Agent Archetypes**: Evaluating capability-based categorizations that profile agents by functional attributes such as tool invocation and network access scope[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Cross-WG Review Alignment**: Supporting working group review tracks, including reliability and failure classifications as well as observability plane crosswalks[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-12**: Initial taxonomy draft originated in the Security and Privacy Working Group was elevated to an AAIF-wide initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed lead of the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Initial delegates named from participating working groups, including Jay White and Katherine Druckman representing Security and Privacy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Repository migration formalized with development transitioning to `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-23**: Workstream reported active synthesis of 10–20 key terms per WG and intake of agent archetype modeling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

mutations.rationale: Update deliverables, workstream leads, repository openness, and governance procedures based on June 2026 working group meeting and deliverable handoffs.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing, and vulnerability taxonomies for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining threat modeling methodologies, defensive architectural patterns, operational best practices, and vulnerability classifications across autonomous agent systems. Operating publicly on GitHub, the group collaborates with external standards bodies including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and the IETF to establish robust boundary controls and policy enforcement mechanisms for multi-agent and tool-augmented runtimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Deliverables and Workstream Ownership
The working group organizes its deliverables into dedicated workstreams hosted in repository folders with assigned co-leads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating agent threat models across CSA MAESTRO, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs/ASI, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF, covering memory poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, blast radius containment, delegated authorization, and supply chain integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing implementation guidelines for securing agent runtimes and tool execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, developing reusable architectural patterns for agent sandboxing, hard guardrails, and cryptographic isolation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing security criteria for other AAIF deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Taxonomy / Landscape Delegation**: Represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman to the central [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

## Operating Procedures
- **System of Record**: GitHub serves as the system of record for maturing and final documents to preserve commit history and attribution, while Google Docs is restricted to early-stage brainstorming due to corporate access constraints[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Technical Committee Reporting**: Monthly progress reports follow a standardized template submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) during the last week of each month, initiating a 7-day acknowledgment window[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-12**: Initial taxonomy draft elevated to cross-WG AAIF initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: WG appointed Jay White and Katherine Druckman as delegates to the cross-WG Taxonomy workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Working group repository made public; taxonomy files transitioned to `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **2026-06-23**: Formally structured workstream lead structure, adopted TC monthly reporting template, and confirmed GitHub as system of record[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry specification and OpenTelemetry semantic mapping framework standardizing session-level execution structure, reasoning, and outcomes across agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an AAIF telemetry specification and semantic framework defining observable concepts across agent execution lifecycles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]. Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model correlates discrete runtime spans into multi-turn session behaviors, capturing execution flow, cognitive reasoning, and external environmental consequences while maintaining strict compatibility with OpenTelemetry standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification

## Trace Model Dimensions
The Agent Behavior Trace Model organizes agent telemetry across three foundational behavioral dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:
1. **Execution Structure**: Captures the temporal and topological relationships of agent operations, including subagent spawning, task delegation, tool execution loops, and control flow branching.
2. **Reasoning and Planning**: Records cognitive state transitions, planning steps, context assembly, and intermediate evaluations driving agent decisions.
3. **Outcomes and Effects**: Documents side effects, tool output mutations, external state modifications, and final task success or termination conditions.

## Taxonomy Plane Crosswalk
The specification maps its behavioral dimensions directly to four conceptual planes defined by the Observability and Traceability taxonomy[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:
- **Orchestration Plane**: Coordinates multi-agent flows, scheduling, and delegation hierarchies.
- **Execution Plane**: Tracks invocation of tools, code sandboxes, and runtime environments.
- **Protocol Plane**: Measures inter-agent and agent-to-tool wire traffic (such as MCP or A2A interactions).
- **Reasoning / Context Plane**: Monitors model token streams, memory retrieval, prompt construction, and context consumption.

## OpenTelemetry Guardrails and Adoption Strategy
The specification adheres to explicit alignment guardrails ensuring that AAIF definitions function as domain extensions rather than replacements for upstream OpenTelemetry schemas[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]. Under its 12-month charter roadmap, the working group employs a formal decision process to compare existing candidate models against defined evaluation criteria, pursuing adoption or extension of existing standards before determining whether a novel normative specification is required[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]. Coordination is also maintained with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing multi-turn telemetry alignment, session-level behavior tracing, and cross-boundary execution observability standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to defining telemetry standards, session-level execution tracing, and diagnostic frameworks across multi-turn agent systems. The working group harmonizes runtime observation mechanisms across model interactions, tool executions, and multi-agent coordination boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Groups and Deliverables

The working group structures its research and specifications across dedicated focus streams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:

- **LLM Primitives**: Develops landscape surveys and gap analyses auditing primitive interfaces and protocol observability models [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates memory architectures, persistence models, and context management across academic research and production platforms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Evaluates execution routing, multi-agent dialog state, and boundary event capture.
- **Agentic Reasoning & White-Box Tracing**: Examines internal model reasoning trajectories, internal representation tracing, and alignment with existing runtime telemetry specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

### Cross-Initiative Collaboration

The working group interfaces with external Foundation initiatives, including the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to standardize core terminology, and evaluates discovery boundaries defined in the [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Operational Governance

Working group activities, issue tracking, and Kanban milestone project boards are maintained publicly in GitHub repositories under the AAIF organization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. Biweekly synchronous sessions provide open presentation slots for community updates, while Discord serves as the primary day-to-day coordination channel [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. Progress, risks, and milestone deliveries report directly into the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on a monthly cadence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing measurement frameworks, failure mode taxonomies, reliable architecture patterns, and recovery mechanisms for enterprise agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under production enterprise conditions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Formally approved on May 15, 2026, the working group addresses non-deterministic agent behaviors by classifying failure modes, defining architectural resilience patterns, and standardizing proactive and reactive recovery actions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

ARWG operates under the leadership of co-chairs Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1], coordinating cross-cutting initiatives with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and delegating low-level telemetry transport mechanics to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44, ^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Guiding Principles and Core Assumptions
ARWG grounds its technical guidance on four key principles [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Reliability and Accuracy by Design:** Prioritizes architectural designs that prevent failures during planning and reasoning over reactive runtime patching.
- **Grounding in Observable Evidence:** Formulates recommendations based on measurable empirical signals and authoritative trust anchors.
- **Vendor Neutrality:** Maintains structural independence from proprietary model providers, orchestration runtimes, and commercial guardrail vendors.
- **Separation of Observability Outcomes:** Defines required reliability signals and failure indicators, delegating trace protocol mechanics to the observability domain.

The group operates under explicit engineering assumptions: agent runtimes will adopt standardized recovery hooks, agents possess immutable instance identifiers across evaluation cycles, configurations (models, prompts, tool definitions) are strictly versioned for reproducibility, and high-stakes tasks provide authoritative system-of-record trust anchors [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

## Scope Boundaries

### In-Scope Workstreams
ARWG focuses on three primary areas [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
1. **Accuracy & Reliability Frameworks:** Taxonomies of failure modes, performance metrics, drift detection protocols, and formal threshold standards for autonomous operation.
2. **Reliable Architecture Patterns:** Proactive structural patterns, such as closed verification loops and authoritative data grounding mechanisms.
3. **Recovery and Corrective Actions:** Specifications for safe-state restoration, state rollback, automated compensation mechanisms, and human intervention handoff triggers.

### Out-of-Scope Activities
The working group explicitly excludes foundation model training and prompt engineering, log and trace wire format standards, production orchestrator runtime development, and jurisdiction-specific regulatory policies [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

## Deliverable Pipeline
ARWG organizes its output across canonical deliverables D1 through D6 and internal operational processes [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]:
- **D1 (Vocabulary and Architectural Framing):** Theoretical and structural terminology establishing evaluation subjects, accuracy dimensions, symptoms, root causes, and correction primitives [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis and Benchmark Survey):** Applied analysis covering multi-persona enterprise requirements, benchmark shortcomings, and interoperability tooling gaps [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D3–D6 & I1:** Downstream engineering guidance, normative evaluation protocols (D6), and internal operational tracking [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

# Lifecycle History
The charter was approved on May 15, 2026, and updated on June 30, 2026 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Deliverable IDs were harmonized to D1–D6 in PR #6 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]. In June 2026, the working group initiated biweekly plenary sessions alternating with D2 working tracks, aligned terminology efforts with the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream, and assigned working group liaisons [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, schema-validated vocabularies, and an interactive ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative tasked with building a unified conceptual vocabulary and an authoritative ecosystem directory for agentic AI systems [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream eliminates siloed terminology and prevents duplicative research by standardizing domain definitions across all foundation working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

The workstream operates an asynchronous, pull-request-driven governance workflow backed by formal working group delegates and domain editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. All terminology definitions are formatted against a SKOS-Lite schema, while ecosystem mapping leverages the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) landscape tool format [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Architecture / Specification

### Data Schemas and Structure

The workstream utilizes two primary structural standards:

1. **Taxonomy Metadata (`SKOS-Lite`)**: Concepts are organized into machine-readable definitions requiring a concise summary for beginners and detailed scope notes for technical practitioners [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Definitions must align with international standards including ISO and NIST, documenting explicit deviations where agentic architectures require refined semantics [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
2. **Ecosystem Landscape (CNCF Format)**: Technology products, runtimes, protocols, and member contributions are cataloged into an interactive map built on the CNCF Landscape 2 generator [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1], linking directly with `landscape.aaif.io` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

### Ingestion and Governance Process

Terminology lifecycle follows a structured multi-stage workflow:

- **Pre-PR Staging**: Raw terms are aggregated into a unified cross-working-group tracking document to identify overlapping scopes and resolve cross-domain conflicts globally before drafting [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Asynchronous PR Submission**: Terms are submitted via individual pull requests adhering to the definitions style guide and AI usage policies mandating human verification [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Domain Editor Attestation**: Designated working group delegates review proposals to ensure architectural fidelity before merging into the main taxonomy registry [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

### Reporting and Technical Committee Oversight

The workstream submits formal monthly progress updates to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on the last business day of each calendar month using the standard reporting format [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]. Reports enter a 7-day asynchronous TC review window before merging [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-21**: Kickoff meeting established the core mission, weekly Monday sync cadence, SKOS-Lite taxonomy schema, and PR-driven workflow model [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].
- **2026-06-01**: Aligned on CNCF-style metadata structure, two-tier definitions (summary and scope notes), and integration plans with `landscape.aaif.io` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **2026-06-08**: Formed delegate core team across working groups and agreed to treat boundary definitions as continuous deliverables [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **2026-06-15**: Reset seed definitions in the repository to enforce the formal review pipeline and committed to ISO/NIST alignment and an explicit AI usage policy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **2026-06-30**: Formally approved the Workstream Charter across participating working groups, deployed web portal CI/CD pipelines, onboarded delegates across WGs (with [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) outstanding), and collected initial batches of 10–20 core terms per working group into a unified spreadsheet [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# References

- [AAIF Landscape Catalog](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)
- [Taxonomy Contribution Skill](../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md)
- [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing compliance frameworks, policy-as-code mapping, risk assessment baselines, and regulatory alignment for autonomous AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) is an AAIF technical body established to evaluate regulatory landscapes, map AI policy frameworks, and develop compliance and governance guidance for autonomous AI systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Operational Structure and Milestones
The working group organizes its efforts around multi-month milestone sprints focusing on policy landscape mapping and comparative regulatory assessments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

- **Policy Landscape Mapping**: Completed a three-month initiative mapping existing agentic AI policy frameworks, standards, guidance documents, and industry best practices to identify structural governance challenges[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Gap and Comparative Analysis**: Progressed into a three-month sprint executing a gap analysis, addressing comparative baselines across regulatory and industry benchmarks[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Completed initial three-month landscape assessment mapping policy frameworks; initiated three-month sprint for gap analysis under chairs Ryan Hagemann and Deborah Eng[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body chartered to define telemetry standards, boundary observability models, and verifiable execution tracing across agent runtimes, protocol layers, and multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# Focus Groups and Deliverables
The working group executes deliverables across specialized focus groups addressing agent telemetry layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]:

- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Merged from two previously distinct focus groups to eliminate deliverable overlaps, addressing foundation model primitives, communication boundaries, and protocol telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Focuses on orchestration, inter-agent coordination, and distributed workflow tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic State, Context & Reasoning**: Investigates runtime context representation, persistent memory states, and decision graph traces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Hardened Traceability Architectures**: Led by Ty Smith to develop recommendations for provable, tamper-evident execution tracing architectures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

The working group also coordinates with the [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) specification initiative and the Cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra and Matthew Lee; initiated charter deliverables, focus groups, and GitHub-based use case and gap analysis tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **2026-07**: Consolidated LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability focus groups to streamline meetings by problem scope, and reviewed Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) trust integration[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, schema-validated vocabularies, and an interactive landscape ecosystem catalog.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to unify agentic AI terminology, define standardized ontology schemas, and catalog the open-source agent ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream includes delegate representatives from every AAIF technical working group to coordinate cross-domain vocabularies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Operations and Review Workflow
The workstream manages vocabulary review via a PR-driven workflow and centralized working spreadsheets containing multi-group candidate terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]:

- **Terminology Targets**: Working groups contribute 10–20 core terms toward an initial v1.0 taxonomy release[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Consensus and Culling**: Employs a consensus "cull" classification to filter generic software terms while retaining agent-specific and accuracy terminology[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Contentious definitions are escalated through Discord community discussions before resolution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-WG Harmonization**: Reconciles overlaps across domain groups, distinguishing foundational terms such as "agent" versus "bot", and establishing distinct concepts such as "Agent Card" alongside "Agent Blueprint"[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05**: Kickoff meeting establishing the charter, PR-driven workflow, and weekly sync cadence[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-06**: Phased curation kickoff, style guide alignment, delegate roster formation, and monthly PR reporting[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-07**: Transitioned into the review phase for ~250 terms across working groups, introduced a consensus cull tracking column, and extended weekly meetings to one hour[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

mutations.rationale: Record deliverable leads, completion of Deliverable 4 (Threat Modeling Gap Analysis), submission of the Security Best Practices draft, and cross-foundation liaisons.

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing controls, and security best practices for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body chartered to identify systemic security risks, publish threat models, evaluate defensive architecture patterns, and formulate operational security controls for autonomous AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group advances several active deliverables managed by designated workstream co-leads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating existing frameworks (MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) across eight behavioral threat domains to publish Deliverable 4[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing operational guidance and gap mitigations for agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security & Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining structured reference designs for runtime security controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing a review gate for architectural and security cross-WG evaluations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

The working group maintains external liaison and alignment efforts with OWASP, AARM, and ETSI TC SAI, while assessing interoperability with LF FINOS AI initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07**: Completed the fourth threat modeling gap analysis deliverable, submitted the first draft of the Security Best Practices Guide, and coordinated delegate participation in the unified [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate the approved workstream charter, leadership structure, meeting cadence, delegate governance model, and web portal deployment pipeline.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, SKOS-Lite vocabularies, and an interactive CNCF-style ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative tasked with curating a unified glossary of agentic AI terminology and maintaining an authoritative ecosystem landscape map.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] Approved on June 21, 2026, the workstream eliminates terminology silos across specialized foundation working groups, prevents duplicate ecosystem research across domains, and provides enterprise technology leaders with a single reference blueprint for the agentic software stack.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Delegate Model
The workstream operates under a federated curation model led by Junjie Bu (Google) as Chair and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) as Co-Chair.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] Rather than authoring vertical domain definitions in isolation, the workstream ingests, reconciles, and deduplicates glossaries provided by active AAIF technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] Each working group chair nominates two Domain Editors to participate in weekly synchronizations and asynchronous pull request reviews—for example, Jay White and Katherine Druckman represent [WG Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

## Scope Boundaries
The workstream maintains strict scope guardrails distinguishing horizontal consolidation from vertical technical ownership:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Horizontal Curation (In Scope):** Consolidating cross-cutting terminology into a SKOS-Lite metadata schema (`prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, `contrastsWith`), maintaining the global CNCF-style ecosystem architecture map (`landscape.yml`), arbitrating terminology intersections between working groups, and operating automated web deployment pipelines.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Vertical Ownership (Out of Scope):** Specialized domain whitepapers (such as regulatory compliance analyses belonging to [WG Governance, Risk & Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)), low-level protocol designs (such as MCP or A2A specifications reserved for vertical working groups), and closed commercial enterprise portals.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

## Portal Architecture and CI/CD
The workstream distributes the interactive Shared Taxonomy Explorer and Landscape Map through automated GitHub Actions workflows deploying to GitHub Pages.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea] The portal build workflow compiles:
1. The CNCF Landscape 2 configuration and data files (`landscape.yml` and static assets).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]
2. The interactive taxonomy directory (`taxonomy/` and `taxonomy-data.js`).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
3. The main landing interface (`index.html`) stamped with a Pacific Time build timestamp.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-21:** Formal charter approved establishing the workstream chairs, federated Domain Editor model, weekly meeting cadence (Mondays at 8:30 AM PT), and delivery roadmap.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **2026-06-30:** [WG Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) formally transitioned its Taxonomy of Terms effort into the workstream, appointing Jay White and Katherine Druckman as delegates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

mutations.rationale: Update leadership, active workstream structure, reporting cadence, and deliverable progress following the June 2026 monthly report to the Technical Committee.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing standards, and security best practices for autonomous agent deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d] Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the working group shifted from initial formation into operational execution in mid-2026 across five active workstreams.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5]

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Scope
The working group organizes its technical outputs into five confirmed workstreams governed by dedicated leads and scoping documentation:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Threat Modeling:** Developing the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) evaluating external frameworks such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Best Practices:** Drafting the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) for operational security controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Taxonomy Delegation:** The former internal Taxonomy of Terms workstream was transitioned to the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as delegates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **External Collaboration:** Interfacing with external security efforts including OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS to align messaging and defensive standards across ecosystems, under guidance requested from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

## TC Reporting and Governance Cadence
The working group reports to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on a standardized monthly cadence:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]
- **Submission Window:** Reports are prepared following `TEMPLATE.md` and submitted by the last business day of the calendar month.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5]
- **Review Period:** The TC review window closes within seven calendar days of submission, after which reports are merged following sign-off or deadline expiration.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]
- **Charter KPIs:** Each report benchmarks progress against four core charter metrics: Adoption, Quality, Community, and Timeliness.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-30:** Submitted the first monthly report to the Technical Committee for June 2026, marking public availability of repositories, formalization of five workstream leads, transition of taxonomy efforts to the cross-WG initiative, and draft completion of the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing guidance, and operational security baselines for autonomous AI agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group structures its technical production across dedicated workstreams and leads:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, producing comparative threat frameworks across agent architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, documenting practical defensive recommendations and incorporating prior industry contributions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, categorizing reusable architectural security primitives.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing systematic security and privacy verification criteria across AAIF deliverables.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinated through delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman alongside the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream, targeting definitions for session replay resistance, constraints, and guardrails.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# External Liaison
Formal institutional collaborations with bodies such as OWASP remain pending approval by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), with informal technical alignment proceeding in the interim.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Overview

The group's work program addresses multi-layer observability across application and network boundaries:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

- **Peer-to-Peer and Network Telemetry**: Investigates agent network measurement across peer-to-peer layers (including libp2p, Lumina, and multiformats) and coordinates with IETF observability initiatives such as Agent Proto, DMSC, and Dawn.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Multi-Agent Delegation and Tracing**: Evaluates multi-agent trace context propagation and cross-boundary correlation models.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

The working group aligns with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) regarding cryptographic payload verification and identity-aware telemetry, as well as the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream for universal terminology harmonisation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, state persistence patterns, and external system coordination across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration (W&PI) Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group established to define a shared workflow model, standardized terminology, and interoperability patterns for agentic AI systems across diverse runtime environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and co-chaired by Adam Seligman (Workato), the group focuses on enabling workflows to coordinate tools, multi-agent hierarchies, external APIs, and human oversight while avoiding vendor lock-in [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group addresses core challenges in enterprise agent orchestration across three primary scope areas [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:

- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Defining universal primitives for tasks, tool invocations, branching, retries, and agent handoffs, bridging non-deterministic agent planning with deterministic workflow engines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Long-Running and Stateful Execution**: Codifying patterns for multi-day workflows, state persistence, idempotency, failure recovery, and workflow-level audit systems of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Tool and External System Coordination**: Developing vendor-neutral patterns for agent interaction with external systems, APIs, CLIs, and asynchronous human approval gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

W&PI explicitly delineates its domain from runtime observability signals like traces and metrics, which are coordinated in collaboration with `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-13**: Charter formally approved by the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **2026-07-23**: Charter updated with detailed deliverable definitions, operating cadences, and cross-WG coordination guidelines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# References

- [W&PI GitHub Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical working group tasked with developing measurement methodologies, enterprise gap analyses, and reliability benchmarks for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group coordinates foundational terminology for system consistency, correctness, and operational robustness [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Architecture / Specification

The group operates across key deliverables and cross-foundation alignment initiatives [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]:

- **D1 (Terminology and Methodology Grounding)**: A staged execution deliverable establishing literature-grounded definitions for dimensions such as outcome correctness, consistency across repeated runs, robustness against perturbations, and production reliability [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. D1 feeds core terminology into `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis)**: A deliverable evaluating practitioner-facing requirements and real-world adoption blockers rather than purely synthetic benchmark inventories [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. It identifies pain points via enterprise surveys across cost, quality, and operational consistency [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **Inter-Group Liaisons (I1)**: Establishing coordination channels with parallel initiatives, including `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-31**: Monthly report submitted documenting transition of D1 to a public pull request, delivery of initial terms to the unified taxonomy, and refocusing of D2 on practitioner gap analysis [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# References

- [ARWG July 2026 Report](https://github.com/aaif/wg-accuracy-and-reliability/blob/10bc173f00e45d93a8f7038cb0c36a89e3219565/reporting/2026-07-report.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and interoperability frameworks across the agentic commerce lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is a technical initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]. The group operates as a protocol-neutral forum tasked with analyzing and harmonizing interfaces across autonomous shopping, merchant catalog discovery, negotiated checkout, payment authorization, fraud risk evaluation, and post-purchase state management[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

Rather than specifying a competing monolithic standard, the working group catalogs existing industry protocols—such as the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agent Payment Protocol (AP2), Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), and x402—identifying integration gaps, trust boundaries, and reusable capability abstractions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Scope and Deliverables

The group focuses on external, commerce-facing interfaces and signals rather than platform internals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. Primary charter deliverables include:

- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map**: A multi-stage taxonomy and capability matrix cataloging actor roles, discovery models, delegated authority checkpoints, checkout negotiations, payment handling, fraud signals, and post-purchase interactions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Commerce Protocol Gap Analysis**: A comparative assessment of existing protocols identifying overlaps, friction points, trust assumptions, and missing handoffs across multi-turn commerce flows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Best Practices and Reference Architectures**: Implementation guidelines addressing credential security, merchant burden mitigation, and multi-actor handoffs[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

# Lifecycle Analysis

The working group organizes its technical evaluations along five lifecycle phases:

1. **Product Discovery**: Contrasts asynchronous product feeds with real-time merchant and marketplace queries, focusing on provenance, catalog freshness, schema normalization, and origin authenticity[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Evaluates stateful, merchant-authoritative transactions, protocol extensibility, transport bindings, and transitions requiring human oversight[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
3. **Payment Handling**: Deconstructs payment orchestration into three core primitives—handler, instrument, and credential—while evaluating static capability discovery against dynamic eligibility, delegated tokenization, and MPP challenge-credential-receipt mechanisms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
4. **Fraud and Trust Signals**: Formulates mechanisms to preserve transaction context across shopper, agent platform, merchant, payment processor, and risk-engine boundaries; isolates agent identity and behavioral risk from shopper identity; and evaluates portable baseline attestations alongside risk-triggered context requests[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
5. **Post-Purchase Operations**: Evaluates the boundary between read-only order monitoring and active state transitions, including cancellations, returns, refunds, and dispute arbitration[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Cross-Working-Group Collaborations

The group coordinates closely with related AAIF bodies:
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authority, decentralized identifiers, and shopper-to-agent credential binding[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for data boundary isolation, credential sandboxing, and sensitive payment data protection[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) for distributed intent tracking, action records, and cross-boundary audit logging[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026**: Working group kickoff and initial actor inventory mapping platforms, merchants, payment networks, and protocol proposals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026**: Adoption of a problem-first lifecycle methodology spanning discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **April 2026**: Delivery of comparative deep dives into discovery feeds versus live queries, stateful checkout protocols (ACP/UCP), and draft charter formulation[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **May 2026**: Official approval of the Working Group charter and payment-handler architecture review comparing ACP, UCP, and MPP[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **June 2026**: Trust and fraud signal analysis delineating agent risk from shopper identity and defining bounded context propagation models[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
