proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Foundational execution vocabulary standardizing multi-agent and human workflows around independent activities, state machines, and boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Workflow primitives provide the foundational terminology and structural abstractions for describing agentic and human-in-the-loop workflows within the Agentic AI Foundation. Under the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group, execution units are anchored on the concept of an Activity rather than legacy workflow steps or tasks[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification
The primitives establish an execution ontology decoupled from circular dependencies:
- **Activity**: The atomic, bounded unit of work within a workflow, defined independently from the overarching workflow orchestrator to avoid circular semantics[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]. An activity encapsulates a discrete operational step executed by an agent, tool, or human participant.
- **Workflow**: A directed composition or orchestration of activities governed by transition rules, acceptance gates, and convergence loops.

Replacing the terminology of "Workflow Step" and "Workflow Task" with "Activity" ensures consistency with established workflow engines while preventing recursive definitional dependency on "Workflow"[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

# Lifecycle History
In PR#31 of `wg-workflows-and-process-integration`, the working group formally deprecated and replaced "Workflow Step / Workflow Task" with "Activity" in `workstreams/taxonomy/terms.md` to break circular definition cycles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, SKOS-Lite vocabularies, and an interactive ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (`ws-taxonomy-landscape`) is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation establishing unified terminology, shared ontologies, and ecosystem categorization across all foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. It provides domain editors, terminological governance, and the AAIF Landscape portal.

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates through weekly terminology-review syncs and structured pull requests to evaluate candidate concepts against domain working group scopes:
- **Universal Terms**: Establishes cross-cutting core primitives such as `Agent` and `Harness`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Relational Ontologies**: Explicitly models semantic relationships between adjacent concepts, including `Skill` versus `Tool`, `Kill switch` versus `Reversibility`, `Harness` versus `Meta-harness`, and `Delegation` versus `Handoff`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Working Group Representation**: Engages cross-group domain editors representing Identity & Trust, Agentic Commerce, Security & Privacy, and Workflows & Process Integration[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the workstream transitioned from term intake into definition drafting and cross-domain harmonization[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. Across three syncs, the group reviewed 53 candidate terms (keeping 37, culling 15, and holding `Multi-agent misdirection` in debate). Definitions for `Harness` merged in PR#37, while definitions for `Human in the loop`, `Meta-harness`, and Identity & Trust entered formal PR review[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluation matrices, and operational specifications for autonomous buyer and merchant agent interactions across the commerce lifecycle[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its core deliverable roadmap around:
- **Deliverable 1 (Capability Map)**: Categorizes pre-purchase, transaction, and post-purchase capability rows (P1–P7) including eligibility inquiry, remedy offer and negotiation, buyer authorization, state-change execution signals, evidence binding, dispute initiation, and adjustment ledgers[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Evidence & Auditability Envelope**: Specifies an 8-field bounded verdict envelope (`verdict`, `verifier`, `verifier_signature`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_fingerprints`, `verification_basis`, `witness_scope`, `timestamp`) for machine-readable settlement and post-purchase auditability[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Cross-Group Terminology & Trust Alignment**: Integrates with [ws-taxonomy-landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) via dedicated working group liaisons[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] and aligns evidence records with [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group expanded its post-purchase workstream via PR#6, providing concrete inputs for Deliverable 1 capability rows P1–P7 and cross-boundary auditability envelopes[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6], while coordinating terminology alignment with the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry specification and OpenTelemetry semantic mapping framework standardizing session-level execution, turn continuity, and multi-agent interaction tracing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to standardize session-level, turn-level, and cross-runtime execution observability across AI agent frameworks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification and nine-task execution plan define practical instrumentation and semantic correlation standards:
- **Baseline Gap Classification**: Differentiates implementation defects, missing instrumentation, and absent semantics by comparing baseline telemetry across independent runtimes (such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and reference SDKs)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Session and Turn Continuity**: Connects completed turns across distributed traces without requiring an uninterrupted, long-running session span[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]. It standardizes correlation across process restarts, pause/resume lifecycles, and caller-trace context propagation while preserving native runtime identities[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].
- **OpenTelemetry Semantic Mapping**: Maps multi-turn conversations, tool invocations, and agent state transitions into vendor-neutral OTel span attributes and events[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

# Lifecycle History
Following August 2026 working group sessions, an execution plan established structured tasks, including Task 2 for multi-runtime baseline telemetry captures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40] and Task 5 for trace continuity across standalone and resumed interaction turns[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and transaction standards for autonomous agent commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral capability models, integration patterns, and protocol evaluations for delegated and autonomous commercial transactions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses agent payment primitives, post-transaction dispute evidence, and machine-to-machine exchange standards[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes commerce capabilities across conversational and autonomous operational modes:
- **Payment Capability Rails**: Evaluates payment rails including x402 (a Linux Foundation project abstracting single transactions into scheme, network, asset, and mechanism layers), AP2, UCP, and ACP across HTTP, MCP, and A2A transports[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Dispute and Accountability Boundaries**: Investigates replacement mechanisms for absent human cardholder evidence, analyzing verifiable-intent records, know-your-agent (KYA) identity frameworks, consent surfaces for silent merchant policy acceptance, and rich transaction metadata (agent identifiers, platform metadata, model versions)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Protocol Deep Dives**: Actively evaluates emerging commercial exchange protocols, including Order Network eXchange (OnX) and Machine Payment Protocol (MPP)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

# Lifecycle History

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing standards, and security implementation guidelines for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. The group produces normative guidance, static-analysis security rules, and cross-working group governance checklists[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group advances several core workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: A practical security guide governing architectural controls and operational failures, scheduled for freeze and release as the group's first official deliverable (with identity and trust concerns deferred to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Actionable Static Analysis Rules**: A code-facing companion tool converting best practice guidelines into automated rules applicable to agent SDKs (evaluating Google, Amazon, and Microsoft agent SDKs)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural patterns including the [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern family and upcoming memory-security patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Security review criteria coordinated across sister working groups including Observability, Governance, Accuracy and Reliability, and Agentic Commerce[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-09-01, the group decided to freeze and merge version 1 of the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide, reviewed initial taxonomy PRs for security terminology, and coordinated cross-working group review efforts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing multi-turn telemetry standards, cross-layer observability models, and verifiable behavioral tracing specifications for AI agents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. The group addresses execution visibility spanning high-level agent reasoning down to kernel syscall instrumentation and cryptographic action auditing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification
Key workstreams and sub-initiatives include:
- **Primitives and Protocols Focus Group**: Directs full-stack agent provenance and extends tracing below L7, incorporating syscall-level monitoring and system-level observability for runtime environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Standardizes multi-turn telemetry and execution traces, progressing through an execution plan that includes runnable provider and agent examples (Task 8) for community contribution and testing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].
- **Cryptographic Action Auditing**: Evaluates structures like Agent Action Capsules—tamper-evident records combining dispatched actions, runtime boundaries, and cryptographic verification through ledger systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry**: Tracing integration across Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Agent Gateway, and agent-to-agent interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group established lower-layer provenance leadership under the Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group, reviewed the Agent Action Capsule demonstration, and advanced the Agent Behavior Trace Model implementation roadmap[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between agent intent generation and execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval reference architecture establishes an enforceable human approval gate and a structural break between agent intent generation and real-world execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]. By strictly separating the proposal, authorization, and execution stages, the pattern prevents autonomous side effects until an authenticated human operator signs off on candidate actions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture separates workflows into distinct operational phases:
1. **Proposal Phase**: The agent ingests context and generates proposed actions or artifacts (such as updated FAQ copy or product release notes) without direct write or publication authority[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
2. **Approval Checkpoint**: Proposed actions are presented through an approval gate (such as [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) or [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)) that binds the proposal record to immutable execution payloads[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
3. **Publication / Execution Boundary**: Once explicit human authorization is granted, a separated execution worker or publishing pipeline commits the action[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

The architecture validates across content management and publishing workflows:
- **Knowledge Base and FAQ Updates**: Agent generates proposed answers and updates; human reviews technical accuracy before content sync[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Release Notes Compilation**: Agent analyzes repository changelogs and drafts release notes; human verifies version claims before publication[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Catalog and Listing Descriptions**: Agent drafts listing metadata; operator verifies compliance with platform rules prior to live catalog updates[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Lifecycle History
Validated against real-world content publishing scenarios in the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md) via PR #36 in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# References
- [Workflows WG Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration)
- Related patterns: [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md).

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand and Design System Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, and asset usage constraints governing AAIF interfaces and generated documents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF brand and design system establishes visual identity rules, typography standards, token architectures, and asset usage constraints across all foundation properties and generated reports.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] The system is built around a single typeface, strictly flat geometry, distinct dual surfaces without generic dark mode, and precise color token semantics.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

# Architecture / Specification
The design system isolates tokens into a machine-generated CSS layer (`design/aaif-tokens.css`) extracted from `design/aaif-design-system.html` via automated scripts to preserve consistency across tooling and automated skills.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

Key styling invariants include:
- **Color Tokens**: The primary action accent is pure black (`--accent: var(--ink)`).[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve strictly as secondary accents within a surface, with coral designated as `--spec-8` rather than an overall brand accent.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] Ground surfaces utilize `--paper`, reserving `--paper-2` for section banding and `--paper-3` for tinted panels.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Dual Surfaces and Dark Mode**: The system defines two first-class surfaces: white editorial and black plate, each chosen deliberately per component.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] Inverted dark modes and `prefers-color-scheme` blocks are explicitly prohibited, as inverted twin palettes violate the visual language.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Typography**: The single brand typeface is Instrument Sans across weights 400, 500, 600, and 700 for display and UI copy.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] Headings use weight 500 with tight tracking (`-0.02em`) and line-heights between 1.05 and 1.15 rather than standard bold, with weight 600 reserved only for h5/h6 levels.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] Monospace stacks are strictly limited to metadata and eyebrow indicators.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Geometry and Depth**: Drop shadows are prohibited; visual depth is achieved exclusively through 1px hairlines, surface tint transitions, and inset strokes.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] Cards, tables, and chips maintain square corners (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded pill tokens (`--radius-pill`) exclusively for interactive buttons and count badges.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Motif and Mark Assets**: Official vector assets in `assets/` (`aaif-mark.svg`, `aaif-mark-square.svg`, and `aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be rendered verbatim without redrawing.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] The decorative agent motif derived from mark primitives is permitted for empty states, dividers, and community event collateral, but strictly prohibited on governance, board, or press publications.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

# Lifecycle History
The design system specification was formalized within repository tooling to ensure report generators, skills such as `../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md`, and chapter provisioning tools render uniform documents across the ecosystem.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3] Its technical framework ensures agents can be discovered across platforms, prove identity, demonstrate delegation authority, and verify human approvals across systems and organizational boundaries.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates technical deliverables across interoperability protocols, trust assertions, and delegation frameworks aligned with the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`):[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Core Focus**: Developing specifications for machine-readable identity verification, attestation of runtime environments (such as `../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md`), and signed action logs via `../standards/evidence-record-spec.md`.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Operational Cadence**: Public working group meetings occur weekly on Thursdays, alternating between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM US Pacific Time over LFX Zoom infrastructure, with recordings and summaries cataloged on LFX.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Communication Channels**: Collaboration is hosted via the public mailing list (`wg-identity-trust@lists.aaif.io`) and the dedicated AAIF Discord community channels.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

# Lifecycle History
The working group leadership was appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members, with Grant Miller (IBM) serving as Chair and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE) serving as Co-Chair for the term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group serves as the technical bridge between evolving global AI regulatory regimes and practical implementation architectures within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a] Led by co-chairs Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates statutory requirements, compliance obligations, and risk management frameworks into actionable technical criteria for autonomous systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]

# Architecture / Specification
The group's multi-phase roadmap aligns public policy requirements with engineering standards:
- **Phase 1 Landscape Analysis**: Identification and indexing of global policy instruments, governance frameworks, and technical standards applicable to agentic systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]
- **Phase 2 Gap Analysis and Thematic Mapping**: Mapping evaluated policy instruments against approximately twelve core governance themes, supported by structured AI prompts designed for repeatable information extraction across regulations and standards.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]
- **Phase 3 Deliverables**: Final publication of unified risk and compliance guidelines connecting statutory mandates to reference architectures and testing specifications, interfacing with sibling groups such as `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group concluded the foundational phase of its landscape analysis and commenced Phase 2 mapping across policy instruments, maintaining a policy of deferring public releases until the comprehensive Phase 3 milestone is completed.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure and governance requirements for open-source projects submitting proposals for AAIF hosting across lifecycle stages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process establishes the operational requirements and review stages for prospective open-source projects applying for AAIF hosting across the Sandbox, Growth, and Impact lifecycle tiers.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] Intake is administered through GitHub issue templates evaluated jointly by the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`) and the Governing Board under Linux Foundation legal oversight.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

# Architecture / Specification
The submission and evaluation procedure mandates explicit legal and governance checkpoints before any project can be designated as an official AAIF project:[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
- **Standardized Application Intake**: Proposers must submit a structured application via the `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/project-proposal.yml` template in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository, detailing project origin, architectural alignment with the AAIF mission, and relationships to existing foundation projects.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] Initial triage is handled by assigned TC intake leads.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
- **Contribution Agreement Gate**: A formal Contribution Agreement is generated from application contacts and must be signed by the project maintainers prior to a Governing Board vote.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] The agreement is countersigned by the Linux Foundation only after an affirmative vote.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
- **Dual Approval Requirement**: Official hosting requires affirmative approval votes from both the Technical Committee (evaluating technical readiness and scope) and the Governing Board (evaluating ecosystem governance and legal fit).[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] Projects may not represent themselves as donated or contributed until all formal execution gates conclude.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

# Lifecycle History
The proposal workflow was formalized in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository to operationalize the foundation's tiered progression model documented in `../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md`.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral architectures, delegation models, and identity specifications for autonomous agent ecosystems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) is a technical body within the Agentic AI Foundation developing vendor-neutral viewpoints, reference architectures, and specifications for autonomous agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, authorization, discovery, consent, and auditability.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f] While traditional identity systems were designed for humans signing into applications or static workloads authenticating to services, agentic systems introduce unresolved requirements around agent provenance, delegation context survival across organizational boundaries, and non-repudiable evidence for human consequential approvals.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives into specialized breakout groups that coordinate back to the plenary session:

- **Use Cases Breakout**: Coordinated by Wei Chen, this track grounds group outputs in concrete enterprise and consumer scenarios to derive rigorous identity and trust requirements.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]
- **Reference Architecture Breakout**: Coordinated by Brian Malone, this track models actors, software components, trust relationships, and interoperability gaps required to govern delegated agent authority.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]
- **Taxonomy Coordination**: Led by liaisons Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky, this track aligns identity and trust concepts with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]

The working group evaluates external specifications and production architectures to identify interoperability gaps:
- [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) for capability registration and federated discovery.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]
- Production identity architectures employing SPIFFE/SPIRE for workload attestation, per-hop token exchange, and actor chain validation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]
- Hardware-attested execution frameworks, including NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace reference design.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]
- External protocol standards such as the IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization draft (`draft-klrc-aiagent-auth`).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]
- Shared execution sandboxes such as Vector for deploying and testing identity primitives under bounded consequence environments.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8]

# Lifecycle History
The working group operates under AAIF and Linux Foundation governance, holding alternating biweekly Thursday plenary meetings at 06:30 and 09:00 Pacific Time.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f] Working proposals progress from breakout working documents into formal repository issues and pull requests, with scheduled presentations and discussion topics tracked through an outstanding agenda queue.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing multi-turn telemetry standards, cross-layer observability models, and semantic conventions for agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed trace propagation rules, and evaluation models for multi-turn AI agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50] The working group resolves visibility and auditability challenges across LLM reasoning loops, tool invocations, asynchronous job queues, and cross-organizational delegation boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The group develops standardized architectures and telemetry conventions across multiple execution layers:

- **Agent Identity Telemetry & Semantic Conventions**: In cross-review with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the group is scoping standardized OpenTelemetry span attributes for agent identity (including `agent.id`, `agent.role`, `agent.invocation_id`, `agent.principal.type`, and `agent.delegation_depth`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]
- **Cross-Boundary Context Propagation**: Defining W3C Baggage and Trace Context protocols that guarantee causal lineage and identity preservation from user requests through orchestrators, subagents, and tool sandbox boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]
- **Telemetry Boundary Security**: Establishing redaction and sanitization rules prohibiting cryptographic keys, tokens, and sensitive signatures from general APM telemetry backends, segregating them into dedicated audit stores.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]
- **High-Frequency Sampling & Cost Governance**: Conducting cardinality assessments to prevent high-frequency agent tool dispatches from creating unsustainable observability storage overhead.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]

# Lifecycle History
The working group aligns its specifications with OpenTelemetry LLM semantic conventions, W3C Distributed Tracing standards, and emerging specifications such as aauth.dev and the OpenID AuthZEN COAZ-MCP binding.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Catalog of production agentic workflows classified by orchestration structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, coordination models, and empirical vendor citations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory documents empirical implementations of production agentic workflows, categorizing each deployment across orchestration structure, coordination mechanisms, autonomy constraints, and verification gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] Maintained by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group ([`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)), the catalog validates architectural classifications against vendor documentation and technical specifications rather than speculative capabilities.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

# Architecture / Specification
Workflows in the inventory are classified using the schema defined in [`./agentic-use-case-classification.md`](./agentic-use-case-classification.md). Recent verification cycles resolved structural attributes across several production use cases:
- **Lead Research & Enrichment**: Classified as a `Sequential pipeline` based on waterfall provider enrichment workflows executing sequential data retrieval stages.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **On-Call Incident Summary**: Classified as `Parallel fan-out`, `Inherently multi-agent`, and `AI-coordinated, planning` based on production incident response architectures where a supervisor splits context across concurrent sub-agents to avoid context saturation and dynamically re-plans based on incoming findings.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **Contract Review & Red-Lining**: Coordination classified as `AI-coordinated, planning` based on legal analysis systems generating and adjusting structured analysis plans.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

Rows where cited sources describe capability without evidencing execution structure—such as deterministic convergence gates in network anomaly detection or explicit execution order in compliance tracking—remain classified as `Unspecified` to preserve evidentiary rigor.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

# Lifecycle History
Classification maintenance systematically audits citation accessibility, resolving broken links and reverting unsourced claims.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] Open questions regarding pipeline versus fan-out criteria continue to be evaluated against operational use cases.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: Twelve-column classification schema defining structural dimensions, coordination mechanisms, and execution patterns for production agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification schema provides a normalized evaluation framework for classifying agent workflows by orchestration structure, autonomy boundaries, and multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47] It establishes precise criteria for characterizing implementations cataloged in [`./agentic-use-case-inventory.md`](./agentic-use-case-inventory.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

# Architecture / Specification
The schema categorizes workflow orchestration patterns, including `Parallel fan-out` and `Sequential pipeline`. However, working group evaluation identified an open definitional tension between these two structural categories:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]
- **Timing vs. Dependency Mismatch**: `Parallel fan-out` is defined by operational execution timing ("concurrent sub-tasks"), whereas `Sequential pipeline` is defined by data dependency ("dependent activities, each feeding the next"). Because timing and dependency are not mutually exclusive opposites, workflows can fail to fit cleanly into either definition.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]
- **Interpretive Approaches**: The working group identified three candidate interpretations for resolving classification: timing as observed at runtime, agent count boundaries, or data dependency graphs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

Resolution of this open question governs whether classification reflects a specific vendor's technical implementation or the intrinsic requirements of the use case.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

# Lifecycle History
Developed by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group ([`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)), this schema continues to evolve as edge cases and classification ambiguities are surfaced from production inventory audits.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry specification and OpenTelemetry semantic mapping framework standardizing session-level execution traces and upstream GenAI conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the Observability & Traceability Working Group ([`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)) to capture multi-turn agent execution, turn transitions, and tool invocation lifecycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47] The model standardizes trace representations across disparate agent runtimes and establishes upstream alignment with the OpenTelemetry (OTel) GenAI semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model links runtime behavioral events to OpenTelemetry spans and attributes. Under Task 9 of the working group's execution plan, empirical trace findings are channeled into upstream standards and runtime fixes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Upstream OTel Semantic Conventions**: Contributing recommendations to OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions to address gaps such as identifying turn-entry spans and standardizing conversation session identifiers across multi-turn exchanges.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Runtime Instrumentation Fixes**: Providing patches directly to agent runtime maintainers where existing runtimes track context identifiers internally (such as conversation IDs) but omit them from emitted spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Vocabulary Alignment**: Bridging taxonomy concepts with the AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group ([`../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)) to harmonize terminology around session boundaries, agent states, and delegation spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Lifecycle History
The Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan comprises a nine-task development lifecycle following the August 2026 working group meetings, transitioning from baseline specification design to active upstream contribution and testing against experimental extensions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical security implementation guidance, failure patterns, and architectural controls across secrets, isolation, and cross-cloud workload identity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide outlines baseline security controls, threat mitigations, and implementation standards for deploying autonomous agents in production environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23] Maintained by the Security & Privacy Working Group ([`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) in collaboration with the Identity & Trust Working Group ([`../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)), the guide specifies controls for credential handling, sandbox isolation, and identity boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# Architecture / Specification
While initial guidance defines a 1-hour cloud default for single-cloud IAM role scopes, cross-environment deployments introduce critical workload identity requirements:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Identity Federation**: Recommending OpenID Connect (OIDC)-based federation patterns to enable agents running in one cloud to authenticate against services in another cloud or on-premises infrastructure without static credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Cross-Cloud Role Assumption**: Defining least-privilege role assumption paths when an agent workload must navigate multiple distinct IAM trust domains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Token Lifetime and Rotation**: Evaluating whether default 1-hour token lifetimes should be lowered or adjusted for autonomous multi-cloud agents to limit exposure windows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Blast Radius and Trust Domains**: Establishing guardrails against privilege escalation and lateral movement across identity chains spanning multiple cloud providers and hybrid infrastructure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# Lifecycle History
Workload identity recommendations are actively being expanded from single-cloud baselines into unified guidance covering hybrid, multi-cloud, and federated agent-to-agent architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Technical Committee (TC) is the governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation, responsible for overseeing technical standards, best practices, foundation-wide technical vision, working group lifecycle, and project intake [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]. The founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for a term spanning March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification
## Membership and Leadership
The Technical Committee is led by Chair David Soria Parra (Anthropic) and Co-Chair Caitie McCaffrey (Microsoft) [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]. Its appointed members include:
- Alan Blount (Google)
- Bradley Axen (Block)
- James Ward (Amazon Web Services)
- Nick Cooper (OpenAI)
- Sambhav Kothari (Bloomberg)
- Steve Faulkner (Cloudflare) [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]

## Project Lifecycle Oversight
The TC oversees foundation projects across their lifecycle stages as defined in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md). Current Impact Stage projects under TC oversight include:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Open protocol enabling integration between LLM applications and external data sources or tools [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].
- **goose**: Open-source, extensible AI agent runtime operating across LLMs to install, execute, edit, and test workflows [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].
- **AGENTS.MD**: Standardized context and instruction specification for AI coding agents and development workflows [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Lifecycle History
The TC charter and initial roster were formally established following foundation launch, with all founding members appointed by the Governing Board for the initial 2026 operating term [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, deterministic gates, and constrained external effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is an AAIF reference architecture designed to resolve a single, bounded operational problem autonomously without requiring human approval for every internal iteration, while enforcing strict execution limits and deterministic acceptance gates prior to applying external effects [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It serves as a companion architecture to [Single-Agent Human-Approved Operation](./single-agent-human-approval.md), allowing autonomous iteration only where independent acceptance evidence is available and the external effect is constrained and reversible [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
## Pattern Composition
The architecture composes three core workflow patterns:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Manages bounded retries, iteration budgets, and safe termination upon repeated failures or budget exhaustion [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Independently checks candidate output using test suites, schemas, policy checks, or linters before permitting any effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Physically separates candidate solution formulation from privileged execution, preventing the agent from directly enacting side effects on authoritative systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Architectural Guarantees
The architecture provides four mandatory operational guarantees [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
1. **Bounded Autonomy**: The agent receives strictly bounded scope, allowed tools, data, credentials, and compute budget declared for the specific run.
2. **Independent Acceptance**: A deterministic acceptance gate evaluates candidate results; the model cannot self-certify its own success.
3. **Controlled Effect**: Only the verified, accepted candidate payload is transmitted to the constrained effect executor.
4. **Safe Non-Convergence**: If the convergence budget is exhausted, evidence remains ambiguous, or scope errors occur, execution halts cleanly into recorded audit logs and escalates to human-managed queues.

## Required Capabilities
Implementation requires eight distinct architectural capability roles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- **Execution Engine**: Admits tasks, drives state transitions, manages retries, and records final exit states.
- **Bounded Agent Environment**: Executes the model reasoning and tool-calling loop within least-privilege boundaries.
- **Isolated / Non-Authoritative Work Area**: Scratchpad workspace (e.g., branch, container, sandbox) where candidate modifications occur without affecting production.
- **Deterministic Acceptance Gate**: Verifies compliance against test suites, contracts, schemas, or reconciliation invariants.
- **State and Context Store**: Persists run progress, attempt count, and intermediate evidence across cycles.
- **Constrained Effect Executor**: Dedicated executor authorized to dispatch only the verified action (e.g., opening a PR or updating a ticket draft).
- **Audit Log**: Immutable trace recording prompts, outputs, gate findings, and executor responses.
- **Escalation Surface**: Human-facing interface receiving unresolvable, non-converged, or aborted runs.

## Exit States
Execution concludes in one of four mutually exclusive terminal exit states [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- `Accepted and Applied`: The candidate passed deterministic validation, and the constrained effect succeeded.
- `Budget Exhausted`: Convergence loop iterations or resource limits were reached without passing the gate, triggering clean handoff to escalation.
- `Scope or Policy Violation`: The agent attempted out-of-scope actions or violated security invariants, triggering immediate isolation.
- `Execution Failure`: Unrecoverable infrastructure or environment error logged for engineering remediation.

# Lifecycle History
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture was developed within the AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group as part of the job-oriented reference architecture portfolio [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation criteria and procedures for validating that an AAIF reference architecture matches real-world agentic workflow use cases.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide establishes the standard procedure for evaluating whether an AAIF Reference Architecture (RA) accurately fits a real-world use case documented in the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. The validation process ensures that reference architectures map directly to recognizable practitioner jobs while clarifying boundaries, capability requirements, and failure modes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Architecture / Specification
## Purpose of Validation
Validation assesses whether an RA addresses the core job and primary boundary of a given use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. A designation of `Validated` confirms architectural fit; it does not require that an existing production implementation already complies with every secondary technical control (such as specific retry settings, storage backends, or credential hashing) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Validation Procedure
Validating an RA against a real use case proceeds in three steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]:
1. **Analyze Purpose and Boundaries**: Review the RA's job statement, boundaries, checklist, guarantees, and terminal exit states.
2. **Evaluate Use Case Evidence**: Compare against documented evidence in the Use Case Inventory:
   - Does the RA solve the primary practitioner job?
   - Are actor roles clearly separated across agent, workflow engine, human reviewer, and external systems?
   - Does the use case possess the defining boundary mandated by the RA?
   - Does the RA address the critical failure, wait, retry, recovery, or escalation paths?
3. **Formulate Verification Checks**: Construct two to three simple evaluation checks focused on the core job and defining boundaries, recording unambiguous `Yes`, `No`, or `Unknown` determinations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Distinction Between Architectural Patterns, Reference Architectures, and Scenarios
Contributors must adhere to the structural boundaries established by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:
- **Patterns**: Solve a single, recurring workflow problem independently (e.g., [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md), [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)).
- **Reference Architectures**: Comprehensive blueprints addressing complete practitioner jobs, composing multiple patterns, capability roles, boundaries, and exit states (e.g., [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)).
- **Scenarios**: Concrete or illustrative domain examples used to validate an architecture; a scenario cannot serve as an architecture name [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Lifecycle History
Authored under the AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to accompany the reference architecture templates and contributing guidelines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4, ^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry specification and OpenTelemetry semantic mapping framework standardizing session-level execution traces, turn lifecycles, and action-observation relationships.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an AAIF telemetry specification establishing standard representations and OpenTelemetry semantic convention crosswalks for agentic interactions across conversation sessions, individual turns, proposed actions, approvals, and tool observations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model resolves telemetry gaps where non-executed or rejected proposals fail to appear in traditional tool execution spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification
## Identity and Relationship Contract
The trace model formalizes relationships across five core entity scopes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:
- **Conversation / Session Scope**: Encompasses the entire multi-turn interaction across time, providing a consistent correlation identifier across discrete turns and execution traces.
- **Turn Scope**: Captures an individual conversational exchange or step. Sequential turns within a single conversation may be traced independently while preserving parent conversation context.
- **Proposed Actions**: Distinct entities representing an agent's intent (e.g., proposing to execute an external command or update a record).
- **Approval Checkpoints**: Verification records referencing proposed actions; approvals can record denials or approvals even when no subsequent execution occurs.
- **Observations / Tool Invocations**: Execution spans and result payloads resulting from accepted and executed tool calls.

## Decoupled Approval and Execution Semantics
Conventional tracing models only emit spans when a tool or API is invoked. The Agent Behavior Trace Model decouples intent from invocation: an agent can propose an action (e.g., ticket creation or shell execution), and an approval or denial gate attaches directly to that proposal identity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. If human or policy approval is denied, the proposal and rejection remain fully traceable in the session graph without requiring or fabricating an execution span [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

## OpenTelemetry Crosswalk
The specification maps these agent concepts onto emerging OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, establishing conventions for standalone turn traces, durable wait spans, and interrupted or resumed dialogues [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History
The contract is defined under Task 3 of the nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan initiated in August 2026 within the AAIF Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, safety envelopes, and deterministic acceptance gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Bounded Autonomous Remediation is an architectural reference pattern defined by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group that governs iterative, automated resolution of infrastructure and application faults within strictly defined resource, execution, and policy limits.

Autonomous agents operating under this pattern run within predefined constraints, leveraging localized diagnosis, change execution, and deterministic validation loops while deferring irreversible or high-risk actions across human approval checkpoints [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# Architecture / Specification

Remediation loops evaluate proposed candidate remediations through a unified acceptance gate mechanism:

- **Safety Boundaries and Convergence**: Remediations operate under bounded convergence budgets, constraining iteration counts, allowed tool APIs, and resource consumption.
- **Unified Acceptance Gate**: The architecture consolidates multi-stage verification into a single acceptance gate where all operational and safety criteria must pass conjunctive evaluation (AND-logic), superseding bifurcated "small gate / big gate" evaluation tiers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
- **Validated Scenarios**: The architecture formally validates autonomous maintenance runs, ensuring scheduled or reactive system maintenance tasks conform to hard constraint checks before deploying changes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37]. Illustrative scenarios include automated staff schedule generation subjected to invariant constraints and maintenance validations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# Lifecycle History

The pattern was established by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group and subsequently updated in PR#37 to incorporate detailed maintenance run validations and replace multi-tiered gating terminology with unified acceptance gate criteria [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# References

- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question evaluation instrument measuring production deployment stages, failure factors, human checking, and operational consequences in agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Survey is a platform-neutral, 16-question empirical instrument developed by the Accuracy & Reliability Working Group to collect firsthand operational data on agentic AI deployments in production and serious pilot environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

The instrument establishes standardized response formats and focal-system anchoring to assess deployment maturity, verification mechanisms, failure frequency, and industry remediation priorities [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Architecture / Specification

The survey specification defines five standardized response formats and groups questions across five core analytical areas [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:

- **Response Formats**: Implements single-select, multi-select, single-response Likert matrices, and conditional inline text entries.
- **Eligibility and Real-World Use (Q1)**: Filters respondents based on active operational exposure within the preceding six months. Stages include serious pilot, limited deployment, broad deployment, paused/retired, or uncertain real-world use. Secondhand knowledge and prototype/generic research triggers an early-exit branch [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **System Profile (Q2–Q5)**: Anchors all subsequent answers to a single focal system, capturing practitioner activities (configuration, testing, monitoring, review, decision-making), primary functional domains, architectural structures, and organizational scale [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Operational Dynamics (Q6–Q8)**: Measures environmental constraints, reliance on human checking, and primary realized benefits [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13)**: Documents the frequency of unacceptable outputs, driving causal factors, detection timing relative to impact, severest consequences, and primary verification evidence sources [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Industry Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Gathers cross-ecosystem priorities for open technical standards, preferred delivery resources, and qualitative community feedback [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Lifecycle History

Developed as an official deliverable by the Accuracy & Reliability Working Group in `deliverables/arwg-survey.md` [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# References

- [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)
- [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, SKOS-Lite vocabularies, and conceptual mappings across foundation working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for aligning definitions, taxonomies, and conceptual boundaries across all AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

Operating as a shared workstream rather than a standalone Working Group, it relies on nominated Domain Editors from each technical working group to coordinate vocabulary proposals and maintain conceptual consistency across the foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates according to specific intake, operational, and schema policies:

- **Contribution Scope**: The workstream is strictly restricted to Taxonomy development; Landscape submissions are deferred on the future roadmap, and pull requests altering the Landscape are closed pending approved intake processes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].
- **Domain Editor Representation**: Each working group designates Domain Editors (representing Accuracy & Reliability, Agentic Commerce, Governance/Risk/Regulatory, Identity & Trust, Observability & Traceability, Security & Privacy, and Workflows & Process Integration) to review candidate terms and ensure proper domain ownership [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- **Terminology Lifecycle**: Concepts are tracked in a centralized spreadsheet through three triage states: `Debate` (under evaluation), `Keep` (admitted for definition), or `Cull` (rejected as non-differentiated general terminology) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- **SKOS-Lite Schema Rules**: Taxonomy definitions in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` enforce sentence-case keys and explicit cross-references [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]. During initial flat check-in, the fields `category`, `broaderTerm`, and `definition` are deferred (`""`, `null`, and placeholder respectively) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]. The value `"Universal"` is disallowed in the `workgroups` array; universal terms carry an empty array `[]` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- **Local Preview Tooling**: The portal runs as a zero-dependency client application serving the Taxonomy Explorer on local HTTP servers for link and JavaScript validation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

# Lifecycle History

Established as a foundational AAIF cross-group initiative. In 2026, the workstream adopted the flat initial intake policy, ratified the Domain Editor roster, and enacted the temporary freeze on landscape contributions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

# References

- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Taxonomy Contributions Skill](../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md)
- [Taxonomy Landscape Meeting Notes](../guidelines/taxonomy-landscape-meeting-notes.md)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, horizontal vocabulary harmonization, and ecosystem mapping across technical working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), connecting all vertical Technical Working Groups to harmonize agentic AI terminology and maintain a unified shared vocabulary [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. While its charter encompasses both a living taxonomy and a CNCF-style ecosystem market map, the workstream operates under an active scope restriction focusing exclusively on the shared taxonomy, deferring landscape contributions until formal review processes are ratified [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

The workstream is chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), appointed by the AAIF Technical Working Group chairs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates under foundational architectural guardrails designed to respect domain sovereignty across technical working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]:

- **Horizontal Index Principle**: The workstream prioritizes consolidation over creation, ingesting and standardizing glossaries produced by vertical working groups rather than authoring domain payloads from scratch [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. In-scope shared terms must affect two or more working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Specialized whitepapers, wire protocols, and domain schemas belong strictly to owning working group repositories [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Guardrails**: Concept deletions or folding look-alike terms into aliases strictly requires written sign-off from the owning working group's Domain Editor, ensuring distinct operational concepts (such as deterministic vs. agentic workflows) remain differentiated [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Scope Phasing**: Pull requests altering the ecosystem landscape (`landscape.yml`) are held closed until formal review procedures are established; active development is constrained to `taxonomy-data.js` and the interactive dashboard [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

### Key Performance Indicators

The workstream evaluates ecosystem health through automated metrics [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]:
1. **Citation Utility**: Automated indexing of taxonomy terms cited across AAIF technical specifications, tracking defined-but-never-cited terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
2. **Vendor-Neutral Balance**: Maintaining corporate contribution parity where no single entity authors over 50% of merged entries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
3. **Ecosystem Coverage**: Ensuring every active AAIF working group maintains at least 10 actively reviewed taxonomy entries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
4. **Arbitration Velocity**: Resolving cross-group terminology conflicts within a quarterly release window [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Lifecycle History

- **Weekly Meetings**: Convenes Mondays at 8:30 AM PT via LFX platform meetings [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].
- **Landscape Scope Deferral**: Workstream consensus restricted intake strictly to taxonomy curation while landscape governance and review pathways are prepared [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contribution and Review Protocols
proposed_concept.description: Contributor guidelines and automated agent protocols enforcing horizontal indexing, paired contrast disambiguation, and anti-erasure review rules in ws-taxonomy-landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The taxonomy contributions protocol provides procedural and automated review rules for contributors and agents submitting terminology to the AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. It codifies ingestion criteria, semantic linking standards, and anti-erasure safeguards governing candidate additions to the shared vocabulary [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification

Agents and contributors operating in the repository must enforce four operational gates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]:

### 1. Landscape Boundary Enforcement
Until formal review procedures are ratified, all contributions affecting `landscape.yml` or the ecosystem map are automatically blocked; PRs attempting to add or modify landscape entries must be closed [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

### 2. Horizontal Indexing
New terms are evaluated against the horizontal boundary:
- **In-Scope**: Shared foundational concepts, cross-cutting primitives, or taxonomies affecting two or more working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Out-of-Scope**: Domain-specific implementation schemas, single-group internal helper variables, and wire protocols, which must remain in vertical working group repositories [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

### 3. Paired Contrast Disambiguation Protocol
When adjacent or look-alike terms intersect (such as [Tool](../taxonomy/tool.md) vs. [Skill](../taxonomy/skill.md)):
- Concept pairs must not be collapsed into an ambiguous shared `scopeNote` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- Definitions must explicitly document counterpart boundaries stating precisely how the term differs from its adjacent peer [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- Entries must be programmatically linked via `relatedTerms` (`skos:related`) or `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

### 4. Anti-Erasure Sign-Off
Look-alike terms reflecting distinct operational models must not be merged into aliases or deleted without explicit written authorization from the owning working group's Domain Editor [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations and Chapter Sync Automation
proposed_concept.description: Automation tooling and reconciliation engines managing AAIF chapter provisioning, multi-tenant Slack and Google Drive ACL synchronization, and chapter asset generation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Community event operations encompasses the CLI engines, synchronization scripts, and review pipelines that maintain AAIF local chapters across Slack channels, Google Drive asset trees, and attendee CRM records [^evt-community-events-pr-44][^evt-community-events-pr-42]. The automation enforces strict separation between intake identities and authenticated account identifiers to prevent permissions leakage and misdirected administrative access [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Architecture / Specification

The automation suite operates across several core synchronization components:

### Tri-Column Identity Resolution
Organizer identities across AAIF systems are resolved across three decoupled fields on intake records rather than collapsed into a single email address [^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- `Slack ID`: The immutable `U…` account identifier, ensuring invitations never key off mutable `@handle` display names [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Slack Email`: The email registered to the Slack account, resolved using `users.lookupByEmail` with domain-limited dot-folding for consumer `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` addresses [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Drive Email`: The explicit address granted ACL access on the chapter Drive folder, defaulting to a visible `(no grant)` sentinel when unassigned [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

Automated runs write only verified email matches; name-based matching generates proposals held for manual review to avoid false-positive account collisions [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

### Chapter Channel Provisioning and Seeding
Chapter Slack workspaces are synchronized via `provision_channels.py` under the following operational rules:
- **Ops Staff Seeding**: Chapter organizer channels automatically seed operations accounts resolved from external configuration lists (`Ops staff email` and `Ops staff domain`), preventing automated accounts from triggering anomalous unreviewed admin alerts [^evt-community-events-pr-44][^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Private Drive Folder Linking**: Organizer channels post direct links to chapter Drive storage containing budgets and CRMs, avoiding public room leaks [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Idempotency and Permissive Scoping**: Message publication enforces unconditional history verification rather than relying on pin status [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Channel renaming requires explicit mapping in `CHANNEL_RENAMES` to maintain persistent channel identifiers [^evt-community-events-pr-43].

### Chapter Asset and Badge Pipelines
Chapter badges are maintained in per-chapter `Badges/` subfolders within each chapter's Drive folder [^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Chapter agent badges are generated via `make_agent_badge.py` by compiling embedded Instrument Sans typography, deterministic per-chapter palette tokens from `design/aaif-tokens.css`, and chapter mascots, rendered into SVG and PNG assets using headless Chrome [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Automation tooling and reconciliation engines managing AAIF chapter provisioning, multi-tenant Slack workspaces, CRM spreadsheets, and Drive permissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Event Operations skill governs the automated provisioning, synchronisation, and audit reconciliation of chapter infrastructure across Google Drive, Google Sheets CRMs, and Slack workspaces.

The automation suite reconciles participant state across central intake forms, regional organizer permissions, and public communication channels without manual intervention, while upholding strict least-privilege access and idempotent execution invariants [^evt-community-events-pr-28] [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

### CRM Lifecycle and Role Decoupling

Chapter relationship management spreadsheets decouple intake applicant intent from administrative lifecycle state across two independent columns [^evt-community-events-pr-28]:
- `Status`: Records administrative triage decisions (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Attended`, `Regular`, `Volunteer`, and `Declined`). Role labels are prohibited from entering this cell.
- `Interested in`: Captures submitted applicant interests (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`, delimited by `/`), preserving applicant intent invariant under subsequent status transitions.

The synchronisation engine (`sync_crm`) unmasks previously withheld applicant profile attributes (`LinkedIn URL`, `Company`, `Role / title`, and `Technical expertise`) for authenticated chapter organizers and enforces pre-split schema validation, routing legacy sheets to `migrate_interested_in.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-28].

### Slack Workspace and Country Channel Routing

Slack channel orchestration automates chapter and regional communication channels:
- **Country-Scope Invites**: `invite_organizers.py` supports `--scope {organizer,country,both}`, resolving accounts across multi-chapter regional jurisdictions to eliminate duplicate invites [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Additive Directory Posts**: `post_country_directory.py` publishes and appends local chapter links to designated country channels while strictly avoiding `chat.update` calls to prevent overwriting existing human-authored content [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Audit Categorisation**: `summarize_audits.py` decouples genuine channel invitation deficits (`gaps`) from participants lacking registered Slack accounts (`no_account`), preventing distorted metrics during intake audits [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Channel Name Overrides**: `sync_resources.py` consults `COUNTRY_CHANNELS` overrides to preserve non-standard room mappings (e.g., `#deutschland`, `#nordics`, `#brasil`) [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

### Drive Permission and Identity Routing

Drive permission synchronisation decouples intake contact records from Google Workspace identity assertions [^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
- **Drive Email Fallbacks**: `sync_access` respects the `Drive Email` column when an accepted organizer's intake email lacks an active Google account, eliminating aborted lock sweeps.
- **Luma Decoupling**: Chapter catalog generation treats Luma registration links as an opt-in precondition (`--require-luma`) backed by global status validation (`--audit-luma`), preventing external page registration latency from stalling chapter onboarding [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

### OOXML Storage Optimisation

Document synchronisation enforces the `ox.NEVER_EMBED` rule: fonts natively rendered in Google Docs (such as Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono) are declared in `word/fontTable.xml` but stripped from embedded binary payloads (`word/fonts/`), leaving only metric fallbacks (Manrope) embedded and reducing file sizes across the chapter estate [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #28**: Separated CRM lifecycle decisions from applicant roles into distinct `Status` and `Interested in` fields, surfaced previously masked profile details, and migrated spreadsheet conditional formatting [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **PR #34**: Enacted `ox.NEVER_EMBED` to declare mono fonts without binary embedding, shrinking OOXML document footprints across Google Drive [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **PR #36**: Introduced country channel invite scoping, additive chapter directory publishing, and `no_account` triage separation in Slack audits [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **PR #45**: Resolved Drive permission failures via `Drive Email` overrides and decoupled chapter row additions from Luma URL creation [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
