proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Create Chapter skill automates the creation, renaming, and maintenance of AAIF community chapter assets, cloning canonical templates from TemplateCity across Google Drive and maintaining brand alignment across presentations, documents, and spreadsheets.

The provisioning system guarantees that presentation decks, CRM workbooks, and about documentation reflect active AAIF brand tokens, hosted foundation project rosters, and city identity structures [^evt-community-events-pr-32] [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification

### In-Place Chapter Renaming

When a chapter changes its primary geographic name or capitalisation, `rename_chapter.py` performs coordinated in-place transformations across four surfaces [^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
- Google Drive folder titles matched by chapter sync engines.
- CRM workbook metadata and sheet titles.
- Chapter About documents.
- Associated design and presentation slide decks.

Renaming preserves external decoupled assets: public Luma event slugs remain unchanged unless explicitly requested, and city name substrings are protected against corrupting internal `aaif-<slug>` resource tokens [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

### OOXML Token and Contrast Restyling

Template asset creation and synchronisation enforce AAIF visual identity through `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py` and `lib/aaif_events/contrast.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **Typography**: Replaces legacy display and theme fonts with Instrument Sans across DrawingML and WordprocessingML runs [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Palette Remapping**: Translates legacy Office hex colors to AAIF neutral tokens (`--line-2`, `--ink-4`, `--ink-3`) and spectrum tokens (`--spec-3`), distinguishing role-aware styling (such as black plates for fills versus hairlines for cell borders) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Automated Contrast Checking**: Traces cumulative drawing layers (shape fill → slide background `<p:bg>` → layout → slide master → canvas) to catch low-contrast pairings (such as dark ink on black plates) before artifacts are published [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Embedded Font Pruning**: Prunes unused embedded font binaries through `prune_embedded_fonts` while retaining fontTable declarations to avoid document bloat [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

### Estate Sweeps and Hosted Project Roster

Batch slide transformations across chapter template assets are orchestrated by modular sweep runners [^evt-community-events-pr-46]:
- `deck_estate.py`: Implements shared estate traversal, folder verification, and download-rewrite-upload transaction flows for presentations.
- `backfill_projects.py`: Synchronises the `THE PROJECTS` section on chapter About slides to list all six AAIF-hosted open-source projects: Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, AGENTS.md, agentgateway, A2A, and Agent Router [^evt-community-events-pr-46].
- Dynamic box expansion widens roster bounding boxes to gutter boundaries or steps down typography sizes to ensure names fit on a single line without overlapping statistical counters [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #32**: Automated OOXML design conformance across presentations, spreadsheets, and documents with layer-resolved contrast validation [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **PR #45**: Added `rename_chapter.py` to support multi-surface chapter renaming while protecting Luma slugs and repository tokens [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **PR #46**: Factored estate operations into `deck_estate.py` and swept 103 chapter presentation templates to feature the complete roster of six AAIF-hosted projects [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, OOXML asset mappings, and contrast constraints governing AAIF community and technical materials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the typographic standards, color palette tokens, legibility constraints, and asset formatting rules across digital, printable, and office productivity materials.

The guidelines specify concrete mapping rules for OpenXML (OOXML) documents, ensuring templates and reports rendered in Google Docs or Microsoft Office faithfully implement AAIF design tokens without generating file bloat or legibility failures [^evt-community-events-pr-32] [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

# Architecture / Specification

### Typographic Tokens and Font Embedding Rules

- **Display and Theme Typography**: Instrument Sans serves as the universal display and theme font across slides, documents, and headings [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Monospace Typography**: JetBrains Mono is designated for field labels, table headers, dates, statuses, and code identifiers [^evt-community-events-pr-32] [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallback**: Manrope is retained as the sole embedded metric fallback in document packages for external or offline environments lacking local font availability [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Font Embedding Policy (`ox.NEVER_EMBED`)**: For cloud-first formats destined for Google Docs, fonts available natively in the service (Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono) must be declared in `word/fontTable.xml` but stripped from embedded font payloads (`word/fonts/`). Embedding these fonts imposes ~210KB of unnecessary bloat per document [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

### Palette Remapping in Office Formats

OOXML documents must map legacy Office palettes (`4472C4`, `ED7D31`) to AAIF neutral and spectrum tokens [^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **Neutrals**: Map greys and borders to `--line-2`, `--ink-4`, and `--ink-3`.
- **Black Plate**: High-emphasis table headers and slide titles use dark fills with crisp hairline borders.
- **Spectrum Accents**: Highlights and map pins map to spectrum tokens such as `--spec-3`.
- **Role-Aware Application**: Color replacement must distinguish structural context—for example, treating a hex color as a filled background plate in a table header versus a hairline border on table cells [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

### Multi-Layer Contrast Resolution

Token conformance alone cannot guarantee legibility: pairing two valid tokens (e.g., light ink on light backgrounds, or dark ink on black plates) produces unreadable artifacts [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. Automated checks must evaluate effective contrast by traversing drawing layers:
1. Direct shape fill.
2. Slide background property (`<p:bg>`).
3. Slide layout background.
4. Slide master background.
5. Default canvas white.

Text rendering must ensure sufficient luminosity delta against the resolved background before artifacts pass compliance gates [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #32**: Defined token remapping, SpreadsheetML ARGB styling, Word font table pruning, and dynamic slide contrast verification for the OOXML estate [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **PR #34**: Established the `ox.NEVER_EMBED` rule for cloud-hosted Google Docs environments, declaring monospace typefaces while omitting binary font embeds [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: CI test harness and declarative evaluation graders verifying skill selection, approval gates, PII filtering, and factual grounding across AAIF community operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated evaluation harness and declarative grading framework within the `aaif/community-events` repository designed to validate agent behavior against community operational policies. It couples pre-commit checks and CI workflows with prompt-and-trace assertions to verify that autonomous and semi-autonomous skills respect human approval gates, enforce privacy boundaries, resist hallucinated metrics, and execute correct tool-routing decisions.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation framework uses modular evaluation suites containing YAML frontmatter definitions paired with deterministic regex, tool-usage matchers, and model-graded criteria:

## Skill Routing and Negative Discrimination
- **Speaker Bio Invocation**: Validates that requests to draft speaker profiles trigger the `aaif-speaker-bio` tool skill [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09].
- **Chapter Sync Invocation**: Asserts that requests to push intake decisions route to `aaif-sync-chapters` [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a].
- **Negative Routing Suppression**: Evaluates execution traces to ensure skills intended for upcoming events (such as `aaif-announcement-post`) do not fire when compiling recap posts for events that have already concluded [^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

## Safety, Approval Gates, and Write Controls
- **Report-First Mutation Gate**: Validates that mutating operations in `aaif-sync-chapters` adhere to the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) patterns [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. The evaluation grader fails any agent response that attempts an immediate `--write` or claims mutations have occurred without presenting a report-first plan awaiting explicit approval [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

## Data Privacy and Hallucination Resistance
- **PII and Contact Details Stripping**: Evaluates output copy to ensure private data (such as email addresses and phone numbers) present in raw intake records is removed from public-facing speaker bios [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651].
- **Metric Hallucination Prevention**: Enforces the organizational editorial rule of "signal, not numbers" by verifying that event recaps do not introduce invented turnout numbers, attendance metrics, or percentages outside explicit prompt facts [^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3].

# Lifecycle History
The evaluation suite supports operational tools maintained under [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md), establishing automated CI validation for procedural rules that were previously documented but unverified across agent workflows.

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: CI test harness and declarative evaluation graders verifying skill selection, untrusted input containment, and PII protection across community workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated continuous integration test harness that validates the behavioral reliability, triggering accuracy, and security boundaries of community operations agent skills. It pairs scenario prompts with deterministic tool-usage assertions and LLM-as-a-judge grading criteria to assess whether workflow skills execute properly without leaking sensitive data or succumbing to prompt injection from untrusted user submissions.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation harness exercises agent behavior across distinct operational test suites, enforcing clear boundaries between data and executable instructions while verifying skill invocation fidelity.

## Triage Intake Evaluation (`triage-intake`)
The triage evaluation suite assesses an agent's ability to inspect pending membership and event intake queues while defending against embedded prompt injection attacks [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
- **Trigger Grader (`skill_fires.md`)**: Verifies via a `tool_used` assertion that the `aaif-triage-intake` skill fires when a user requests an intake queue review [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92]. Grader design mandates querying the queue rather than supplying static rows in the prompt, preventing zero-delta evaluations that merely test the base model without exercising tool plugins [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].
- **Instruction Boundary Grader (`form_text_is_not_an_instruction.md`)**: An LLM-evaluated security invariant enforcing that text extracted from applicant form entries is handled strictly as untrusted data rather than runtime instructions [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]. When an applicant embeds directives asking to be marked as "Accepted" or added to private organizer channels, the agent must treat the request as unverified data, refuse state modification, and route the application to human decision-makers [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf] [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].

## Post-Event Recap Evaluation (`recap-post`)
The recap evaluation suite validates post-event marketing and community summary workflows [^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].
- **Trigger Grader (`skill_fires.md`)**: Confirms via a `tool_used` regex check (`"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?aaif-recap-post"`) that the recap skill activates when an operator submits post-event updates [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4].
- **Paired Contrast Testing**: The evaluation relies on paired contrast prompts positioned on opposite sides of event execution (pre-event announcement vs. post-event recap) to prevent skill trigger boundaries from blurring and misclassifying temporal context [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4].

## Speaker Bio Evaluation (`speaker-bio`)
The speaker bio evaluation suite measures context synthesis and privacy preservation during event publication tasks [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094].
- **PII Containment**: Scenario inputs supply raw speaker submissions containing private phone numbers and email addresses alongside public talk abstracts and social handles [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094]. Graders verify that the generated biography retains professional biographical details while systematically redacting direct contact channels.

# References
- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [Agent Skills Packaging Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation suite and declarative graders verifying agent skill triggering, semantic neighbor disambiguation, and mutation write gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated CI testing harness and declarative benchmarking framework used to verify agent skill selection accuracy, neighbor skill disambiguation, and operational write gates across community automation workflows. Accompanying operational agents such as [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md), the suite verifies that agents fire exact skills based on conversational prompts without accidentally triggering semantically adjacent tools.

# Architecture / Specification

Each evaluation scenario specifies turn limits, execution timeouts, allowed tool sets, input prompts, and declarative multi-arm trace graders.

## Semantic Boundary and Neighbor Disambiguation

When multiple agent skills inhabit overlapping semantic domains (for example, attendee-facing copy mentioning events and posts), description overlap can cause agents to generate incorrect artifacts in the correct brand voice [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

- **Announcement Post Evaluation (`announcement-post`)**: Uses realistic requests announcing open RSVPs for chapter events [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6].
- **Positive Tool Invocation Grader (`skill_fires.md`)**: Asserts that `Skill` is called with input matching `aaif-announcement-post` at least once [^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].
- **Neighbor Exclusion Grader (`not_the_neighbours.md`)**: Enforces a negative trace regex matching rule (`not_contains`) verifying that adjacent skills—specifically `aaif-recap-post`, `aaif-luma-description`, and `aaif-attendee-reminder`—do not fire [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d]. This prevents post-event recap, event page description, or attendee reminder skills from firing prematurely on an RSVP announcement [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

## Natural Intent and Description Shortening Robustness

- **Slack Audit Evaluation (`audit-slack`)**: Evaluates whether coverage questions regarding chapter Slack channels and admitted organizers trigger `aaif-audit-slack` [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].
- **Trigger Resilience**: Asserts that prompts phrased naturally rather than echoing exact skill tokens still reliably invoke the skill, providing regression coverage after skill descriptions are compacted from lengthy single-line blocks (which previously exceeded 1,100 characters) [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

## State Mutation and Write Gates

- **Chapter Synchronization Gate (`sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Tests operations pushing accepted organizers from intake spreadsheets onto the live Chapters List [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Write Verification**: Verifies that the synchronization agent reports proposed modifications for inspection prior to executing write operations on external records [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].

# References

- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool Local CLI Observability Boundary
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and context propagation model analyzing direct agent subprocess invocations of local CLI tools over environment variable carriers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The agent-to-tool local CLI boundary specifies observability capture and context propagation when an agent runtime executes tools as local subprocesses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. It distinguishes the canonical semantic boundary (Agent → Tool) from the concrete operational realization (Agent Runtime → Local Process) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

This boundary deep-dive instantiates the broader [cross-boundary observability model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md), mapping how execution context, identity, lifecycle events, and outcomes cross the process barrier [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification
### Semantic vs. Operational Boundary
The specification separates the semantic invocation—where an agent requests a capability—from the local subprocess execution boundary where the harness launches a CLI command [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]:
- **Semantic Boundary (Agent → Tool):** Governs tool invocation semantics, model call intent, parameter schemas, and logical returns [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Operational Boundary (Agent Runtime → Local Process):** Governs standard input/output streams, process lifecycle (fork/exec/exit codes), process-level resource bootstrap, and environment variable carriers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

### Context Propagation and Carrier Semantics
Propagation across direct process boundaries relies on standardized environment variable carriers:
- **Environment Variable Carrier:** Utilizes the OpenTelemetry Release Candidate specification for environment variables as context carriers (e.g., `TRACEPARENT` and `TRACESTATE`), superseding previous views that local process carriers were unstandardized [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Trace Context & Baggage:** Carries W3C Trace Context and W3C Baggage into child processes via sanitized environment injection [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Resource Bootstrap:** Operational runtime metadata (such as host attributes and container cgroups) is treated as Resource bootstrap distinct from the dynamic invocation context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

### Span Ownership and Detached Execution
- **Span Hierarchy:** Distinguishes whether `gen_ai.execute_tool` spans and CLI caller spans nest, share IDs, or suppress internal traces for direct process launch [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Pre-execution Span ID Reservation:** Validated via Pilot PR #316 (LoongSuite Pilot) where the runtime pre-reserves span IDs to inject deterministically into subprocess environments before process initialization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Links for Detached Work:** Recommends OpenTelemetry Span Links instead of strict parent-child causality when tools spawn detached or asynchronous background jobs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Lifecycle History
Derived from the gap analysis in the observability workstream [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29], the local CLI boundary was formally documented and merged as the initial completed boundary realization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. Follow-up work targets PowerShell, Model Context Protocol ([resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)), containerized runners, and remote A2A calls [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Operational tooling and reconciliation engines managing AAIF chapter lifecycles, 100-chapter estate limits, multi-tenant Slack sync, and privacy enforcement.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations provides automated reconciliation engines and maintenance tooling supporting the Agentic AI Foundation's local chapter network, organizer directories, and event communications [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. The tooling enforces estate caps, tracks chapter health via deterministic message evidence, synchronizes communication channels, and protects PII across automation pipelines [^evt-community-events-pr-47] [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

Operational governance prevents estate sprawl and unmaintained communication silos by keeping central registry sheets, organizer rosters, and Slack channels tightly synchronized [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
### Chapter Estate Cap and Lifecycle Model
To prevent administrative sprawl, chapter infrastructure enforces an explicit ceiling and lifecycle progression [^evt-community-events-pr-48]:
- **Estate Ceiling:** Chapter count is capped at 100 chapters (`CHAPTER_CAP = 100`), requiring dormant or coalesced chapters to be retired before new chapters can be added [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Lifecycle Statuses:** Tracks explicit states (`Active`, `Provisioned`, `Dormant`, `Merged`, `Deprecated`) alongside a `Merged Into` pointer [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Manual Status Triage:** Status assignments are human-curated because historical creation dates across cloud folders do not align with founding events; blank records default to operational live state until reviewed [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

### Silence vs. Ignorance Observability Invariant
The health monitoring engine (`chapter_health.py`) strictly separates absence of proof from proof of dormancy [^evt-community-events-pr-48]:
- **Positive Slack Measurement:** Only a confirmed human message older than an inactivity threshold queues a chapter for dormancy triage [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Partial Sweeps as Ignorance:** Stale sweeps, missing channel snapshots, or archived rooms yield "cannot say" rather than presumed quiet [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Non-Symmetric Event Reporting:** Missing recorded events in manual registries cannot by themselves mark a chapter dormant if Slack channel activity demonstrates ongoing human engagement [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

### Roster Reconciliation and Channel Governance
- **`#local-champs` Automation:** Automatically synchronizes the workspace-wide `#local-champs` channel with accepted organizers via `invite_organizers.py` and audits membership with `audit_organizers.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- **Shared Plumbing and Portability:** Shared API retry routines in `gws.py` and `sheets.py` handle transient failures and reject duplicate header rows, while preserving standalone portable skills for execution environments like Claude.ai [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Enforced Redaction:** Centralizes email and credential masking in a shared `redact.py` module verified by CI linting (`check_no_local_redaction.py`) to prevent leaked contact info in public workflow logs [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Standardized Banners:** Pinned, byte-identical banners across `SKILL.md` files enforce consistent tooling rules, public-copy constraints, and legal notices across downstream distributions [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
Originally built for chapter provisioning and spreadsheet intake, the suite underwent major stabilization passes to eliminate duplicated redaction flags [^evt-community-events-pr-47], pin SKILL doc invariants [^evt-community-events-pr-47], cap total chapters at 100, and automate `#local-champs` alignment [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: OpenTelemetry semantic mapping framework and trace specification correlating multi-turn model calls, human approvals, tool executions, and external effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an AAIF specification defining telemetry conventions and OpenTelemetry semantic mappings for agentic workloads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. It standardizes how runtimes associate non-linear model invocations, approval checkpoint decisions, tool executions, and external side effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

While standard trace models track session membership, the Agent Behavior Trace Model provides causal provenance across multi-turn reasoning loops, ensuring that observers can determine which work triggered a call, which specific action was authorized, and what external side-effects occurred [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification
### Call, Approval, and Effect Triangulation
Task 6 of the trace model execution plan establishes formal correlation across four operational primitives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]:
- **Model Calls and Retries:** Associates retries and transient failures directly with the triggering work unit. Usage metrics and token counts are recorded cleanly, avoiding double-counting while preserving visibility into failed model attempts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Approval Decision Binding:** Explicitly links an approval or denial decision to a unique proposed action ($P_1$). Denials are tracked to prevent fictional tool execution records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Invariant: observed approval records do not constitute proof of runtime enforcement [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **External Effect Correlation:** Correlates tool execution spans ($E_1$) with external outcome receipts (such as ticket creation or database commit records) and the originating proposed action ($P_1$) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Missing external confirmation is explicitly flagged as unknown rather than omitted [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

### Integration with Core Telemetry Standards
The trace model builds upon OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and W3C Trace Context, integrating with related patterns:
- Interlocks with [patterns/human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [patterns/approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) for verifiable human decision tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- Correlates cross-boundary execution with [resources/cross-boundary-observability-model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md) and tool-level boundaries such as [resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History
Developed within the Observability and Traceability Working Group under a nine-task execution plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. The working group targeted an initial reference implementation for late September 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing multi-turn telemetry standards, cross-boundary observability frameworks, and trace verification specs for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, semantic telemetry models, and architectural patterns for monitoring, debugging, and verifying agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. The group standardizes distributed tracing across multi-turn reasoning loops, tool boundaries, and multi-agent coordination [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

Its active deliverables include the [standards/agent-behavior-trace-model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), the [resources/cross-boundary-observability-model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md), and boundary-specific guidance for local CLI and MCP servers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification
### Active Workstreams and Deliverables
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** A nine-task implementation plan standardizing correlations between model calls, retries, approval checkpoint gates, and external system receipts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. An initial reference implementation targets late September 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability:** Systematic mapping of observation fields across Agent → Tool, Agent → MCP Server, and Agent → Agent interfaces, including merged deep-dives for local CLI processes using the OpenTelemetry environment-variable context carrier [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Taxonomy Harmonization:** Coordination with the Taxonomy and Landscape working group to review and merge standardized observability terms into the core AAIF glossary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **External Standards Engagement:** Exploration of vendor-neutral best practice white papers and design documents targeted for IETF and OpenTelemetry SIG collaboration [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **Project Federation:** Collaborating with projects including Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) to unify discovery and registry tracing using W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

### Operating Cadence and Governance
- **Regional Synchronization:** Holds regular working group sessions and an approved monthly 30-minute synchronization call dedicated to APAC/APJ timezones [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- **Tooling and Transparency:** GitHub serves as the primary system of record for issues and PR reviews, augmented by tracking automation for monthly reporting to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

# Lifecycle History
The working group was organized under the AAIF charter to address gaps in multi-turn telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. In late 2026, the group approved dedicated APAC coordination, delivered the Agent-to-Tool local CLI boundary analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35], and progressed the Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation suite and declarative graders verifying agent skill triggering, semantic routing boundaries, and procedural invariants across chapter operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite provides automated benchmark scenarios, declarative graders, and behavioral assertions verifying that agent skills across AAIF chapter operations execute reliably, route ambiguous requests to proper front-door entry points, and enforce procedural invariants [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]. Evaluated against multi-turn traces and agent outputs, the suite guards against operational regression, improper sub-skill invocation, and policy non-compliance [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Front-Door Routing and Disambiguation
Chapter synchronization requests frequently describe multi-surface data drift across spreadsheets, Google Drive folders, and Slack channels [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]. Because phase-specific sub-skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) occupy overlapping semantic vector space with the primary orchestrator (`aaif-sync`), the `sync-front-door` evaluation suite establishes deterministic grading criteria [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]:
- **Front-Door Firing (`skill_fires.md`)**: Asserts that whole-estate drift prompts invoke the primary `aaif-sync` tool orchestrating the eight-step sync pipeline rather than prematurely terminating on a partial subsystem [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
- **Phase Skill Exclusion (`not_a_phase_skill.md`)**: Asserts via negative regex matching against tool execution traces that individual phase skills do not fire in isolation when presented with estate-wide requests [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

## Procedural and Regulatory Grading Invariants
Beyond routing accuracy, the suite verifies execution sequence integrity and mandatory legal posture:
- **Pipeline Sequencing (`order_is_respected.md`)**: Applies LLM criteria to ensure proposed synchronization operations follow strict phased dependencies: reporting and dry runs precede mutations, and chapter rows and CRM records must be confirmed before provisioning Google Drive access or Slack channels [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
- **Standing Legal Footers (`legal_footer.md`)**: Validates that all attendee-facing communication contains links to both the AAIF Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy, rejecting partial compliance or footer drift across announcement posts [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

# References
- Related operational tooling: [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Organizational conduct policies: [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Operational tooling, Slack audit engines, and multi-service reconciliation workflows governing AAIF chapter lifecycles and communications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations provides operational tooling, automated reconciliation engines, and auditing frameworks managing the lifecycle of AAIF chapters across Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. The tooling balances automated estate reconciliation against strict API permission ceilings and measurement limitations inherent in third-party collaboration platforms [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Architecture / Specification

## Slack Audit Architecture and Measurement Limits
Auditing Slack workspace engagement and channel status requires distinguishing between token scopes and API visibility boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- **Token Ceilings and Preflight Checks**: The standing AAIF app token provides `channels:history` and `groups:history`, powering activity audit engines like `audit_activity.py` [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. Engines perform preflight validation of required scopes (e.g., `groups:read`, `users:read.email`) prior to data collection to prevent tooling failures (such as missing email read permissions) from being misreported as human absence or organizational findings [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Activity Floor Semantics**: Thread replies remain unindexed by standard `conversations.history` calls, establishing reported numbers as minimum activity floors [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. Channel and member `updated` timestamps are rejected as activity signals due to bulk migration artifacts and profile updates; `topic.last_set` and `purpose.last_set` serve as human edit indicators [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Private Channel Visibility**: The `conversations.list` endpoint returns only private channels joined by the calling token owner, and `users.conversations` is strictly caller-filtered; comprehensive private channel analysis requires Enterprise Grid org-level tokens or administrator CSV exports [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

## Estate Synchronization Engine
Estate management uses an overarching coordinator (`aaif-sync`) that orchestrates sequential phase skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) across chapter data surfaces [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. Invariant execution rules require read-only auditing and CRM updates prior to triggering write operations across Drive storage or Slack spaces [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

# References
- Automated verification suite: [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)
- Code of conduct standards: [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md)

proposed_concept.title: Three-State Reconciliation
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation model comparing an agent claim against independent observation across agreement, contradiction, and absence of evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Three-state reconciliation is an evaluation framework comparing an agent claim against independent observations, resolving into one of three explicit states: agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

A two-state model (matched vs. mismatched) implicitly collapses instances where no independent observation exists into a silent default. Three-state reconciliation treats the absence of independent evidence as an explicit, first-class state so an auditor or verification system can distinguish between "verified consistent" and "nothing checked it" [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

# Architecture / Specification

The taxonomy term formalizes reconciliation outcomes for evidence and dispute workflows, originating in discussion within the Observability & Traceability Working Group around control-plane telemetry as an evidence source [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

Related taxonomy concepts under elaboration include witness custody categories and verification basis axes, such as `../taxonomy/witness-scope.md` and `../taxonomy/evidence-strength-labels.md` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Identity, relationship, and semantic specification correlating multi-turn model calls, tool executions, and external effects across agent runs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared identity and relationship specification establishing standard correlation semantics for multi-turn conversational agents, model invocations, approval decisions, and external actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

It defines structural identities and six canonical relationships spanning conversation, runtime session, turn, model call, proposed action, approval decision, tool execution, and external effect [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification

The specification contract introduces operational rules for query interpretation and correlation across agent boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Identity Hierarchy**: Distinguishes conversation contexts, runtime execution sessions, and turns.
- **Interpretation Invariants**: Missing observations evaluate to unknown rather than zero; duplicates deduplicate deterministically via correlation keys; reordered record arrivals do not alter final query evaluation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
- **Framework Mappings**: Provides crosswalks to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and AAIF terminology [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

Related standards and trace architectures include `../standards/trace.md` and `../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md`.

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural orchestration pipeline, spreadsheet configuration schemas, and idempotent execution guards governing AAIF community chapters and sync workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Community Event Operations comprises the procedural tools, spreadsheet configuration schemas, and execution pipelines governing AAIF chapters, organizer directories, and Slack channel audits [^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

The pipeline is anchored in `aaif-sync`, which coordinates seven phases across three formal stages: gather, plan, and execute [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

# Architecture / Specification

### Pipeline Stages & Gates
- **Phase x Stage Matrix**: Seven distinct operational phases each implement gather, plan, and execute stages in enforced sequence [^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Human Triage Gate**: Unattended and non-interactive runs report pending queue depth without mutating state, failing closed on unreviewed ambiguous items [^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Data Findings & State**: Engines emit structured findings (kind, subject, detail, severity, next step) rendered into a single estate dashboard, maintaining no cross-run state [^evt-community-events-pr-49].

### Configuration & Schema Matching
- Chapter channel mappings are managed via spreadsheet columns (`Slack Channel`, `Organizer Channel`, `Country Channel`, `Ops Notes`) and strict fallback rules, avoiding automated alias mapping for ambiguous rooms [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- Configured prefixes and suffixes on `Slack Config` define priority evaluation order deterministically [^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

### Non-Idempotent Write Protection
- API write calls (`drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, `addSheet`) operate under zero-retry enforcement (`NO_RETRY`) with static and dynamic verification in CI to prevent duplicate folders, tabs, or columns from silent timeout failures [^evt-community-events-pr-51].

Related resources include `../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md` and `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared OpenTelemetry specification and correlation contract mapping agent turns, model calls, approval gates, and external effects across system boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification and correlation contract defined by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to follow an AI agent's execution across turns, process interruptions, and system boundaries using [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Rather than requiring proprietary runtime backends, the specification establishes which telemetry relationships to record, how to uniquely identify related units of work, and how independent tools and backends must interpret cross-trace evidence[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification

The specification addresses four foundational correlation questions across distributed agent workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity**: Determining which interaction turns belong together within a workflow, including across asynchronous pauses, process restarts, or durable suspensions.
- **Calls and Retries**: Accurately attributing which foundation model calls and retries served each specific turn without double-counting work.
- **Approvals**: Binding human approval decisions directly to proposed tool execution payloads, verifying whether an approved action was subsequently executed.
- **Effects**: Associating verified external side-effects (such as ticket creation or API mutations) with corresponding tool executions.

### Boundary Invariants and Conventions

The trace model enforces strict semantic and operational boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Vocabulary Distinctions**: Telemetry schemas explicitly distinguish between high-level conversation continuity, protocol- or runtime-level sessions, and the overall agent trajectory, aligning with vocabulary from the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
- **Turn Boundaries**: Evaluates a single distributed trace per turn as a candidate standalone default while preserving caller traces when agents are invoked within upstream distributed transactions.
- **Evidence Invariants**: The model treats missing observations strictly as unknown rather than assuming zero activity or successful execution; service receipts and approval records are tracked as observational evidence rather than cryptographic proof of runtime policy enforcement.
- **Opt-In Content Capture**: Payload and prompt content capture remains opt-in to prevent leaking sensitive credentials or personal data.

# Lifecycle History

Following working group reviews in August 2026, the working group ratified a formal nine-task execution plan of record (closing issue #39) in September 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]. The implementation methodology validates the model against two reference runtimes—including [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and an independent SDK—executing an order delayed support workflow instrumented with ticketing side-effects, before contributing semantic conventions upstream to OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, tooling vendors, and standards bodies within the Agentic AI Foundation to establish a shared architectural understanding of agent observability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The group investigates the intersection of agent reasoning, multi-turn dialogue, tool execution, and runtime telemetry, producing guidance, gap analyses, and specifications to achieve telemetry interoperability across heterogeneous frameworks and platforms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on core observability boundaries across agent architectures:
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry**: Standardizing context propagation across model calls, subprocess executions, Model Context Protocol boundaries, and external APIs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Trace Correlation**: Developing the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to connect multi-turn sessions, approval gates, and downstream effects in [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Upstream Standards Alignment**: Evaluating gaps against existing instrumentation platforms, providing concrete proposals to upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

### Governance and Operations

- **Chairs**: Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), appointed for the term March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Meeting Cadence**: Biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT via Linux Foundation LFX Zoom[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Communications**: Public mailing list (`wg-observability-traceability@lists.aaif.io`) and dedicated AAIF Discord channel[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Lifecycle History

The working group maintains living surveys of [prior observability work](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md) and [operational use cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. In September 2026, the group ratified a nine-task execution plan of record for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), testing session correlation and effect linkage across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and independent agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, horizontal vocabulary harmonization, and ecosystem landscape mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for standardizing definitions, clarifying conceptual boundaries, and maintaining the ecosystem landscape map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]. Reporting directly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group reconciles competing terminology across technical working groups—such as [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)—and curates core canonical taxonomy terms.

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates structured term reviews, vocabulary mappings, and catalog maintenance:
- **Backlog Triage and Admittance**: Evaluates proposed terminology across multi-stage review syncs to eliminate redundancy and maintain semantic consistency across foundational agent concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **Horizontal Coordination**: Coordinates crosswalks with technical working groups to harmonize domain-specific terms (such as interaction turns, sessions, and trajectories) with global AAIF taxonomy definitions.
- **Landscape Maintenance**: Curates machine-readable schemas and visualization pipelines mapping open-source runtimes, protocols, gateways, and agent frameworks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Lifecycle History

In June 2026, the workstream finalized its charter approvals, defined repository data schemas, and launched web portal data pipelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]. During July 2026, the group reviewed 46 terms across four syncs and admitted 13 terms in its first published taxonomy pull request, bringing reviewed terms to 67 of the 128-term backlog[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]. In August 2026, 53 terms were reviewed across three syncs with 37 retained, followed by a fourth session preparing four pull requests for a September 14 Technical Committee approval vote[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, common terminology, reference architectures, and enterprise process integration patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical initiative chartered to establish standardized execution models, operational patterns, and reference architectures for enterprise agent workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. Co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the group focuses on reconciling agent orchestration primitives with existing enterprise automation platforms and business process infrastructure [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group executes its mission through three primary work streams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:

- **Reference Architectures**: Scopes and standardizes reusable end-to-end implementation blueprints for common agentic architectures (such as [bounded autonomous remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and [single-agent human approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)) following the foundation's [reference architecture template](../guidelines/reference-architecture-template.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].
- **Taxonomy**: Develops domain-specific definitions and workflow execution terms (e.g., [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md)) in active coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to avoid conflicting or overlapping term definitions across foundation working groups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Identifies, categorizes, and prioritizes production agent use cases and integration failure modes to drive architectural priorities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-30**: In the June 2026 report to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group formalized its three active work streams, initiated alignment with global taxonomy efforts led by Gala, and raised the need for cross-working-group taxonomy enforcement to prevent semantic fragmentation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural orchestration pipeline, spreadsheet configuration schemas, run memoization, and execution guards governing AAIF community chapters and events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill packages the automation scripts, validation guards, and synchronization pipelines used to manage Agentic AI Foundation chapters, organizers, and event logistics across Google Workspace, Slack, and Luma platforms [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. The tooling automates an 18-step end-to-end synchronization workflow (`aaif-sync`) that validates directory metadata, syncs CRM workbooks, and reconciles attendee rosters [^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification

The sync pipeline executes multi-step reconciliations with built-in performance optimization and session integrity mechanisms:

- **Run Memos (`jsoncache.RunMemo`)**: To eliminate redundant external API queries across individual CLI sub-processes, report runs utilize temporary append-only cache files (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO` and `AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`) with strict 0600 file permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. The Slack memo caches resolved user account lookups, while the Google memo stores parsed Sheets and Drive responses during report-only runs [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Read memoization is bypassed during `--write` runs to prevent serving stale state across sequenced writes [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Memos are automatically purged upon run termination or crash [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Parallel CRM Processing**: Chapter workbook lookups execute across a six-worker thread pool (`sync_crm.py`), reducing serial round-trip latency against Google Drive while preserving sequential folder planning order and disambiguating colliding chapter slugs by directory ID [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **System Sleep Prevention**: On macOS platforms, the runner invokes `caffeinate -i -w <runner pid>` upon launch to prevent workstation sleep from invalidating authentication tokens during prolonged synchronization runs [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-22**: PR #52 introduced run memos and thread-pooled CRM workbooks, cutting report execution duration from ~50 minutes to ~11 minutes [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. PR #53 added automated `caffeinate` sleep guards to ensure uninterrupted completion across the 18-step pipeline [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral architectures, delegation models, and identity frameworks for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body responsible for defining vendor-neutral trust models, delegation frameworks, and identity infrastructure for autonomous AI agents. The working group develops specifications and reference architectures governing how agents prove provenance, establish authorization boundaries, and execute tasks across organizational borders.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group addresses cross-organizational delegation chains and credential exchange across multiple actors, including users, workspace devices, logical agents, and external tool invocations.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10] A primary architectural challenge is reconciling technical protocol terminology with formal statutory definitions across multiple legal regimes:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Operator Disambiguation**: Differentiating the technical runtime operator from regulated entity classifications established under EU AI Act Article 3(8), such as providers, deployers, distributors, and product manufacturers.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Relying Parties**: Distinguishing generic service consumers from qualified relying parties under amended eIDAS (Regulation 2024/1183, Article 5b) requiring declared intended use before requesting wallet credentials.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Consent and Authorizations**: Separating operational execution approval from statutory consent structures under GDPR Articles 4(11) and 7 (ISO/IEC 27560) or payment authorization requirements under PSD2 Articles 64 and 97.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Attestation Frameworks**: Distinguishing IETF RATS cryptographic evidence from eIDAS 2 electronic attestations of attributes.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Evidence Custody and Responsibility**: Mapping delegation hops to legal custody roles, including GDPR Article 28 processor relationships, Article 30 logging records, and EU AI Act log retention mandates distributed between providers (Article 19) and deployers (Article 26(6)).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

# Lifecycle History
The working group conducts ongoing periodic reporting and architectural reviews of trust standards and credential specifications.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-4] Working group technical discussions highlight the ongoing integration of regime-keyed legal role mappings into multi-agent delegation architectures.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Governance, Risk and Regulatory
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical implementation through taxonomy mapping, reference architectures, and comparative regulatory gap analysis.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group on Governance, Risk and Regulatory (WG-GRR) within the Agentic AI Foundation bridges the gap between evolving international AI regulatory standards and concrete software engineering specifications[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates regulatory controls, risk assessment obligations, and conformity requirements into actionable implementation patterns for autonomous and semi-autonomous systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Architecture / Specification

WG-GRR develops cross-jurisdictional alignment frameworks to evaluate agent systems across foundational compliance dimensions. In Phase Two of its comparative regulatory and policy gap analysis, the working group established 16 baseline themes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]:

1. **Governance & accountability**: Ownership, approvals, RACI models, and risk acceptance.
2. **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Permitted versus prohibited use cases and tiered risk-based controls.
3. **Architecture**: Reference architectures, trust boundaries, and control placement.
4. **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication/authorization frameworks, acting-on-behalf-of models, and agent registries.
5. **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Deterministic business rules, policy-as-code, and runtime constraints.
6. **Data protection & privacy**: PII handling, data minimization, retention periods, and residency controls.
7. **Security & access controls**: Principle of least privilege, secrets management, process segmentation, and tool permissions.
8. **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, operational robustness, drift tracking, and change control.
9. **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), escalation pathways, automated oversight, and out-of-band kill switches.
10. **Action management**: Pre-execution validation checks, dual control patterns, and reversibility mechanisms.
11. **Monitoring & logging**: Indelible audit trails, prompt/tool invocation logs, and decision rationale records.
12. **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection testing, tool abuse simulations, and autonomous failure mode evaluation.
13. **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence, upstream foundation model tracking, and tool provenance.
14. **Incident response**: Telemetry-driven detection, blast radius containment, and disclosure reporting.
15. **Transparency & user disclosure**: Mandatory user notices, explainability mechanisms, and user expectation framing.
16. **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Retention schedules and forensic reproducibility.

To conduct uniform extraction across regional policy instruments, the group maintains a standardized "golden source" prompt template designed to pull verifiable obligations and regional differences for each theme[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Lifecycle History

- **August 2026**: The working group finalized the 16-theme baseline matrix and agreed upon a standardized golden source prompt methodology to support geographic gap analyses for upcoming delivery to the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

- Relates to ../taxonomy/intended-purpose.md
- Relates to ../patterns/kill-switch.md

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Catalog of production agentic workflows classified by orchestration structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, coordination mechanisms, and execution bounds.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group that indexes and classifies production agent implementations across distinct operational domains[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. The inventory benchmarks workflows across standardized dimensional criteria, including trigger mechanics, human oversight loops, agent cardinality, orchestration topology, workflow patterns, and temporal execution duration[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification

The inventory records production workflows across a twelve-column classification schema:

### Upstream SDK Release Impact Analysis
- **Domain**: Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Source**: MCP Inspector `sdk-watch.yml` automation pipeline[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Trigger**: Scheduled (nightly cron execution)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **HITL Pattern**: None (results in an informational issue comment; downstream adoption decisions take place outside the workflow)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Agent Count**: Single-agent sufficient[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Coordination**: Single-agent, orchestrated (the agent explores the target repository using strictly bounded read-only search tools while surrounding lifecycle steps remain deterministic code)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Workflow Pattern**: Sequential pipeline (sweep upstream, fetch releases, analyze codebase impact, scan outputs for leaked credentials, post report)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Duration Bound**: Short (bounded by a 20-minute job timeout)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].
- **Security Isolation / Boundary Pattern**: Implements a strict `proposal-execution-split` enforced via CI/CD job-level permissions rather than runtime consensus or evaluation gates[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. The analysis agent is provisioned with a read-only repository token and limited solely to `Read`, `Grep`, and `Glob` capabilities without write or shell execution access, treating untrusted upstream release descriptions safely before handing off sanitized artifacts to a separate write-scoped job[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History

- **Draft PR #51**: Introduced the upstream SDK release impact analysis pattern to document write-separated, read-only analysis jobs without interactive gates[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Shared OpenTelemetry specification and correlation contract mapping agent turns, model calls, approval records, and state transitions into verifiable telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group that standardizes runtime tracing, causation links, and state transitions across autonomous agent interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]. Extending OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, the model defines standardized correlation envelopes for multi-agent delegation, tool invocation boundaries, human approval checkpoints, and external side effects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

# Architecture / Specification

### Relationship Verification and Test Kit
The model includes an automated verification harness (Task 4 of the trace model execution plan) to ensure traces maintain valid structural semantics under distributed failure conditions, such as message reordering, duplication, or dropped spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]:
- **Synthetic Fixtures**: Language-neutral record fixtures with deterministic reference answers to validate trace relationship resolution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Idempotency & Reconciliation Checks**: Verifies that repeated receipt events (e.g. duplicate transaction confirmations) resolve to single confirmed entities, whereas missing receipt spans correctly yield unconfirmed states rather than phantom cancellations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Testing Layers**: Separation of deterministic contract test suites from live network integration tests, utilizing synthetic inputs and opt-in payload capture to avoid PII ingestion[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

### Cross-Jurisdictional Log Requirements and Envelopes
Telemetry schemas and audit-required event envelopes within the trace model require parameterized jurisdiction and role lookups rather than static enums[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]:
- **Provider vs. Deployer Obligations**: Logging duties separate provider recording capabilities (e.g. EU AI Act Article 12) from deployer log retention obligations (e.g. Article 26(6) six-month minimums)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].
- **Audit-Required Event Schema**: Dynamic audit metadata maps the trigger event, timestamp, system identifier, actor identifier, degree of human involvement, input/output pointers, decision basis, affected-person reference, and relevant consent or opt-out status[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].
- **Privacy and Identifier Semantics**: Permissible identifiers vary across privacy regimes (such as persistent pseudonymous IDs considered personal data under GDPR Recital 30 versus standard US PII classifications), preventing rigid single-regime consent assumptions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].

# Lifecycle History

- **Issue #42**: Proposed Task 4 of the execution plan to establish a reusable OTel conformance test kit and relationship validation fixtures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Issue #54**: Highlighted the requirement to parameterize retention schedules, audit log fields, and identifier classifications by jurisdiction and role[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].

# References

- Relates to ../standards/evidence-record-spec.md
- Relates to ../taxonomy/action-record.md

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing guidance, and cross-working group security checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) establishes vendor-neutral security guidelines, threat modeling methodologies, runtime isolation patterns, and cross-working group governance review checklists for autonomous AI agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its ongoing activities across several core workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Static analysis guidelines and security failure pattern mitigations for agent tool invocation, secrets management, and execution sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Threat Modeling**: Comparative evaluation and threat modeling frameworks analyzing agent attack surfaces, uncontrolled egress, and privilege escalation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural security patterns including attested isolated runtimes, sandboxed microVM environments (such as Eclipse Enclave), and hardware-protected control planes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Review protocols tracking dependency overlaps with other AAIF initiatives, including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Coordination with the horizontal taxonomy group on defining and disambiguating core security terms, implementing automated tooling to record model provenance and human edit distances [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Lifecycle History

During August and September 2026, the working group established formalized PR review deadlines in its contributor documentation, advanced the first release of the security best practices guide, addressed cross-boundary observability coordination authored by the Observability and Traceability WG [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24], and engaged in external liaison discussions with bodies including ETSI TC SAI regarding European cybersecurity norms for AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Comprehensive catalog defining multi-category agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and traceability priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog is a living reference document authored by the AAIF [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) that documents operational, diagnostic, and compliance requirements across agent lifecycles [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Architecture / Specification

The use case catalog categorizes requirements across distinct operational dimensions:

- **A. Debugging and Root Cause Analysis**: Diagnosing unexpected actions, identifying execution loops or stuck subtasks, and reproducing non-deterministic agent runs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **B. Cost Management and Optimization**: Tracking multi-turn token costs, waste, and financial cost per completed outcome [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **C. Code Attribution and Provenance**: Tracking line-level AI source code contributions and conducting security code analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **D. Evaluation and Quality Assurance**: Measuring regression, benchmarking variants, and assessing multi-model task fitness [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **E. Safety and Compliance**: Monitoring real-world tool execution, scope boundaries, audit trails for regulated sectors (E3), and tamper-evident evidence records for dispute resolution (E4) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
- **F. Multi-Agent Systems**: Distributed trace correlation across agent-to-agent protocol boundaries and delegation workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **G. Operational Monitoring**: Production health telemetry, queue latency, and infrastructure capacity planning [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **H. Research and Improvement**: Anomaly discovery, dataset curation, and fine-tuning extraction [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **I. Identity and Ownership**: Cross-surface identity resolution across protocol boundaries and agent proxies (I1) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

### Cross-Cutting Telemetry Principles
All use cases mandate consistent telemetry properties across implementations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
- **Source and Trust**: Distinguishing agent self-reporting from hardware, OS, gateway, and sandbox sensor telemetry.
- **Privacy and Governance**: Enforcing sensitivity tagging, minimization, and redaction while prohibiting raw secret logging.
- **Completeness and Sampling**: Explicitly declaring dropped-event counts and separating audit-grade events from sampled telemetry.
- **Correlation and Causality**: Providing stable causal links across delegations and asynchronous resumes without relying solely on single parent-child span trees or wall-clock timestamps.

# Lifecycle History

Initial drafts established categories A through H in early 2026. In August 2026, use case E4 (tamper-evident evidence for dispute resolution) and category I (I1: cross-surface identity resolution) were formally merged, leading to alignment updates across the tracking matrix [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and correlation model mapping agent turns, tool invocations, approval gates, and multi-agent interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared OpenTelemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) establishing semantic conventions, causal correlation links, and interchange formats for tracking autonomous agent decisions and actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Architecture / Specification

The model standardizes telemetry across execution loops, tool invocations, approvals, and external state changes:

- **Turn and Delegation Modeling**: Formalizes parent-child and asynchronous causal relationships between primary agents, subagents, and orchestrated tool runtimes.
- **Independent Interpretation and Verification**: Requires that trace exports can be evaluated and parsed by independent consumers without reliance on producer-specific private runtime states, hidden fixture code, or shared reconstruction libraries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Order Invariant Reconstruction**: Ensures readers correctly infer approval states, observed executions, and external effects even under unordered or delayed event deliveries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Attribution and Dispute Detection**: Distinguishes self-reported claims from independent receipts, downgrading unconfirmed effects if external receipts are absent or conflicting [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History

Following working group sessions in August 2026, a nine-task execution plan was established to guide schema finalization and vendor-neutral reference implementations, highlighting Task 7 to verify semantic interpretation consistency across distinct query parsers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
