# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative dedicated to standardizing universal terminology, categorizing ecosystem components, and maintaining machine-readable taxonomies across foundational agentic concepts. The group coordinates naming conventions across domain-specific working groups and maintains data formats powering the AAIF ecosystem landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains the formal vocabulary models and validation tooling supporting AAIF deliverables:

## Data Infrastructure and Schema Validation
The canonical taxonomy catalog is structured as declarative JSON (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) backed by automated Zod schema validation in continuous integration [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79]. This pipeline eliminates custom JavaScript parsing, enforces syntactic correctness and field boundaries, and provides typed schema checking for contributor proposals [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

## Cross-Domain Taxonomy Harmonization
The group harmonizes specialized vocabularies developed across AAIF working groups, including ongoing Agentic Commerce definitions:
- **Agent-in-the-Loop Transaction**: Nomenclature updated from earlier drafts of "agent-mediated transaction" based on working group feedback to specify active participation boundaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71].
- **Agent-Completed Transaction**: Introduced to define autonomous commercial completion flows within the commerce taxonomy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70].

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned its taxonomy repository from executable JavaScript data files to schema-validated JSON with Zod parsing to improve CI reliability and contributor ergonomics [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem directory and CNCF Landscape 2 visualization mapping open-source and commercial agent frameworks, runtimes, protocols, and developer tooling across the AI landscape. It organizes projects under standardized categories to provide visibility into agentic technologies and their maturity [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is maintained via declarative configuration files and automated publishing workflows:

## Submission and Eligibility Guidelines
Entries in the landscape are curated based on community criteria and technical relevance:
- **Intake Mechanism**: New submissions are proposed through pull requests updating `landscape.yml` accompanied by vector SVG logos conforming to format guidelines [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].
- **Popularity and Maturity Thresholds**: General third-party submissions typically observe a 1,000-star threshold on public repositories to demonstrate community adoption [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].
- **Ecosystem and Downstream Projects**: Projects downstream of foundational AAIF initiatives—such as fleet orchestrators built around [Goose](../resources/goose.md)—undergo eligibility review for categories like Orchestration & Multi-Agent even when below general star thresholds [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained as a continuous catalog supporting the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). Community discussions regularly address listing thresholds and category assignments for emerging multi-agent orchestrators [^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model for Agentic Systems
proposed_concept.description: Analytical coordination framework structuring agent observability across LLM primitives, protocol boundaries, and infrastructure layers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Model for Agentic Systems is a coordination artifact developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to evaluate telemetry gaps across heterogeneous execution boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]. Rather than defining a standalone telemetry protocol or competing with existing logging frameworks, the model functions as a common boundary map to assess where interoperability breaks down across standards and implementations, guiding targeted upstream contributions and foundation recommendations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25].

Contemporary agentic systems span multiple conceptual and physical boundaries where telemetry conventions diverge. While monitoring solutions frequently capture isolated invocations, they routinely lose correlation across multi-step delegations, protocol handoffs, and underlying infrastructure environments. The model formalizes these transitions to illuminate persistent blind spots in cross-system identity, context propagation, provenance, protocol negotiation, and responsibility tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a].

# Architecture / Specification
The model structures observability analysis into three distinct horizontal layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]:

- **LLM Primitive Layer**: Governs fundamental generative building blocks, including agents, packaged skills, external tools, models, and memory architectures.
- **Protocol Boundary Layer**: Governs interaction patterns across transport specifications such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and HTTP/streaming interfaces. Primary interaction points include discovery, capability negotiation, request/response cycles, task delegation, streaming pipelines, cancellation signaling, and structured error handling.
- **Infrastructure Boundary Layer**: Governs runtime hosting environments, gateways, policy mediation proxies, container runtimes, and physical network fabrics.

### Cross-Boundary Observability Blind Spots
The framework targets five core operational areas where cross-layer visibility fails[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]:
1. **Delegation and Hand-offs**: Preserving parent-child causality when tasks are transferred between autonomous agents.
2. **Context Propagation**: Carrying execution trace baggage, state snapshots, and session context across transport boundaries.
3. **Provenance and Trust**: Establishing verifiable audit chains that authenticate which models, tools, or inputs produced specific outputs.
4. **Protocol Negotiation and Failure Modes**: Monitoring dynamic capability mismatches, version negotiations, and unhandled transport exceptions.
5. **End-to-End Responsibility Chains**: Tracing decision accountability across multi-agent and human-in-the-loop workflows.

# Lifecycle History
Authored as a foundational working document within the Observability and Traceability Working Group to guide the AAIF gap analysis work package and structure comparative landscape assessments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary of composable execution blocks and boundary contracts structuring single-agent and multi-agent reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Workflow primitives are standardized, composable operational units and execution boundaries defined by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to serve as shared building blocks across single-agent and multi-agent reference architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]. Spanning an indexed catalog from P1 through P19, these primitives decouple architectural patterns from proprietary orchestrator frameworks and establish consistent execution semantics across system boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].

By establishing explicit structural invariants across transitions, workflow primitives ensure that autonomous planning cycles, tool invocations, approval gates, and multi-agent delegations maintain verifiable state durability, resource budgets, and deterministic policy constraints[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification
The primitive vocabulary defines core workflow components, including fundamental building blocks such as `Trigger`, `AgentStep`, `Budget`, and `Handoff`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].

### Boundary Contracts
Every execution transition crossing a primitive threshold must satisfy formal boundary contracts[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]:
- **AgentStep Boundary Contract**: Defines pre-condition validation, state isolation, and telemetry propagation requirements before and after individual autonomous agent iterations.
- **Handoff Contract**: Mandates schema validation, authorization verification, and execution context preservation whenever control transfers between agents or transitions to human reviewers.

### Topology and Reference Architecture Integration
Primitives are assembled to compose both single-agent and multi-agent architectures:
- **Single-Agent Patterns**: Employs primitives P1 through P12 to implement durable waits, validation gates, and approval structures in workflows such as [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].
- **Multi-Agent Topologies**: Arranges primitives into six canonical multi-agent topological structures (T1 through T6) defining supervision hierarchies, peer handoffs, and swarm networks[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].

# Lifecycle History
Drafted in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to bridge horizontal taxonomy efforts with actionable reference architectures and topology models[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology through delegate-driven triage, SKOS-Lite schemas, and multi-working-group consensus.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is an Agentic AI Foundation initiative establishing a horizontal, shared vocabulary across all active Technical Working Groups and mapping the broader agent ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]. While global landscape intake is paused pending approved intake criteria, the workstream operates an active SKOS-Lite taxonomy definition pipeline governed by working group delegates and workstream maintainers Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].

# Architecture / Specification
## Governance and Contributor Roles
The workstream organizes participation across three operational tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]:
- **Contributors**: Any community member or working group participant eligible to file issues, propose terms, and draft definitions within the current taxonomy scope.
- **Domain Editors**: Nominated technical delegates representing the seven active Technical Working Groups who actively author, curate, and review terms within their subject-matter areas.
- **Maintainers**: Workstream chairs holding repository write access and final administrative authority to rebase and merge approved pull requests.

## Term Review Lifecycle
Taxonomy intake enforces a multi-stage review process before terminology merges into the SKOS-Lite glossary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]:
1. **Working Group Formulation**: Terms are originated and vetted within individual Technical Working Groups.
2. **Spreadsheet Staging**: A sponsoring delegate enters the term into the shared taxonomy tracking spreadsheet and alerts editors via Discord.
3. **Weekly Triage Evaluation**: The workstream evaluates candidate terms during weekly meetings against practical usage, real-world utility, and working group ownership. Terms receive one of three formal outcomes:
   - `KEEP`: Term is accepted for pull request drafting.
   - `CULL`: Term is rejected.
   - `DEBATE`: Term is deferred for broader community discussion.
4. **Pull Request Submission**: The owning delegate opens a pull request providing a one-sentence definition and extended details in a `scopeNote` field.
5. **Cross-Group Approval**: Pull requests require approvals from at least two Domain Editors representing different Technical Working Groups. Any delegate retains veto power over a proposed term.
6. **Finalization**: Maintainers merge approved terms using GitHub's rebase-and-merge strategy, transitioning the spreadsheet entry to `FINALIZED`.

# Lifecycle History
The end-to-end term curation process and cross-working-group approval thresholds were formalized in PR #83 to standardize vocabulary intake across foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural orchestration pipeline and spreadsheet reconciliation engine managing AAIF chapter event sync, access control, and country chapter folds.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill automates data reconciliation, organizer access synchronization, and multi-surface record management across Agentic AI Foundation local and national chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-57]. The pipeline coordinates chapter states across Google Sheets, Google Drive directories, Luma calendars, CRM tracking tables, and Slack communication channels[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Architecture / Specification
## Country Chapter Folding
To enable local organizers to host events across multiple cities under a unified national entity, the system implements chapter folding via `lib/aaif_events/cities.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-57]:
- **Centralized Resolution**: The `chapter_for()` helper maps municipal entries (such as Tokyo, Wellington, and Auckland) directly to their respective country chapters (`AAIF Japan` and `AAIF New Zealand`)[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- **Reader Consistency**: Every intake consumer calls `chapter_for()`, including `sync_chapters.resolve_city`, `sync_about`, `sync_crm`, `sync_access`, and the Slack audit pipeline, preventing split-state organizer allocations[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- **Precedence Over Rows**: The `COUNTRY_CHAPTER_FOLDS` map in `clean.py` explicitly overrides retired sheet rows to ensure legacy municipal rows cannot reclaim folded cities during automated synchronization passes[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

## Multi-Surface Execution Ordering
Because the resolution logic executes at runtime, chapter transitions require a mandatory multi-surface execution order before code changes are deployed[^evt-community-events-pr-57]:
1. **State Asset Renaming**: Sheet rows in the Chapters List, Google Drive folders, About documentation, CRM rows, and Luma calendars must be renamed prior to merging code folds. Merging ahead of asset renames causes synchronization engines to propose duplicate chapter rows and erase active organizer mappings[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
2. **Channel Migration**: Chapter Slack channels are renamed out-of-band with participant consent (e.g., `japan-organizers` and `new-zealand-organizers`)[^evt-community-events-pr-57].
3. **Runtime Validation**: Automated suite assertions verify that no reader regressions permit duplicate chapter generation across live datasets[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History
Country chapter folding was implemented via PR #57, transitioning municipal chapters in Tokyo and Wellington into AAIF Japan and AAIF New Zealand[^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Overview
The AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes skill (`aaif-wg-meeting-notes`) is an agent skill that converts raw meeting materials into standardized Markdown documentation for Agentic AI Foundation working groups[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]. Originally adapted from operational prompts established in the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the skill formats meeting transcripts, audio recordings, and AI summaries into clean consensus records[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification
## Packaging and Invocation Structure
The skill uses progressive disclosure to minimize context overhead across general agent sessions[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
- **Directory Structure**: Maintained within an isolated directory containing `SKILL.md` (agent instructions) and `template.md` (target output layout)[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].
- **Agent Integration**: Deployed directly into an agent skills path (such as `~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/`)[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].
- **Explicit Activation**: Configured to load only when named explicitly in a user prompt, ensuring deterministic processing without passive context consumption[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

## Output Schema
The output format standardizes meeting records across all foundation working groups[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
- **Topics Discussed**: Structured breakdown of agenda items and technical deliberations.
- **Decisions**: Explicit list of formal consensus points and technical determinations reached.
- **Deliverables**: Status tracking for specifications, whitepapers, and shared repositories.
- **Action Items**: Concrete operational tasks mapped to designated owners.
- **Artifact Hyperlinks**: References linking directly to LFX AI summaries, audio transcripts, and video recordings.

# Lifecycle History
Contributed via PR #2 in `aaif/working-group-chairs` to provide portable meeting documentation tooling across all working group chairs[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Overview
The AAIF Working Group Monthly Report skill (`aaif-wg-monthly-report`) is an agent skill that automates drafting monthly progress reports for the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]. Generalized from workflows developed in the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the skill synthesizes repository event telemetry and meeting records into structured governance deliverables[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification
## Input Signal Aggregation
The agent ingests three distinct inputs to assemble a monthly progress record[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
- **Monthly Meeting Notes**: Parses all meeting notes generated during the target calendar month.
- **Repository Telemetry**: Analyzes GitHub activity across the working group repository, tracking merged pull requests, new issues, and community contributions.
- **Preceding TC Report**: References the prior month's report to track milestone continuity, recurring initiatives, and deliverable status.

## Generation and Review Workflow
- **Target Location**: Outputs the draft directly to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` matching the structure specified by the [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].
- **Human Supervision**: Working group chairs review the generated draft, adapt domain-specific ecosystem highlights, and submit the final document as a pull request[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].
- **Execution Packaging**: Packaged as a discrete folder containing `SKILL.md` and `template.md` that loads into agent environments (such as `~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/`) only upon explicit naming[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in PR #2 of the `aaif/working-group-chairs` repository to standardize monthly reporting operations across foundation leadership[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical implementation through gap analysis, compliance mapping, and audit trail standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group bridges international artificial intelligence regulatory requirements, compliance frameworks, and concrete technical implementations for agentic systems. It conducts comprehensive policy-to-technical mapping exercises to translate high-level legal and audit mandates into verifiable engineering artifacts and operational controls.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's Phase 2 gap analysis focuses on mapping cross-jurisdictional policy instruments to core engineering themes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9]. Key areas of evaluation include:

- **Policy Mapping Clusters**: Evaluating requirements across the EU AI Act (Articles 12, 19, and 26(6)), China TC260 agent guidelines, Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, SOC 2, PCI DSS v4.0.1, and ISO/IEC 42001[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Converging Record-Shape Standards**: Shifting compliance assessment from subjective policy outcomes ("logging required") to machine-checkable artifact verification by tracking converging audit trail standards:
  - **ISO/IEC 24970**: AI system logging standard developed jointly by JTC 1/SC 42 and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
  - **prEN 18229-1**: CEN AI Trustworthiness Framework Part 1 (Logging), maintaining a normative reference relationship to ISO/IEC 24970[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
  - **IETF draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail**: JSON-based record structure specifying mandatory schema fields mapped directly to major regulatory and certification regimes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Evidence Verification Criteria**: Standardizing the operational distinction between [self-reported](../taxonomy/self-reported.md) telemetry and independently attestable [action records](../taxonomy/action-record.md), incorporating recording-independence gradients, pre-execution denial and escalation logging, external timestamp anchoring, and metadata for decision reproducibility[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

# References
- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Evidence Strength Labels](../taxonomy/evidence-strength-labels.md)

proposed_concept.title: Action Record
proposed_concept.description: Tamper-evident, content-private, and independently verifiable record proving what an agent executed, requested, or was denied during runtime execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An action record is a tamper-evident, content-private, and verifiable record detailing actions executed, proposed, or denied during an agent's lifecycle. Rather than generic runtime logs or [self-reported](../taxonomy/self-reported.md) operational telemetry, an action record provides cryptographic and architectural guarantees enabling external auditors and systems to verify execution history independently.

# Architecture / Specification
Emerging international standards, including ISO/IEC 24970, prEN 18229-1, and IETF draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail, demonstrate structural convergence on the canonical shape of agent audit records[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9]:

- **Hash-Chaining and Integrity**: Records utilize cryptographic hashing to form immutable chains resistant to retroactive modification[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Recording-Independence Gradient**: High-trust actions cannot rely solely on the acting agent as the single recorder, requiring independent observer or harness attestation[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Pre-Execution Capture**: Mandatory pre-execution logging for denied actions, policy halts, and human escalations prior to external side effects[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Temporal Anchoring**: Incorporation of deterministic local timestamps with support for external timestamp anchoring services[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Decision Reproducibility Metadata**: Structured payload schemas capturing context, model identifiers, policy constraints, and prompt inputs necessary to reconstruct decisions during audits[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

# References
- [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, activity units, and convergence budgets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture defines a controlled execution environment where an autonomous agent diagnoses and resolves operational failures within strictly bounded task parameters. It couples iterative exploration with deterministic budgets and safety checkpoints to prevent runaway execution or out-of-scope operational impact.

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture explicitly differentiates between business-level problem bounds and internal execution units to maintain operational clarity[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]:

- **Business Task**: The bounded business problem or operational incident admitted to and handled by a remediation run (such as resolving a specific deployment alert or failed node)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]. The business task sets the boundary conditions, blast radius, and target recovery objectives.
- **Activity**: The granular workflow subunit executed within the context of a business task (such as running a health check command, inspecting logs, or applying a configuration patch)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].
- **Convergence Controls**: The run operates under a [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), ensuring that repeated activity iterations terminate deterministically against strict iteration count and resource budgets.
- **Gate Separation**: Enforces transition gates such as a [deterministic acceptance gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) or [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) before promoting remediation changes to production systems.

# References
- [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)
- [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)
- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations is an automated operational skill and data reconciliation engine that processes speaker and organizer submissions across AAIF chapter event tracking sheets. It performs cross-tab integrity checks, validates contact details, and automates status synchronizations across spreadsheet views.

# Architecture / Specification
The operational pipeline manages applicant records across multiple role tabs (such as organizers, speakers, and prospects) with synchronized decision logic:

- **Multi-Role Verdict Tracking**: Submissions may simultaneously exist on multiple role tabs with distinct status assignments (such as an applicant who is denied as an organizer but remains an active prospect for a speaking role)[^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Decided-No Suppression**: The scanner skips flagging data discrepancies (such as missing LinkedIn profiles or invalid email addresses) when every role tab listing an applicant records a conclusive non-acceptance status: `Denied`, `Inactive`, or `Duplicate`[^evt-community-events-pr-58]. If even one role tab remains active or in prospect status, flagging remains active.
- **Status Column Safeguards**: If a role tab lacks required status metadata (`Status`, `Timestamp`, `Email`), suppression is bypassed to ensure issues are not silently overlooked[^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Formula Generation**: The `install_flags` utility constructs dynamic issue formulas via `issues_formula()`, leaving decided-no rows blank to avoid spurious visual alert highlights[^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# References
- [AAIF Audit Slack](../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md)
- [AAIF Create Chapter](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md)

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing baselines, and security best practices for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing threat models, defensive architectural patterns, and actionable security best practices for autonomous agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group orchestrates cross-workstream initiatives covering threat analysis, security catalogs, design patterns, and cross-boundary governance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical production across core workstreams and operational deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]:
- **Security Best Practices**: Authors the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), supported by a feature matrix mapping controls across people, process, and technology [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Identity and trust controls are coordinated directly with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].
- **Threat Modeling**: Maintains the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), baselining external threat frameworks including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across agent-specific threat vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Develops formalized architectural and operational security patterns, including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group ratified merge governance policies prohibiting authors from self-merging artifacts into the `deliverables/` directory, instituted alternate-week APAC meeting sessions, and submitted a request to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) regarding formal liaison exchange with ETSI TC SAI on agent cybersecurity requirements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]. Both the Best Practices Guide and Threat Modeling Gap Analysis merged as initial Draft deliverables on September 30, 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security controls, threat mitigations, and execution boundary standards across agent lifecycles, authored by the AAIF Security & Privacy Working Group.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide defines operational security baselines, threat mitigation strategies, and architectural guardrails for deploying autonomous agents in production environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Produced under the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the document operates as an evolving specification maintained through community pull requests and issue tracking [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide focuses on core agent security domains while deferring identity, attestation, and trust primitives to the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to ensure clean organizational boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Technical controls are paired with a Security Best Practices Feature Matrix that categorizes requirements into people, process, and technology dimensions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. These practices are designed for automated translation into static analysis rules and compliance checks against agent runtime SDKs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

# Lifecycle History
The guide's initial draft merged into `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md` on September 30, 2026, following extensive community review across roughly 88 comments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]. Complex architectural questions, including multi-cloud workload identity guidance, were split into dedicated tracking issues for future iterations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight agentic threat areas.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis evaluates contemporary industry threat modeling frameworks against the specific security risks posed by autonomous agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Developed by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg under the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document assesses coverage gaps across eight core threat domains and establishes a foundation for agent-specific risk modeling [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

# Architecture / Specification
The analysis benchmarks four established industry frameworks: OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Rather than creating an independent general taxonomy, the report recommends adopting existing classification baselines while focusing working group efforts on agent-native gaps, including recursive tool invocation, autonomous multi-turn execution, and cross-agent privilege escalation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

# Lifecycle History
The analysis merged as Draft v0.1 at `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md` on September 30, 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]. Following this milestone, dedicated threat modeling working sessions were established to drive forward gap mitigations and classification mapping [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1].

mutations.rationale: Clarify universal scope of Agent-to-agent interaction as a protocol-agnostic coordination concept rather than a protocol-specific mechanism.

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-agent
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining direct communication, task delegation, and coordination interactions between autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent-to-agent designates a general operational interaction in which one autonomous agent communicates, delegates tasks, or coordinates activities with another agent [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81]. Governed under the universal taxonomy curated by the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the term establishes a platform-neutral classification for inter-agent behavior across decentralized and centralized systems alike [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81].

# Architecture / Specification
The definition operates as an overarching, protocol-agnostic concept covering diverse exchange paradigms, including direct peer-to-peer messaging, hierarchical orchestration, and distributed blackboard architectures [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81]. The taxonomy explicitly notes that Agent-to-agent is not restricted or synonymous with any single transport specification, intentionally avoiding direct conflation with specific protocol implementations such as Google Agent2Agent (A2A) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81].

# Lifecycle History
Introduced into the cross-working-group universal terminology set via PR #81 in `ws-taxonomy-landscape`, the definition passed schema validation checks across the foundation's taxonomy test suites [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-81].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural separation of authority between proposal generation and execution in single-agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval Reference Architecture defines an enforceable structural break between an agent's proposal generation and the downstream execution of side effects, requiring verified human authorization prior to runtime enactment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. This architecture structures workflows around distinct capability roles rather than specific physical deployment topologies, ensuring that authority boundaries remain invariant whether components run across distributed microservices or inside a single orchestration harness [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

By decoupling proposal drafting from execution privileges, the pattern ensures that autonomous agents cannot directly invoke high-impact side effects without traversing an immutable approval gate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture organizes system capabilities into three logical roles:
1. **Proposal Generator**: An AI agent that inspects task context, formulates proposed actions or tool calls, and submits structured execution candidates without holding the authority or credentials to enact them directly [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
2. **Approval Gate**: An external boundary checkpoint where designated human operators review, inspect, and approve or reject proposed actions against governance policy [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
3. **Executor**: A secured execution runtime possessing point-of-effect credentials that only executes validated payloads upon presentation of a verified approval grant [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

Separation in this architecture focuses on authority and access privilege rather than process isolation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. Side effects governed by the gate include non-exhaustive operations such as production database mutations, external message publication, financial transactions, and credential issuance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. Qualification for this reference architecture requires verifying that a single agent produces the candidate proposal subject to human approval, regardless of whether internal critique or generation sub-steps are employed [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History
Developed under the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md). Refined in PR #53 following Technical Committee feedback to clarify authority boundaries versus physical deployment topology and broaden side-effect definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# References
- Proposed under [WG Workflows PR #53](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/pull/53)
- Derived from [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- Related to [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: Proposal-Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural governance pattern separating intent generation, authorization, and workflow execution into decoupled authority roles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal-Execution Split pattern isolates the generation of an intended action from its authorization and runtime execution, ensuring that an agent cannot enact side effects solely on its own authority [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. This architectural split guarantees that candidate operations must transition through an explicit governance checkpoint before accessing sensitive tools or committing side effects [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

The separation focuses fundamentally on authority and capability boundaries rather than physical process boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. As a result, the pattern can be realized both across distributed multi-tier services and within unified harness-level execution runtimes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern defines an authority barrier separating proposal generation from action execution:
- **Intent Formulation**: The model produces an unauthenticated action manifest or tool call proposal describing intended effects [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
- **Policy and Authorization Gate**: An independent evaluation plane assesses the proposal against deterministic policies, organizational rules, or human approval gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].
- **Effect Execution**: An execution engine receives validated approval evidence and executes the target operation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

At the implementation layer, this pattern can be instantiated via orchestration- and harness-level controls, such as the `canUseTool` capability gate in agent SDKs (e.g., Anthropic Claude Agent SDK), or through distributed protocol proxies and sidecars [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53]. The pattern mitigates risks including unconstrained autonomous state corruption, unauthorized financial outlays, unintended message broadcast, and credential leakage [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History
Authored within the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md). Updated in PR #53 based on Technical Committee review to clarify authority separation versus process isolation and document harness-level implementation mechanisms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-53].

# Overview
Community Event Operations provides automated operational tooling and data reconciliation workflows for AAIF community chapter events, synchronizing participant intake submissions across role-specific tracking sheets and chapter CRMs [^evt-community-events-pr-59]. The pipeline automates the ingestion, filtering, and triage of community submissions while maintaining referential integrity across Google Sheets formulas and external directory integrations [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

# Architecture / Specification
The operations framework manages intake filtering, deduplication, and downstream synchronization across several distinct components:
- **Per-Role Multi-Gate Filtering**: Processes intake responses where applicants answer individual Yes/No questions per role (organizing, speaking, hosting venues, or collaborating) rather than a single selection, permitting applicants to qualify across multiple role tabs simultaneously [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Formula Guards and Migration Integrity**: Employs formula migration tooling (`migrate_intake_role_gates.py`) to safely transition live spreadsheet formulas, injecting explicit guards that emit `MISSING FORM COLUMN: <question>` rather than silently blanking tab rows on column schema alterations [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Role Tab Orchestration**: Routes verified applications into dedicated management tabs (`Organizers`, `Hosts`, `Speakers`, and `Collaborators`), maintaining positional alignment for typed triage status and reviewer columns against append-only formula outputs [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **CRM Synchronization Engine**: Reconciles survey interest text and chapter-level tracking rows, rebuilding legacy composite interest fields for downstream CRM parity while enforcing mandatory presence of role gate questions [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained by community operations maintainers. Updated in PR #59 to replace single-choice interest intake with multi-role Yes/No questions, add the non-synced `Collaborators` role tab on Intake Ops, and implement schema guards across formula filters [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships, execution states, and verification evidence across agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines a standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships, execution states, and verification records across autonomous agent workflows. Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model normalizes cross-boundary telemetry across language model invocations, tool executions, and external service interactions.

# Architecture / Specification

The trace model couples OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) data structures with verifiable agent evidence payloads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]. The trace model test harness implements automated CI gating against standardized reference fixtures:

- **OTLP/JSON Conformance Vectors**: Six reference test cases evaluating duplicate receipts, missing receipts, ticket ID changes, and cross-tenant action ID reuse [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Receipt Signature Verification**: Cryptographic validation isolating signature integrity checks from underlying effect correlation, ensuring that synthetic signatures are not mistakenly interpreted as authenticating tenant metadata [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Basis-Context Reading**: A verification reader consuming query context from `basis.json` prior to evaluating assertions against `expected.json` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Vector Integration**: Integration with the `agent-evidence-vectors` suite for pinned accept/reject validation of signed execution records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](./evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Trace Standard](./trace.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security controls, threat mitigations, and execution boundary standards across agent life cycles and runtime operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide provides actionable security controls, threat mitigations, and execution boundary standards across the agent lifecycle. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document establishes architectural guardrails, credential containment, and runtime enforcement mechanisms.

# Architecture / Specification

Section 4 outlines authorization frameworks governing agent tool dispatch and execution boundaries. Recent working group proposals re-evaluate human-in-the-loop authorization models in light of operational fatigue studies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]:

- **Pre-Execution Interception Hooks**: Replacing or placing the four-tier human approval framework behind a deterministic pre-execution hook that intercepts all candidate tool calls prior to execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Decision Matrix (Allow, Deny, Modify, Ask)**: Enforcing programmatic deterministic rules first, delegating ambiguous boundaries to secondary model judges, and triggering human-in-the-loop approval only when the decision evaluates to an explicit "ask" [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Context and Argument Keying**: Authorizing actions based on the specific invoked tool combined with concrete arguments and execution context (e.g., distinguishing read-only from drop operations in database calls), rather than coarse static operation types [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Human Fatigue Mitigation**: Grounded in empirical data indicating human review pass-through rates exceeding 95% under prompt repetition, the framework favors automated boundary enforcement over continuous human sign-offs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Standard Alignment**: Leveraging external specifications such as the OWASP Agent Control Standard (ACS) and existing runtime platform hook catalogs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# References

- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral architectures, delegation models, attestation formats, and authority verification for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral architectures, cryptographic delegation models, attestation standards, and authority verification mechanisms for autonomous agents. The group coordinates identity standards across execution boundaries to ensure verifiability and non-repudiation in multi-agent and human-agent collaborations.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's technical deliverables focus on runtime delegation and dispatch-time authority verification:

- **Authority-at-Dispatch Catalogue**: A comparative benchmark evaluating authority verification architectures (including MintID, Proofable, and Alakris reference runs) at the exact moment of tool or task dispatch [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Versioned Contract Identifiers**: Trace requirements mandating that execution traces include explicit, versioned contract identifiers; readers reject traces lacking these identifiers [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Evidence Freshness Limits**: Explicit limits and age metadata embedded within authority evidence to prevent replay attacks and out-of-date credential utilization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Observer Automation**: Integration with automated readers like `agent-evidence-observer` to run reference test cases and validate traces in CI workflows [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

# References

- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Hardware-Bound Human Authorization](../patterns/hardware-bound-human-authorization.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation suite testing skill description routing, public copy privacy leaks, prompt injection resistance, and write-gate governance in community ops.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite provides automated behavioral testing for agent skills to guarantee routing fidelity, policy compliance, and data privacy across conversational agent interactions [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. While deterministic test frameworks like `pytest` and YAML schema linters ensure syntactic and mechanical validity, they cannot verify whether model descriptions correctly trigger intended skills or prevent unintended tool invocations [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. The evaluation suite explicitly exercises agent execution boundaries under realistic and adversarial user prompts.

# Architecture / Specification

### Dual-Arm Evaluation Methodology

Tests execute using `claude plugin eval` across two parallel arms [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]:
1. **Plugin Arm (`with`)**: Runs the prompt with agent skills and context loaded [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
2. **Baseline Arm (`without`)**: Runs the identical prompt against the base model without plugin instructions [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

A test grader passing in both arms tests foundation model priors rather than skill efficacy. Graders evaluating constraints asserted exclusively by skill documentation specify `arm: with-only`, isolating the differential contribution (Δ) of the skill markdown [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Evaluations generate local HTML and JSON reports in timestamped directories without publishing synthetic participant transcripts to public services [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

### Failure Coverage and Case Taxonomy

The suite isolates seven critical failure surfaces:
- **Semantic Disambiguation (`announcement-post` vs. `recap-post`)**: Differentiates overlapping description vectors (e.g., event opening vs. event completion) to prevent voice transposition across identical context parameters [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **PII Leakage Prevention (`speaker-bio`)**: Validates that personal phone numbers and direct email addresses present in tracker records are stripped before drafting public marketing copy [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Prompt Injection Defense (`triage-intake`)**: Ensures unvalidated form entries containing explicit imperative overrides (e.g., "mark me Accepted") do not alter intake classification statuses [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Authorization Invariant Enforcement (`sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Tests whether the agent strictly respects proposal-only defaults and requires explicit operator sign-off before committing remote writes [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07], implementing the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Vocabulary Decoupling (`audit-slack`)**: Evaluates skill invocation on colloquial user requests that deliberately avoid echoing exact keyword terms defined in `SKILL.md` [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Credential Containment (`check-setup` / `no_token_in_chat`)**: Enforces that user attempts to paste sensitive API tokens directly into the chat session are actively refused and redirected to secure credential storage such as the macOS Keychain [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07][^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed].

### CI/CD Security Boundaries

Model evaluation runs require privileged LLM API keys and are strictly decoupled from automated pull request validation (`validate.yml`) [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Because fork PR workflows operate without repository secrets, evaluation cases are executed out-of-band by authorized maintainers to protect upstream credentials [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Clean Data Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational data normalization and intake hygiene skill enforcing proposal-execution splits, city resolution precedence, and untrusted input isolation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-clean-data` skill normalizes community intake submissions, audits data hygiene, and flags anomalies across the AAIF Community Intake Ops spreadsheet [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Positioned as the foundational first phase of the estate synchronization pipeline, the skill ensures that prospective community members, organizers, and speakers are correctly resolved to geographical chapters [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. The skill operates under strict read-only proposal defaults, requiring manual human authorization prior to mutating upstream records [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Modes and Two-Phase Mutation

The underlying engine (`scripts/clean.py`) enforces an architectural [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]:
- **Scan Mode (`scan`)**: Default read-only pass detecting formatting defects (whitespace, erratic capitalization, non-canonical LinkedIn URLs) and raising judgment flags (invalid emails, duplicate submissions, unassigned locations) [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. It outputs human-readable previews or machine-readable JSON proposals without altering sheet contents [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
- **Apply Mode (`apply`)**: Commits changes only when provided an explicitly approved proposal payload (`changes.json`) [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. Updates are written using `RAW` mode rather than `USER_ENTERED` to prevent inadvertent formula injection, and every modified row receives a persistent trace log in an `Autofixes` column [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7][^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

### City Resolution Precedence and Downstream Invisibility

Unresolved geographic entries remain invisible to downstream synchronization scripts, omitting applicants from Chapter CRMs and Drive permissions [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]. City resolution follows strict precedence [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]:
1. Form dropdown `City` value (if not `Other`) [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
2. Free-text `City > Extracted` derived through heuristic parsing [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].
3. An explicit `Resolved City` manual override, which permanently supersedes automated derivations [^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112].

Selections indicating `Other` mandate manual operator review via red conditional formatting flags without automatically creating chapters or altering status columns [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

### Tooling Invariants and Security Controls

- **Tooling Constraints**: Interfacing with Google Workspace documents is strictly limited to the official `gws` CLI driven by Python [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Headless office suites like LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are strictly prohibited due to destructive font substitutions and schema stripping during round-trip conversions [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Untrusted Input Boundaries**: Raw form responses are treated as untrusted data; natural language directives embedded within user fields cannot modify system statuses, chapter assignments, or authorization grants [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **PII Containment**: Ephemeral proposal artifacts (`changes.json`) containing personally identifiable information must be written to temporary directories (`mktemp -d`) and deleted immediately after review [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Backup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Immutable snapshot and local backup skill protecting operational Google Workspace files and local data prior to destructive transformations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-backup` skill creates versioned, immutable local file snapshots of essential AAIF operational assets, including the Community Intake Ops sheet and chapter documents, before high-risk administrative operations [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Designed as an operational safety floor, it ensures complete historical rollback capabilities prior to schema migrations, column reordering, or automated bulk cleaning passes [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].

# Architecture / Specification

### Immutability and Versioning Architecture

The backup engine (`scripts/backup.py`) adheres to strict data retention invariants [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]:
- **Non-Destructive Versioning**: Every snapshot operation writes to a fresh, timestamped file path (`<dest>/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>`) within the data directory [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Existing backups are never overwritten, establishing an append-only version history [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].
- **Target Flexibility**: Supports Google Drive document IDs (exporting native Docs, Sheets, and Slides to `.docx`, `.xlsx`, and `.pptx` formats respectively) as well as direct local file paths copied verbatim [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].

### Tooling and Format Protection

- **API-Driven Export**: All Drive interactions depend on the authenticated `gws` command-line utility and native Python libraries [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].
- **Prohibition of Headless Converters**: Tools such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are strictly forbidden for document reading, conversion, or previews [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Bypassing the native Google Drive export pipeline via third-party desktop converters drops unsupported OpenXML markup and substitutes proprietary brand fonts [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning, backfill reconciliation, four-surface renaming, and design system styling sweep engine managing AAIF community assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill orchestrates the end-to-end lifecycle of local AAIF chapters, spanning Google Drive workspace generation, spreadsheet template instantiation, Luma calendar bindings, and continuous visual design conformance [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. In addition to provisioning new chapter surfaces, the skill hosts the estate-wide design system sweep engine (`restyle_design_system.py`), which audits and conforms existing presentation decks and CRM workbooks to the foundation's official typography and color standards [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# Architecture / Specification

### Design System Sweep Engine (`restyle_design_system.py`)

The styling engine audits and updates assets across Google Drive folders against the AAIF design token definitions [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]:
- **Strict Template Scope Isolation**: The sweep selectively targets files whose filenames explicitly match known templates or chapter CRMs (e.g., `<City> CRM.xlsx`) [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Active event decks, organizer drafts, and completed event archives are deliberately skipped and cataloged in the audit report to prevent accidental rebranding of localized assets [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **SpreadsheetML vs. DrawingML Parsing**: Workbook manipulation is constrained to `xl/styles.xml` and theme parts, leaving worksheet values and string tables untouched [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. The engine accounts for SpreadsheetML syntax requirements (such as 8-digit ARGB hex tokens and explicit `<patternFill>` structures), avoiding the silent styling failures encountered when applying DrawingML rules to spreadsheets [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Pre-Change Immutable Archiving**: Prior to committing changes over remote files, the engine generates pristine local backups within `backups/restyle-<UTC>/` [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Earliest copies are preserved permanently across runs to guarantee reliable rollbacks [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Visual Contrast Repair and Asset Provisioning**: Includes programmatic WCAG AA legibility analysis against newly applied background plates and dynamically distributes chapter-specific agent art without cross-contaminating template icons [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Setup Diagnostics Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only pre-flight diagnostics skill verifying Python runtime, Google Workspace authentication, credentials, and external service access for community operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-check-setup` skill provides automated, read-only environment and dependency verification for operators running the AAIF Community Events Toolkit[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]. It validates that an operator's local environment possesses required runtimes, command-line interfaces, service authentication tokens, and API credentials across Google Workspace, Slack, and Luma without modifying system state or exposing secret tokens[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill executes a deterministic verification script (`scripts/check_setup.py`) designed to return clear status indicators and remediation guidance for non-technical users[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]:
- **Runtime and Package Structure:** Asserts the presence of Python 3 and identifies whether execution occurs within an unpacked standalone skill archive or a complete repository checkout[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Google Workspace CLI (`gws`):** Evaluates `gws` command availability, active OAuth credentials, and Google Drive API scopes, preventing failures caused by default scopes omitting Drive permissions[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Spreadsheet Access:** Validates edit permissions on the AAIF Community Intake sheet by inspecting sheet metadata[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Credential Resolution Hierarchy:** Verifies access tokens via an established resolution chain: process environment variables, repository `.env` files, and the macOS system keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`)[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].
- **Headless Document Rendering:** Confirms the availability of Google Chrome to support automated HTML-to-PDF export pipelines[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].
- **Decoupled Operation:** Adheres to a fault-tolerant design where offline drafting skills (such as announcement posts or speaker biographies) remain functional even if external API connectivity checks fail[^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04][^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77].

# Lifecycle History
Introduced in the AAIF Community Events Toolkit to provide self-service setup validation and plain-English troubleshooting for non-technical community volunteers running agent assistants such as Goose and Claude Desktop[^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-announcement-post` skill guides AI agents in generating scannable, builder-focused LinkedIn announcement posts when registration opens for AAIF community events[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. It enforces concise structure, typographic style constraints, mandatory governance disclaimers, and rigorous privacy boundaries that prevent the leakage of attendee or organizer personal data[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill combines automated event data retrieval with deterministic output constraints[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]:
- **Input Resolution:** Fetches verified event logistics from chapter tracker documents in Google Drive using `fetch_tracker.py` or extracts details from explicit user prompts[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Copy Structure:** Formats output into an approximately 120-word post comprising a one-line hook, logistical details (what, when, where), speaker highlights with a single core takeaway, and an RSVP call-to-action linking registration platforms like Luma or Gradual.AI[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. Visual decoration is limited to at most one emoji and three hashtags[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Public-Copy Privacy Rule:** Strictly bars publishing private personal details, including email addresses, phone numbers, venue door access codes, and unannounced attendee names[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]. Agents are forbidden from echoing private values in conversational transcripts even to explain omissions or request confirmation[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Mandatory Legal Footers:** Enforces inclusion of standard trailing links to the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy on all public-facing attendee drafts[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9].
- **Framework Integration:** Follows the file-based packaging structure defined in [standards/agent-skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) and complements operational coordination in [skills/community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

# Lifecycle History
Merged into the `aaif-events` agent plugin to ensure community marketing conforms to AAIF brand voice, non-commercial peer sharing, and privacy standards[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9][^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-online-series` skill automates the creation and asset rebranding of new AAIF online initiatives (such as paper clubs, reading groups, and technical webinars) within Google Drive[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]. Functioning as the virtual counterpart to in-person chapter creation in [skills/aaif-create-chapter](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md), it clones the master `TemplateSeries` workspace into the dedicated `Online/` folder and rebrands file contents and directory names to match the new series identity[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].

# Architecture / Specification
The provisioning process implements strict asset management and rendering boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]:
- **Tooling Constraints:** Mandates that all Google Drive reads, writes, and transformations occur exclusively via Python scripting using the `gws` CLI[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516]. It explicitly forbids desktop office suites (e.g., LibreOffice or `soffice`) to avoid font substitution and OOXML syntax degradation[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].
- **Asset Bundle Structure:** Provisions an online-specific runbook (`Event Tracker.docx` customized for virtual join links, streaming platforms, tech checks, chat moderation, and recording workflows instead of venue/catering logistics), an `Attendee CRM.xlsx`, and presentation banner decks (`.pptx`)[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].
- **Rebranding Transformations:** Performs case-sensitive token replacement across file content and file names, substituting template placeholders (`San Francisco`, abbreviation `SF`, and Luma slug `aaif-sanfrancisco`) with the new series title and slug[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].
- **Folder Segregation:** Preserves architectural boundaries by placing virtual event programs under `Online/`, strictly separated from physical municipal communities under `Chapters/`[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516].

# Lifecycle History
Created to support AAIF virtual working groups and global online series, standardizing asset creation under the unified `aaif-events` plugin architecture[^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-8848e516][^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-create-event` is an operational agent skill for provisioning upcoming community events within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chapter and online series infrastructure [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]. It downloads the target chapter or series `Event Tracker.docx` from Google Drive via the `gws` command-line tool, clones template event milestone sections, computes phase task deadlines backward from the event date, and stages public Luma event creation subject to explicit human approval [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill combines agent orchestration with deterministic local document editing and credentialed API integration [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]:

- **Tooling Constraints**: Reads and writes to Google Drive are mediated strictly through Python calling the `gws` CLI [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]. Office Open XML manipulations (.docx) execute at the byte level on local temporary files, preserving fonts and binary structures, while desktop office converters such as LibreOffice are prohibited to prevent document corruption [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].
- **Tracker Specialization**: The skill dynamically differentiates between in-person chapter trackers (requiring `VENUE` and `LOCATION / CITY` fields) and virtual series trackers (requiring `PLATFORM` and `STREAM / JOIN LINK` fields), aborting loudly if mismatched fields are passed [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].
- **Timeline Stamping**: Pre-event milestone task due dates are automatically calculated backward from the specified event execution date, maintaining the exact operational cadence defined in the tracker template [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].
- **Human Approval Gate**: Interfacing with the Luma API requires per-calendar API keys managed securely via macOS Keychain or environment variables. Staging an event on Luma presents the rendered proposal first and only initiates the live push upon explicit confirmation from the human operator, implementing a strict [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].

# Lifecycle History
The skill operates alongside [aaif-create-chapter](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md) and [aaif-create-online-series](../skills/aaif-create-online-series.md), relying on preflight credential verification implemented in [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md) [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1].

# References
- Reference implementation: `skills/aaif-create-event/SKILL.md` [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-5e9465e1]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-dayof-slides` is an agent skill that converts event records from an AAIF chapter's tracker into structured, label-driven presentation copy for the official "Day of Event" deck (`Slides.pptx`) [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]. It populates per-event slides while strictly preserving fixed brand slides, adhering to visual identity standards, and enforcing privacy rules to prevent accidental disclosure of attendee personal data [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces several architectural and presentation invariants [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]:

- **Brand Protection and Immutability**: Fixed slides covering AAIF global network statistics and mission overviews are marked immutable and must be preserved verbatim [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].
- **Lockup and Footer Governance**: On cover and welcome slides, the `HOSTED BY` slot holds the immutable AAIF lockup [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]. Additional logo placeholders (`LOGO 1`, `LOGO 2`) are reserved exclusively for image replacement by chapter organizers rather than textual substitution [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]. Venue hosts and participating foundation members are acknowledged explicitly in prose on slide 12 [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].
- **Public-Copy Privacy Rule**: All outputs generated by the skill are treated as public materials. Private data—including email addresses, phone numbers, venue door codes, and non-public attendee names—are strictly barred from slide copy, terminal transcripts, and conversational replies [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]. Omissions must be referenced generically rather than echoing sensitive values back into the conversation context [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].
- **Drive & File Workflow**: Drive interactions are executed using `gws` and Python, utilizing byte-level OOXML edits or Google Slides API conversion and PDF export while barring desktop rendering suites such as LibreOffice to prevent typography degradation [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

# Lifecycle History
Packaged under the [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) specification within the `aaif/community-events` repository, aligning with the visual standards defined in [brand-guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01].

# References
- Reference implementation: `skills/aaif-dayof-slides/SKILL.md` [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-bb8c2b01]
