# Overview
`aaif-carousel-copy` is a specialized agent skill designed to extract event metadata from an AAIF chapter event tracker and draft concise copy for a six-slide LinkedIn carousel presentation [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]. The skill aligns community promotion with the foundation's architectural voice, structuring slides to lead with practitioner value rather than marketing hyperbole [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces specific constraints regarding structural layout, tone, and privacy [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]:

- **Six-Slide Structure**: The carousel adheres to a strict six-slide framework where slide 1 provides an engaging hook, intermediate slides detail topic substance and speakers, and slide 6 provides the call to action (CTA) [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04]. Every slide consists of a headline constrained to a maximum of seven words followed by a single short supporting line [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Editorial Voice**: Follows the foundation's "builder-to-builder" voice: focusing on concrete engineering practice over product promotion, technical specificity over grand claims, and informative signal over metric vanity [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Privacy Protections**: Applies the public-copy rule common to all community event skills: attendee PII, unpublished venue entry instructions, and contact information must never appear in copy, responses, or agent transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].
- **Rendering & Asset Pipeline**: Populates the chapter's `Event Template/LinkedIn Carousel.pptx` via `gws`, converting to Google Slides for PDF export or utilizing `aaif_events.slides_export` for high-fidelity PNG rendering [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].

# Lifecycle History
Integrates with AAIF communication standards defined in [social-media-guidelines](../guidelines/social-media-guidelines.md) and [brand-guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-02d85f04].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` is an automated, read-only verification skill that audits the AAIF community Slack workspace to evaluate channel coverage, organizer assignments, topic health, and member participation [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]. Executed as Phase 8 of the community estate synchronization pipeline, it acts as an independent reconciliation gate to ensure directory integrity without modifying workspace state [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Architecture / Specification
The audit architecture separates data collection, activity measurement, and HTML report compilation [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]:

- **Multi-Engine Audit Layer**:
  - `audit_organizers.py`: Evaluates whether all recognized chapters possess corresponding public and organizer channels, verifying that approved leaders are present [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
  - `audit_topics.py`: Analyzes subject-matter channels to identify dormant rooms, redundant overlapping topics, and discoverability for newcomers [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
  - `audit_members.py`: Assesses workspace composition and the baseline newcomer experience [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
  - `audit_activity.py`: Provides the underlying measurement layer, tracking message volume, distinct posters, and recency of human engagement across channels [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Unified Reporting**: `summarize_audits.py` synthesizes engine outputs into a single standalone HTML deliverable (`slack-full-audit.html`), indexing chapters, organizers, topics, and members alongside a prioritized focus section [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d, ^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Cache Management and Leak Prevention**: Raw Slack API responses are cached atomically with workspace fingerprinting [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]. Cache files and reports contain sensitive member profiles and emails, requiring file permissions of `0600` inside a `0700` directory [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]. Both engines enforce a preflight check refusing execution if cache or report paths could be tracked or staged by `git add -A` [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d].
- **Untrusted Input Handling**: Slack profile fields, channel descriptions, and message contents are classified strictly as untrusted data, never as control instructions [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]. Directives within user profiles requesting administrative rights or channel additions are flagged for human review rather than processed autonomously [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Lifecycle History
The skill relies on setup checks from [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md) and feeds reconciliation discrepancies into source data remediation skills such as [aaif-clean-data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md) [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# References
- Reference implementation: `skills/aaif-audit-slack/SKILL.md` [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- Cache architecture reference: `skills/aaif-audit-slack/references/caches-and-composition.md` [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Attendee Reminder Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill drafting concise, logistics-focused attendee reminder communications and RSVP updates for AAIF community events under strict PII controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Attendee Reminder skill (`aaif-attendee-reminder`) guides conversational AI agents in drafting pre-event reminder notices for registered attendees of Agentic AI Foundation community gatherings.[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e] Reminders are scheduled approximately one week before an event and the morning of the event, adhering to a concise (~70 words), logistics-first format that highlights date, time, venue entry procedures, and speaker details while prompting recipients to update RSVPs if their attendance plans change.[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e]

# Architecture / Specification

## Content and Formatting Standards

The skill enforces an objective, builder-to-builder tone centered on signal rather than promotional metrics.[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e] Drafted copy must conclude with a standardized footer referencing the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy.[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e]

## Public-Copy and Privacy Safeguards

To prevent personal identifiable information (PII) leakage across published channels, the skill enforces strict redaction invariants:[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e]
- **Field Redaction**: Contact data such as speaker email addresses, phone numbers, attendee names from intake rosters, and venue door codes are withheld from copy.
- **Descriptive Substitution**: Non-publishable logistics are described abstractly (for example, noting that entry codes are emailed privately by venue managers) rather than printed directly.
- **Transcript Hygiene**: Agents are prohibited from echoing redacted values back to operators, even to explain an omission or confirm data removal.

## Tracker Resolution and Automation

Event logistics are fetched dynamically from chapter tracker sheets using `fetch_tracker.py` from the companion status skill.[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e] Queries match exact titles or unique substrings, rejecting ambiguous queries to prevent sending misattributed event notices.[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e] All tracker data downloaded to temporary scratch disks is purged following copy generation.

proposed_concept.description: Immutable snapshot and local backup skill protecting operational Google Workspace files and local data artifacts across agent execution environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Backup skill (`aaif-backup`) provides automated, immutable point-in-time snapshotting of mission-critical Google Workspace sheets and local operational files across chapter workflows.[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7] Designed to prevent irreversible data loss during programmatic mutations, the skill preserves version histories in dedicated local storage while keeping binary artifacts excluded from version control systems.[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]

# Architecture / Specification

## Snapshot Layout and Storage Locations

Snapshots are generated as append-only, timestamped files formatted as `backups/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>` (for example, `backups/aaif-community-intake-ops/2026-07-03T142530Z.xlsx`).[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7] Storage location adapts to the runtime context:[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]
- **Local Checkouts**: Preserved in the repository's git-ignored `backups/` directory.
- **Installed Plugins**: When executed inside host clients such as Goose or Claude Desktop, snapshots are routed to `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF/backups/` on macOS, ensuring snapshots survive plugin upgrades without cluttering operator working directories.

## Execution and Ingestion

Backups are executed via CLI invocation targeting either default community sheets (such as the Community Intake Ops sheet) or arbitrary Google Drive file identifiers and local spreadsheets.[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]

## Restoration Protocol

Restoration operations are strictly manual and deliberate.[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7] Rather than overwriting whole files—which risks breaking embedded formulas and conditional formatting on role tabs—operators copy data values back from historical snapshots into live sheets.[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Packaging, runtime abstraction, credential resolution, and execution boundary guidelines ensuring agent skills run consistently across git checkouts and installed plugins.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines specify structural and runtime isolation contracts required for agent skills to operate reliably across varied execution environments, including developer git checkouts and packaged host installations.[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6] AI agent runners such as Goose and Claude Desktop install and invoke plugins under disparate filesystem topologies and stripped shell environments, necessitating strict path resolution conventions, credential fallback chains, and scratch directory boundaries.[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]

# Architecture / Specification

## Checkout vs. Installed Plugin Runtimes

Plugin architectures must account for divergence in installation semantics:[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]
- **Host Installations**: Host applications like Claude Desktop install decoupled, versioned directory snapshots lacking `.git` metadata, invoking scripts from the operator's active working directory with an empty shell profile.
- **Relative Path Resolution**: Commands defined in `SKILL.md` files must resolve paths using an explicit `<skill-root>` variable rather than static paths relative to repository roots (e.g., avoiding `skills/<name>/...`).

## Secret and Credential Resolution Chain

Because host applications cannot pass environment variables through user shells into plugin child processes, engines resolve operational secrets via a prioritized three-tier fallback hierarchy:[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]
1. Active process environment variables.
2. Root-level `.env` configuration files.
3. Native operating system secure storage (such as the macOS Keychain), ensuring installed plugins retain access without hardcoded credentials.

## Filesystem and Scratch Isolation

Plugins must never default writes to the process's current working directory (CWD), which often maps to synced personal user folders.[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6] Operational state, caches, and backups must target centralized application data directories (e.g. `aaif_events.datadir`) or isolated temporary directories created via `mktemp -d` and cleaned up after execution.[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]

## Public Repository PII Safeguards

Publicly distributed agent plugins operating on real organizational rosters must treat commits as immutable.[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6] Automated linting hooks (such as `check_no_real_pii.py`) and synthetic fixture constraints prevent live personal data from entering version control or agent transcripts.[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]

# Overview

The Taxonomy Contributions skill (`aaif-taxonomy-contributions`) provides structured protocols for AI agents preparing contributions to the AAIF Common Taxonomy and Landscape workstream.[^evt-public-agents-pr-3] The skill unifies contribution requirements across schema specifications, issue templates, and runtime data files, preventing common workflow failures such as opening pull requests for terms that require working group discussion issues.[^evt-public-agents-pr-3]

# Architecture / Specification

## Contribution Routing and Pre-Drafting Checks

Before generating pull requests or taxonomy entries, the skill guides agents through a standardized decision flow:[^evt-public-agents-pr-3]
- **In-Flight Proposal Deduplication**: Inspects open pull requests and issues to prevent duplicate or conflicting submissions.
- **Routing Validation**: Directs contributors to use the appropriate channel (Define issue template vs. Landscape PR) based on definition maturity.
- **Objective Tone Enforcement**: Enforces pre-competitive neutrality by detecting and stripping marketing superlatives prior to submission.

## Operational Performance and Efficiency

Empirical testing demonstrated that agents equipped with the skill reduced exploratory repository tool calls from 15 calls down to 6 targeted operations, successfully validating schema compliance against live landscape schema rules.[^evt-public-agents-pr-3]

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting template, pull request workflow, review timelines, and required metadata conventions for AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template standardizes the format, submission workflow, and metadata conventions used by Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups to report monthly progress to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]. Working groups utilize this uniform template to document active deliverables, cross-working-group dependencies, decisions required from the Technical Committee, and community milestones [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

# Specification
Working group monthly reports must adhere to standardized intake and submission conventions to enable automated ingestion and cataloging by the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]:

- **Pull Request Title Format**: Report pull requests must strictly follow the format `[Report] <YYYY-MM>` (for example, `[Report] 2026-09`), superseding legacy formats that included working group names [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Labeling Requirements**: Every report pull request must include the `monthly-report` GitHub label to support automated discovery and tracking across foundation repositories [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **File Naming Conventions**: Monthly report file names are case-sensitive and must conform to the directory hierarchy established by the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Governance Alignment**: Submission requirements align with Technical Committee operating procedures defined in `../guidelines/working-group-submission-guidelines.md` and `../governance/technical-committee.md` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

# Lifecycle History
The reporting workflow previously permitted variant pull request title styles such as `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`. In PR#62 of `wg-observability-and-traceability`, the instructions were aligned with Technical Committee reporting guidelines to enforce the `[Report] <YYYY-MM>` structure, mandatory `monthly-report` labeling, and case-sensitive filenames [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and ecosystem map visualizing agentic frameworks, protocols, and runtimes under strict CI parsing and security bounds.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem catalog and reference map visualizing agent runtimes, protocols, control planes, and developer tools across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. Maintained under the guidance of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape indexes member and community initiatives through a declarative metadata schema enforced by automated continuous integration validation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape catalog is configured via `landscape/landscape.yml` and verified by a dedicated CI test and validation suite (`scripts/validate-landscape.mjs`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Schema and Validation Invariants
Catalog entries require `name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, and a recognized `project` governance classification (such as `member`), with optional source repository references (`repo_url`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. URLs must strictly use HTTPS schemes and omit whitespace or credentials. Entry names undergo Unicode normalization during validation to prevent homograph duplicates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Parser Hardening and Resource Bounds
To defend CI and browser rendering against hostile or oversized inputs, the validator enforces js-yaml's `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` and depth constraints (`maxDepth`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]:
- **Filesystem Budget**: File size is verified via `statSync` before reading, capped at 512 KB[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Object Graph Limits**: The validation walk limits the parsed graph to 500 items, 5,000 objects or arrays, and 20,000 total node references[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Forbidden Syntax**: YAML merge keys, node aliases referencing objects or arrays (preventing cycles), and unprintable control or formatting characters are rejected[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Search and Presentation Runtime
The browser application (`app.js`) mirrors CI parsing settings to prevent runtime discrepancies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. The client-side search engine evaluates queries using a bounded, Unicode-aware regular expression walk (`u` flag) with shared match budgets, rendering error messages with `textContent` instead of `innerHTML` to prevent script injection[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Deployment Guardrails
A dedicated symlink guard (`scripts/check-no-symlinks.sh`) runs during pull request checks and packaging to verify that no symlinks exist in deployment sources, preventing tar-dereference publication steps from leaking runner-local files[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Landscape Categorization
Hosted foundation assets are cataloged across structured categories, such as Autonomous Agent Frameworks hosting [Goose](goose.md) as a member project alongside protocol infrastructure like [AgentGateway](agentgateway.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument evaluating real-world AI system deployments, failure visibility, and shared industry priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group Survey is a platform-neutral, 16-question evaluation instrument developed by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather firsthand empirical evidence on AI agent deployments operating in production environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]. Designed to assess operational realities rather than synthetic benchmarks, the survey measures deployment maturity, failure frequency, pre-impact failure recognition, and community priorities across diverse industry workflows [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

# Architecture / Specification
The survey specifies standardized response formats, strict data governance parameters, eligibility screening, and a single focal-system evaluation structure [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

## Response Formats and Governance
- **Response Formats:** Employs single-select, multi-select, single-response matrix (Likert scale), and conditional inline text entries [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
- **Privacy and Data Governance:** Prohibits respondent names, employer identities, and customer confidential information; responses are stored by AAIF and published exclusively in aggregate, with short text answers redacted of identifying context before quotation [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

## Questionnaire Structure
The survey organizes 16 questions across five operational dimensions centered on a single focal system evaluated over a six-month window [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]:
1. **Eligibility and Real-World Use (Q1):** Gates participation based on maturity. Respondents working with serious pilots, limited deployments, broad deployments, paused/retired systems, or unspecified real-world use proceed to the survey; respondents with only demos, prototypes, secondhand knowledge, or no experience exit early [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
2. **About the System (Q2–Q6):** Evaluates direct practitioner roles (design, quality testing, operations, and human oversight), functional work domain, architectural structure, human checking mechanisms, and organizational scale [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
3. **Benefits and Challenges (Q7–Q8):** Identifies primary operational benefits alongside principal architectural and organizational constraints [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
4. **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13):** Measures unacceptable output frequencies, root-cause accuracy factors, failure detection prior to downstream impact, severity of real-world consequences, and primary quality validation evidence [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
5. **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16):** Surfaces shared-industry technical priorities and preferred cross-organizational resource investments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Slack Audit Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only Slack workspace inspection skill providing channel health auditing, member activity tracking, and on-demand spam detection.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Slack Audit Skill provides read-only inspection tools for community administrators to audit channel health, verify permissions, and detect commercial spam across Agentic AI Foundation Slack workspaces [^evt-community-events-pr-61]. Operating on demand, the skill inspects public channels, conversation threads, and token-owner direct messages to identify vendor solicitation and account rental schemes without persisting sensitive conversation records [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces read-only access boundaries and strictly treats community message text as untrusted data [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

## Spam Detection Engine (`audit_spam.py`)
The on-demand spam audit module flags member activity using composite behavioral signals [^evt-community-events-pr-61]:
- **Detection Heuristics:** Identifies service and partnership pitches, "DM me" conversion attempts, LinkedIn account rental offers, commercial money bait, duplicate message cross-posting across three or more channels, and promotional messages posted outside dedicated promotion rooms [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Scan Boundaries:** Inspects public channels, parent-thread replies within an extended lookback window (controlled via `--thread-lookback`, default 365 days), and direct messages accessible via `search.messages`. Shared vendor rooms (`ext-*`) and organizer channels (`*-organizers`) are excluded from scoring [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Untrusted Input Sanitization:** Prints output strictly to the terminal with zero disk persistence. Message snippets are rendered within `<<msg>>` boundary markers, with internal delimiter characters in message bodies and display names systematically neutralized [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Human Verification Gate:** Outputs diagnostic leads rather than automated penalties; account deactivation remains an administrative human action executed via the console [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

## API Integration and Resilience
- **Method Allowlist:** Explicitly permits `conversations.replies` and `search.messages` within `aaif_events.slack.ALLOWED_METHODS` for read-only audit callers [^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Paging Robustness:** Avoids Slack API `conversations.history` filtering anomalies where `oldest=` arguments fail to return active messages by fetching pages chronologically and terminating manually at the window boundary, flagging incomplete or skipped channel queries [^evt-community-events-pr-61].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and transaction standards for AI commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body establishing vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and transaction standards for autonomous agent interactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9]. The working group defines foundational architectural patterns for commercial operations, including [Agentic Checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md) and [Delegated Payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The working group evaluates external and emerging commercial agent protocols and coordinates cross-boundary transaction specifications [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].

## Protocol Comparative Analyses
Through its recurring technical reviews and monthly deliverables, the working group conducts comparative deep dives into autonomous commerce specifications, focusing on onX, Merchant Payment Protocol (MPP), and Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9]. Reviews analyze each protocol through four structural criteria:
- **Problem Domain:** The specific commercial friction, cart abstraction, or payment coordination challenge addressed [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].
- **Runtime Mechanics:** Operational execution mechanisms, messaging flows, and state synchronization across agent boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].
- **Governance and Status:** Standardization stage, release lifecycles, and open governance structures [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].
- **Inter-Protocol Handoffs:** Integration demarcations where individual protocols transition responsibilities to peer transaction layers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining intake requirements, stage progression across Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus, and oversight procedures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the governance framework, stage progression criteria, and operational expectations for open-source initiatives hosted under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e]. Administered under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy standardizes onboarding, incubation, maturity evaluation, and offboarding across all foundation projects [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].

# Architecture / Specification
The policy establishes formalized maturity tiers and review criteria for hosted projects [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].

## Lifecycle Stages
Projects progress through defined stages:
- **Sandbox:** Entry-level stage for experimental, early-stage, or newly donated projects seeking community validation, contributor onboarding, and initial technical alignment under AAIF [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].
- **Growth:** Incubation stage demonstrating active multi-organizational contribution, regular release cadences, production adoption, and verified adherence to foundation governance and security standards [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].
- **Impact:** High-maturity stage representing industry reference implementations and critical open-source standards with diversified leadership and broad production deployment [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].
- **Emeritus:** Controlled archival stage for projects that have reached natural end-of-life or been superseded [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].

# Lifecycle History
The canonical policy and associated proposal process documentation were consolidated under the Technical Committee repository (`aaif/technical-committee`) to unify technical governance, intake review, and stage progression procedures [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime safety controls, and security best practices.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across agentic architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. The group develops vendor-neutral threat models, defensive design patterns, and baseline security guidelines that agent developers, system deployers, and peer working groups can adopt to secure autonomous systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6].

# Organization and Governance
The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the inaugural term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. Subsequent chair terms align with the anniversary of charter approval per Technical Committee governance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

The working group conducts two alternating meetings to support global participation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]:
- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6].
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET on alternating weeks to provide working-hours access for contributors across Asia-Pacific time zones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group directs several key technical deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]:
- **Threat Modeling**: Completed an initial comparative gap analysis evaluating traditional methodologies against autonomous agent architectures, followed by threat modeling extensions using MITRE ATLAS and OWASP ASI frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Security Best Practices**: Authored the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide, with the initial draft published and open to community contributions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Developed and merged initial architectural patterns including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) into the core patterns catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Cross-Working Group Alignment**: Collaborates with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on telemetry seams and with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on hardware and runtime attestation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Contributes security terms into the cross-WG effort coordinated by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace context, and execution verification architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry standards, distributed tracing conventions, and execution audit architectures for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21]. The group focuses on capturing causal execution chains across LLM primitives, tool invocations, and multi-agent protocols [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].

# Initiatives and Active Workstreams
The working group coordinates several specifications and industry alignments:
- **Telemetry Seams and OTel/OCSF Mapping**: Collaborating with the OpenTelemetry (OTel) GenAI SIG and the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) to define standard extension points and nine identified integration seams for coding agents, agent SDKs, and AI gateways [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) Observability**: Defining telemetry requirements and an observability specification section for the decentralized [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) standard [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Context Engines and Verifiable Replay**: Assessing cryptographic audit structures, provable execution replay, and zero-knowledge boundary protocols such as CIGAR (Context Intelligence Graph Agentic Runtime) and Agent Action Capsule (AAC) specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Cross-Boundary Security Coordination**: Partnering with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to integrate attestation evidence and policy enforcement boundaries into trace contexts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Taxonomy Definitions**: Reviewing operational telemetry classifications, such as [Operationally Conformant](../taxonomy/operationally-conformant.md) and universal reasoning terms, in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-64], [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-65].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security controls, threat mitigations, and execution boundary standards across the autonomous agent lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides actionable controls, architectural patterns, and threat mitigations across the complete lifecycle of autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]. Authored under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document establishes baseline safeguards covering prompt injection resilience, sandboxing boundaries, credential privacy, and runtime governance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c], [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline establishes concrete controls across core security dimensions:
- **Execution Boundary Sandboxing**: Segregating agent execution environments, employing structural intent separation via the [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), and enforcing hardware-bound isolation through [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Runtime Governance and Remediation**: Mandating independent out-of-band intervention mechanisms via the [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern and verifiable authorization gates via [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Credential Hygiene and Gateway Mediation**: Protecting secrets during dynamic tool invocation and preventing token leakage when agents interact with remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or personal agent gateways [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Lifecycle History
The best practices baseline was structured in workstream pull requests within the Security and Privacy Working Group before merging to the main deliverable repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]. In October 2026, the working group published the initial draft and transitioned the document to accept community pull requests under the standard deliverable review process [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology through delegate-driven triage, domain editor governance, and ecosystem mapping.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative establishing a canonical vocabulary and tracking ecosystem artifacts across open-source agent frameworks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-19b34556]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates terminology proposals directly with specialized AAIF working groups through nominated Domain Editors[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Merging Rule

The workstream manages term lifecycles and merge criteria via a structured delegate model:
- **Domain Editors**: Each working group nominates delegates who serve as Domain Editors. They submit candidate terms from their respective groups, draft formal definitions, and conduct peer reviews[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. The proposing working group retains ownership of term definitions.
- **Two-Editor Asynchronous Approval**: Definition pull requests can merge asynchronously once two Domain Editors approve the pull request and all review comments have been resolved[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Synchronous group votes are reserved exclusively for contested terms.
- **Review Filtering**: A Ready for Review milestone isolates pull requests that have advanced through the internal workstream process to ensure reviewer bandwidth is not consumed by unvetted submissions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

## Deliverables

- **Unified Agentic Taxonomy**: Formalized repository of cross-cutting and specialized definitions spanning [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md), [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and [Workflows & Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].
- **Agentic AI Landscape**: Ecosystem catalog ([Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)) tracking industry implementations, paused in September 2026 to prioritize terminology and await [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) neutrality guidelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Lifecycle History

- **June 2026**: Charter approved, base schemas established, and web portal pipelines deployed[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-19b34556].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and classification map tracking open-source and commercial frameworks, agent runtimes, orchestration engines, and tool protocols across the agentic AI domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. Stewarded under the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the deliverable aims to organize tools according to standard capability layers and open specifications[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Inclusion Governance and Workstream Pause

Contributions to the Landscape track were paused by the workstream in September 2026 pending formal charter review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]:
- **Taxonomy Prioritization**: Reviewer resources were concentrated on landing consensus taxonomy definitions across active working groups before indexing external tools[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].
- **Inclusion Criteria**: Unrestricted landscape entries raised foundation neutrality concerns; the workstream determined that explicit inclusion criteria and granularity thresholds must be submitted to the Technical Committee prior to reopening intake[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Lifecycle History

- **June 2026**: Initial landscape web portal pipeline and schema structure published.
- **September 2026**: Contribution guide updated (PR #61) to pause landscape ingestion and direct community submissions strictly to taxonomy terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

proposed_concept.title: Maskura
proposed_concept.description: Open-source policy boundary proxy intercepting agent S3 storage calls to enforce PII redaction, hybrid post-quantum encryption, and passkey approvals.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Maskura is an open-source security and policy boundary proxy operating between autonomous AI agents and S3-compatible object storage backends[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62]. Created by Amit Mor (231self) and submitted as an AAIF Sandbox proposal under the Apache-2.0 license, Maskura provides a mediation layer governing which data representation—plaintext, PII-filtered, or envelope-encrypted—crosses into agent or tool context[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].

# Architecture / Specification

## Storage Interception and Cryptographic Controls

Maskura exposes an S3-compliant interface supporting AWS CLI/SDK clients, Model Context Protocol servers, and direct agent calls with streaming and multipart upload support[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62]:
- **PII Filtering**: Automated redaction and masking applied to object representations before data is dispatched to models or agent harnesses[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].
- **Post-Quantum Hybrid Envelope Encryption**: Per-field encryption combining X25519 and ML-KEM-768 with AES-256-GCM, maintaining legacy RSA-OAEP decrypt support[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].
- **Sandboxed Transforms**: In-flight data transformation pipelines executed inside WebAssembly sandboxes powered by Wasmtime[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].
- **Signed Policy and Passkey Approvals**: Policy updates signed with Ed25519 and encoded in CBOR, paired with WebAuthn passkey approvals producing verifiable evidence bundles[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].
- **Agent Identity Scoping**: Per-key workspace boundaries restricting agent access to dedicated storage partitions[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].

## Working Group Alignment

Maskura coordinates with several AAIF working groups:
- [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Scoped credentials and policy-bound object access across storage APIs[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].
- [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md): Fail-closed policy gates, isolated transform sandboxes, and auditable evidence outputs[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].
- [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Verifiable records documenting exact policy executions and agent data visibility[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].

# Lifecycle History

- **October 2026**: Submitted to the Technical Committee as an open-source project proposal for the AAIF Sandbox stage (Issue #62)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-62].

# References

- [Maskura Repository](https://github.com/231self/maskura)
- [AAIF Project Proposal #62](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/62)

mutations.rationale: Clarify confidential computing execution boundaries to reflect that hardware memory isolation does not eliminate bearer token credential exposure.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security controls, threat mitigations, and execution boundary standards across the autonomous agent lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides defensive controls, threat mitigations, and isolation boundary rules for building and operating autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]. Authored by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document defines baseline expectations for sandboxing, credential issuance, prompt sanitization, and runtime attestation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification

## Confidential Computing and Credential Boundaries

Hardware-enforced confidential computing environments (such as Intel TDX or AMD SEV virtual machines) isolate guest workload memory from untrusted host hypervisors and administrators[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]. However, security guidelines clarify the operational limits of confidential enclaves regarding credential management:
- **Guest Memory vs. Bearer Exposure**: While hardware isolation shields guest memory from external inspection, any bearer token released to software executing inside the guest environment grants full authority to whoever possesses it[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].
- **Token Validity and Scope**: Credential exposure within an enclave is governed by the token's configured permissions, audience restrictions, and expiration lifetime rather than the underlying hardware protection[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].
- **Defense-in-Depth**: Confidential computing must be paired with short-lived, down-scoped credentials, attested delegation, and hardware-bound authorization gates rather than assuming tokens are safe merely by virtue of enclave execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

# Lifecycle History

- **Draft Revisions**: Section 2 boundary tables corrected via PR #42 to remove claims that credential exposure is inapplicable under confidential computing, aligning guidelines with standard bearer token threat models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

# References

- [AAIF Security & Privacy PR #42](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/42)

proposed_concept.title: Open Tool Specification
proposed_concept.description: Declarative, contract-first specification defining schemas, security scopes, field masking, and governance policies for capabilities consumed over the Model Context Protocol.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Open Tool Specification (OTS) is a declarative, language-agnostic, contract-first specification for defining tools, resources, and prompts consumed by AI agents over the Model Context Protocol (MCP).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63] Analogous to OpenAPI for REST endpoints, OTS defines a machine-readable document describing capability schemas, backend implementations, security boundaries, and runtime constraints.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63]

# Architecture / Specification
OTS decouples capability definition into three architectural layers: the semantic interface presented to the agent, an aggregated discovery catalog, and backend runtime execution mapping.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63]

### Core Project Components
1. **Specification (OTS 1.0.0)**: Schema definitions covering capability metadata, server configurations, component reuse, per-tool scopes, cache TTL, idempotency, agent error semantics, and field-level output masking via `x-ots-mask`.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63]
2. **OTS Gateway**: A Go-based reference proxy positioned between agents and MCP servers that returns identity-filtered catalogs, validates inputs and outputs, enforces quotas and token budgets, masks sensitive fields, and routes requests across backend servers.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63]
3. **OTS Visual Designer**: An IDE visual extension for VS Code supporting specification authoring, embedded gateway execution, and test scenario debugging.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63]

### Integration with MCP
OTS acts as a governance and contract layer on top of standard MCP wire protocols rather than replacing them.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63] Client agents such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) can connect directly to the OTS Gateway as a consolidated MCP endpoint without client-side modifications.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-63]

mutations.rationale: Reference architecture proposed in PR #56 coordinating concurrent subagent research across heterogeneous sources into an aggregated report.

proposed_concept.title: Parallel Research and Merge
proposed_concept.description: Multi-agent reference architecture coordinating concurrent, isolated subagent research across disparate sources and reconciling findings into a unified, referenced report.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Parallel Research and Merge reference architecture coordinates multiple subagents researching separate sources concurrently and synthesizing their findings into a single structured report with source citations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture addresses information retrieval across distributed or heterogeneous sources where sequential processing induces latency and shared context windows cause token bloat.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56] The workflow executes through three main phases:

1. **Query Partitioning and Dispatch**: An orchestrator decomposes a compound question into independent research subtasks, initiating concurrent execution branches via [Parallel Fan-Out and Join](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]
2. **Isolated Source Investigation**: Dedicated subagents conduct investigations within segregated environments governed by [Branch Isolation](../patterns/branch-isolation.md), gathering evidence and citing source records independently.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]
3. **Synthesis and Merge**: An aggregation agent combines findings across completed branches, reconciles discrepancies, surfaces missing data points, and compiles the final report.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

The architecture relies on [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) for handling long-polling source queries and adheres to [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) for boundary enforcement.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

mutations.rationale: Workflow orchestration pattern introduced in PR #56 dispatching concurrent subtasks and joining partial or complete results.

proposed_concept.title: Parallel Fan-Out and Join
proposed_concept.description: Workflow orchestration pattern dispatching independent subtasks across concurrent agent workers and joining partial or complete results under explicit failure tolerances.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Parallel Fan-Out and Join is an orchestration pattern that distributes decoupled tasks across concurrent worker agents and joins their outputs into a reconciled result set while gracefully managing partial failures and missing outputs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

# Architecture / Specification
In agent workflows requiring multi-source discovery, sequential polling creates latency bottlenecks and fragile dependency chains. Under Parallel Fan-Out and Join:

- **Fan-Out**: An orchestrator dispatches independent execution branches across separate subagents or tool executions concurrently.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]
- **Resilient Join**: The join step aggregates returned results based on dynamic completion criteria. If individual worker branches encounter timeouts, authentication errors, or missing sources, the join aggregator records the gap as omitted evidence rather than failing the entire pipeline.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]
- **Downstream Aggregation**: The partial or complete output set is presented to downstream merging layers, such as in the [Parallel Research and Merge](../architectures/parallel-research-and-merge.md) architecture.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

mutations.rationale: Context and execution boundary pattern introduced in PR #56 maintaining strict separation across concurrent agent research tasks.

proposed_concept.title: Branch Isolation
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern enforcing strict execution context and memory boundaries between concurrent subagent tasks to prevent context pollution and cross-branch interference.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Branch Isolation is an architectural pattern that maintains distinct execution environments and context boundaries for concurrent subagent tasks to prevent token bloat, context contamination, and unintended state sharing.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

# Architecture / Specification
When executing multi-agent workflows such as [Parallel Research and Merge](../architectures/parallel-research-and-merge.md), running parallel workers in an unsegmented environment causes intermediate tool outputs and hallucinated assertions to pollute sibling reasoning chains.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

Branch Isolation establishes:
- **Context Segmentation**: Each worker agent operates with its own scoped system prompt, ephemeral context window, and dedicated tool instances.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]
- **Execution Containment**: Transient errors, large payload fetches, and exploratory traces remain encapsulated within the individual branch.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]
- **Clean Return Boundaries**: Sibling branches communicate exclusively through structured artifacts returned to the parent join node via [Parallel Fan-Out and Join](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md), maintaining complete branch separation during execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-56]

proposed_concept.title: Attestation & Evidence Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF working group defining standards, witness taxonomies, and portable bundle formats for independently verifiable AI agent actions and decisions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attestation & Evidence Working Group (AE-WG) is a proposed cross-cutting technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation tasked with standardizing how statements about AI agent actions, decisions, authorizations, and outcomes are attested and preserved as independently verifiable evidence.[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on creating evidence formats that survive across organizational boundaries and allow third parties to independently verify historical agent operations without relying on centralized authorities.[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]

### Primary Workstreams
- **Bilateral and Multi-Party Attestation**: Protocols ensuring each participant in an interaction cryptographically seals its own observation, deriving consensus or dispute deterministically.[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]
- **Portable Evidence Bundles**: Self-describing, offline-verifiable data structures declaring their completeness and disclosure boundaries.[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]
- **Witness and Root-of-Trust Taxonomy**: Structural classification mapping verification mechanisms—such as transparency logs, timestamp authorities, Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)—to the guarantees they provide.[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]

### Cross-Group Collaboration
The AE-WG operates liaisons with sibling AAIF bodies:
- Sourcing entity identifiers from the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]
- Consuming runtime telemetry models from the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]
- Mapping evidence classes to compliance mandates defined by the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]
